### .jsc reference

URL: https://joust.julc.dev/languages/jsc-reference/

This page defines `.jsc`, as the front end in `julc-state-dsl` implements it
([`v2/Lexer.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-dsl/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/dsl/v2/Lexer.java),
[`v2/Parser.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-dsl/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/dsl/v2/Parser.java),
[`v2/Checker.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-dsl/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/dsl/v2/Checker.java),
[`v2/JavaEmitter.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-dsl/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/dsl/v2/JavaEmitter.java))
and [ADR-0018](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/docs/adr/0018-jsc-2-immutable-contract-language.md) states
it. For a guided introduction, read the [.jsc guide](https://joust.julc.dev/languages/jsc/); for the functions, the
[standard library](https://joust.julc.dev/languages/jsc-std/).

> **A preview:** 
`.jsc` is a preview: the core language of milestone M1, M2a's values and native assets (`Value`, `Address`,
`Credential`, `funds`, `send`, `mint`, `burn`, `accept`), and M2b's params, invariants, events, `quorum` and
`authorized`, M2c's composition (other contracts' instances and states, deposits made and received, send datums,
stored values), `.jsc` and Java libraries (M4, below), and M3's owned and keyed objects, script purposes and
migration.

##### Lexical rules

| Element | Rule |
|---|---|
| Header | Optional: when the first word of the file, after whitespace and comments, is `jsc`, it is followed by `1`. A file without a header is version 1. Any other version is refused (`JSC0113`), `jsc 2` included: it was the header of the previews, and there is no alias |
| Line ends | LF or CRLF only. A lone CR, NEL, U+2028, U+2029, VT and FF are refused (`JSC0147`): some editors break lines there and a `//` comment could hide the code after them |
| Format characters | No Unicode format character (category Cf: the bidirectional controls, zero-width characters) anywhere in the file, comments and strings included (`JSC0145`); a leading byte-order mark is allowed |
| Comments | `//` to the end of the line, and `/* … */` |
| Identifiers | `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`: ASCII only (`JSC0146`), so no two names can look alike. Case-sensitive |
| Integers | Decimal digits, `_` between groups (`1_000_000`). No sign: `-5` is unary minus. `5 ada` is 5,000,000 |
| Bytes | `#` then an even number of hex digits (`#cafe`, `JSC0102`); upper case is lower-cased |
| Strings | `"…"` on one line, with the escapes `\"`, `\\` and `\n`; no control characters (`JSC0104`). Only `require` messages and `utf8("…")` arguments |
| Separators and newlines | Newlines do not end statements: a statement ends where its expression cannot continue, or at `;` (optional). Two tokens look at the line: a `[` or a `(` continues an index or a call only on the line of what it follows, so `m[k]` and `f(x)` start on one line, and on a later line `[` or `(` starts a new expression. A line that starts with a binary `-` continues the expression above it (a subtraction) and warns `JSC9007`: join the lines, parenthesise, or end the line above with `;` |

##### Grammar at a glance

```text
file      = [ "jsc" "1" ] "package" seg { "." seg } { import | type | enum | fn } contract { import | type | enum | fn }
library   = [ "jsc" "1" ] "library" seg { "." seg } { import | type | enum | fn }     ("jsc 2" is reserved and refused)
import    = "import" "{" Ident { "," Ident } "}" "from" String     (String: "std/…", a relative "./x.jsc", or "java:<class>")
          | "import" "contract" "{" Name "}" "from" String          (M2c: another contract, "./Name.jsc"; not in a library)
type      = "type" Name "=" "{" { field [","] } "}"
enum      = "enum" Name "{" { Name [ "{" { field [","] } "}" ] [","] } "}"
field     = Ident ":" typeRef
typeRef   = Ident [ "." Name ] [ "<" typeRef { "," typeRef } ">" ]      (Oracle.State, Instance<Oracle>)
fn        = "fn" Ident params ":" typeRef ( "=" expr | block )
contract  = "contract" Name [ "(" option { "," option } ")" ] "{" { member } "}"
option    = ( "minAda" | "maxDatumBytes" | "maxValidityMs" | "assetSlots" ) "=" Int [ "ada" ]
          | "stakeSelf"                                                             (M3c: a flag, no value)
member    = "state" "{" { field [","] } "}"          (exactly once)
          | "params" "{" { field [","] } "}"          (at most once)
          | "event" Name [ "{" { field [","] } "}" ]
          | "invariant" [ Name "." ] Ident ( "=" expr | block )                    (T.name: M3a3)
          | "init" params [ "payable" ] block
          | ( "action" | "destroy" ) Ident params { modifier } block
          | "view" Ident params ":" typeRef ( "=" expr | block )
          | "owned" Name "{" { field [","] } "}"                                    (M3a)
          | "owned" Name "keyed" "by" Ident [ "(" keyOpt { "," keyOpt } ")" ] "{" { field [","] } "}"   (M3b)
          | "owned" ( "init" | "action" | "destroy" ) Name "." Ident params { modifier } block
          | "withdraw" Ident params { modifier } block                              (M3c: the handlers)
          | ( "certify" | "vote" ) Ident params { modifier } ( "=" expr | block )
          | "propose" Ident params ( "=" expr | block )
          | "init" "migrate" "from" "params" "." Ident params block                  (M3c: the adoption)
          | fn | type | enum
keyOpt    = "signed" | ( "maxKeyBytes" | "linkCooldownMs" | "linkWindowMs" ) "=" Int
params    = "(" [ param { "," param } ] ")";   param = Ident ":" ( typeRef | "reads" "params" "." Ident | "shared" | "into" )
modifier  = "payable" | "open" | "batched" [ "only" ] | ( "only" | "after" | "before" ) Ident
          | "quorum" fieldRef fieldRef | "authorized" fieldRef | "receives" [ typeRef ] | "admits" Name   (admits: M3a3)
          | "retire" | "migrates" "to" Ident                                          (retire: M3b; migrates to: M3c)
fieldRef  = Ident | "params" "." Ident
block     = "{" { stmt } [ [ "return" ] expr ] "}"
stmt      = "const" Ident [ ":" typeRef ] "=" expr
          | "require" "(" expr "," String ")"
          | "pay" "(" expr "," expr ")"
          | ( "send" | "mint" | "burn" ) "(" expr "," expr ")" | "accept" "(" expr ")" | "emit" "(" expr ")"
          | "send" "(" expr "," expr "," expr ")" | "deposit" "(" expr "," expr "," expr ")"
          | "if" expr block [ "else" ( if | block ) ]
          | "match" expr "{" { pattern "=>" ( block | require | pay | expr ) [","] } "}"
          | "for" "(" "const" Ident "of" expr ")" block
pattern   = "_" | "None" | "Some" "(" Ident ")" | Name [ "{" Ident [ ":" Ident ] { "," … } "}" ]
expr      = see the operator table; primaries: Int [ "ada" ], Hex, "true", "false", Ident, Ident "(" args ")",
            "(" expr ")", "[" [ expr { "," expr } ] [ "," "..." expr ] "]", "{" [ "..." expr "," ] inits "}",
            Name "{" inits "}", if-expression, match-expression
args      = argument { "," argument };   argument = expr | Ident "=>" body | "(" [ Ident { "," Ident } ] ")" "=>" body
```

A file holds one contract (`JSC0114`), a contract one `state` block (`JSC0121`) and exactly one `init` (`JSC0401`).
Members may come in any order. A block's last expression is its value; a statement after it is `JSC0127`.

##### Contract options

| Option | Java element | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minAda` | `long minAda()` | derived from `maxDatumBytes` | Lovelace locked as the state UTxO's min-ADA deposit; below the derived value is a compile error |
| `maxDatumBytes` | `int maxDatumBytes()` | `512` | Largest serialised state the validator accepts |
| `maxValidityMs` | `long maxValidityMs()` | `3600000` | Widest validity interval a call that reads the transaction may use |
| `assetSlots` | `int assetSlots()` | `4` when a method moves native assets, else `0` | Native assets the state UTxO's deposit is sized for (ADR-0007 D2); 0 to 64 |
| `stakeSelf` | `boolean stakeSelf() = true` | off | M3c (ADR-0010 D2): a flag, written without a value (`JSC1301`). The state's address is staked to the contract's own script, so its funds earn rewards; needs a `withdraw` and a `certify` handler (`JSC1302`) |

Values are non-negative integer literals (`ada` allowed); anything else is `JSC0402` or `JSC0403`.

##### Types and their encodings

The encoding is fixed and is what the [ABI manifest](#the-abi-manifest) states. It is JuLC's encoding of the generated
Java, so a `.jsc` contract and a Java contract with the same state agree on chain.

| `.jsc` | Java | On-chain data (manifest `data`) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Int` | `BigInteger` | integer (`int`) | unbounded on both sides |
| `Bool` | `boolean` | `Constr 0 []` false, `Constr 1 []` true (`bool`) | |
| `Bytes` | `byte[]` | bytes (`bytes`) | `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` compare bytes |
| `Key` | `byte[]` | bytes, 28 of them (`bytes28`) | a `Key` is a `Bytes`; the reverse only through `asKey` |
| `Hash` | `byte[]` | bytes, 28 of them | a script hash or policy id; `asHash` |
| `List<T>` | `JulcList<T>` | list (`list<…>`) | |
| `Option<T>` | `Optional<T>` | `Constr 0 [x]` / `Constr 1 []` (`option<…>`) | `Option<Option<T>>` is refused (`JSC0305`) |
| `Map<K, V>` | `JulcMap<K, V>` | map with unique keys in canonical order (`map<…>`) | `K` is `Bytes`, `Key` or `Hash`, at most 64 bytes (`JSC0308`) |
| `BigMap<K, Int>`, `BigMap<K, Bytes>` | `MerkleMap` | the `MerkleMap` record: its root, and the reads and writes of the call (`merkleMap<…>`) | a state field only (`JSC0803`) |
| `type R = { f: T, … }` | a generated record | `Constr 0` with the fields in declaration order | no generic records |
| `enum E { A, B { x: Int } }` | a generated sealed interface and one record per variant | `Constr i`, `i` the variant's declaration index, then its fields | |
| `Credential` | the ledger's `Credential` | `Constr 0 [key hash]` (`KeyCred`) / `Constr 1 [script hash]` (`ScriptCred`) | built with `keyCred(k)`, `scriptCred(h)`; read with `match c { KeyCred { key } => …, ScriptCred { hash } => … }` |
| `Address` | the ledger's `Address` | `Constr 0 [credential, staking option]` | built with `wallet(k)`, `wallet(k, stakeKey)`, `script(h)`, `script(h, stakeKey)`; `a.payment` is its credential |
| `Value` | the ledger's `Value` | a map of maps, each policy's token names in canonical order (shorter first: its *wire form*) | a local's, a `fn`'s, `funds`' and the effects'; M2c: a field of the state, the params, a record or a variant, never in a `List`, `Option` or `Map` (wrap it in a record) nor a method parameter (`JSC0341`) |
| `Instance<C>` | the API's `ForeignInstance` | `Constr 0 [policy, instance id]` (`ForeignInstance`) | M2c: another contract's instance, `C` imported (`import contract`); a `params` field only (`JSC0445`), used whole as a deposit's target and by `reads` |
| `C.State`, `C.T` | the imported contract's own records (`Oracle.State`) | as that contract encodes them | M2c: read, not stored: a `const`'s, a `fn`'s or a lambda's type, never a field, a method parameter, a memo or a datum (`JSC0446`); not matched (`JSC0446`) |

There are no strings at run time, no implicit conversions, no `null` and no generic user types. Type, enum and variant
names start with a capital (`JSC0205`), have no `_` (`JSC0206`), share one namespace (`JSC0910`), and may not be a
name the processor generates (`Lifecycle`, `Calls`, `Step`, `Funds`, … : `JSC0220`).

###### Checked inputs

Every `init` argument and every action and destroy parameter (the redeemer) is checked by generated code before the
method's body runs, recursively through records, enums, lists and options: every `Key` and `Hash` is 28 bytes, and
every `Map` has unique keys of at most 64 bytes in strictly ascending canonical order; every `Credential` holds a 28-byte
hash, and every `Address` the ledger's encoding with a well-formed payment credential and, if it has one, a staking hash (an address with a staking pointer is refused). A checked address may still be your contract's own script, and `send` to it always fails (`#send:`). If you store an address you will send to later (a refund list, a beneficiary), refuse it when you take it: `require(paymentScript(a) == None || asHash(paymentScript(a) ?? #00) != funds.policy, "not this contract")`. A failure is a located `require` failure. View parameters are not checked: a view runs off chain on your own inputs.

##### Names and scope

- A name is bound once and never redeclared or shadowed (`JSC0212`).
- In an action, destroy or view, no parameter, `const`, lambda parameter, loop variable or `match` binding may take a
  state field's name or a built-in's (`caller`, `received`, `balance`, `validFrom`, `validTo`, `state`, `params`,
  `funds`): `JSC0213`. In an `init`, which has no input state, parameters may share the names of the fields it
  creates.
- No binding and no state field takes the name of a declared type, enum, variant or `fn` (`JSC0222`): `const Open:
  Phase = phase` would make `phase == Open` always true.
- Names cannot contain `__` (`JSC0210`) or be Java keywords and literals, members of `Object`, or names the generated
  code uses (`ctx`, `State`, `Outcome`, `deploy`, `instance`, `seed`, `ByteStringLib`, `Int`, `List`, `Option`, …:
  `JSC0211`). The full list is `RESERVED` in `Checker.java`.
- The generated client binds `s` and `r` in actions and destroys, `s` in views, and `seed` and `result` in an
  `init`; a parameter may not take them (`JSC0216`).

##### Members

| Member | Generated Java | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `state { … }` | `public record State(...)`, components in order | at least one field (`JSC0303`) |
| `init(params) [payable] { … }` | `@Init public static State init(params[, Ctx ctx])` | returns the first state (`JSC0410`); only `payable` (`JSC0405`); cannot pay (`JSC0404`) |
| `action name(params) mods { … }` | `@Action public static State name(State s__, params[, Ctx ctx])`, or a record of the state and its payouts when it pays | returns the next state (`JSC0410`) |
| `destroy name(params) mods { … }` | `@Destroy public static JulcList<Payout> name(State s__, params, Ctx ctx)` | no result (`JSC0411`); must pay at least once (`JSC0409`); cannot be `payable` (`JSC0406`) |
| `view name(params): T = expr` | `@View public static T name(State s__, params)` | no transaction built-ins (`JSC0415`), no `pay` |
| `fn name(params): T = expr` | a `static` method of the contract class | pure: no state, no built-ins, no `pay` |
| `params { … }` | `@Params public record Config(...)` | once (`JSC0431`), at least one field (`JSC0432`); read as `params.f` in methods, views and invariants, never in a `fn` (`JSC0433`) |
| `event Name { … }` | a variant of `public sealed interface Event` | the contract's events; emitted with `emit(Name { … })` |
| `invariant name = expr` | `@Invariant public static boolean name(State s__[, Config params__])` | a `Bool` over the state and the params, like a view's body, without `require` (`JSC0441`); not with `BigMap` state (`JSC0435`) or `batched` actions (`JSC0436`) |
| `owned T { … }` | `@Owned public record T(...)` | M3a (ADR-0003): an owned object's record; each object is its own UTxO. Its fields follow the state's rules (no built-in name, `JSC0208`; a `BigMap` at the top, M3a2). It needs an owned init (`JSC1208`) and an escape hatch, an owned destroy without `shared`, `before` or `after` (`JSC1209`; warned, `JSC9016`, when every hatch needs the deployment's parties: `authorized params.f` or a quorum over params); a contract with owned types destroys no instance (`JSC1210`) and keeps no `BigMap` state (`JSC1211`); an owned type is no field or parameter of another value (`JSC1207`) |
| `owned init T.m(params) [payable] { … }` | `@OwnedInit public static T m([@Shared State s, ]params[, Ctx ctx])` | returns the new object; only `payable` (`JSC0405`); cannot pay, send, mint or deposit (`JSC0404`) |
| `owned action T.m(params) mods { … }` | `@OwnedAction public static T m(T s__[, @Shared State s], params[, Ctx ctx])`, or `TOutcome` when it has effects | its input is the object: bare names and `state` read it, and so do `only`, `after`, `before`, `quorum`; returns the next object |
| `owned destroy T.m(params) mods { … }` | `@OwnedDestroy public static JulcList<Payout> m(T s__, …, Ctx ctx)` (or `Settled`) | pays out what the object holds (`JSC0409`) |
| `owned T keyed by f (opts) { … }` | `@Owned(key = "f", maxKeyBytes = n, …) public record T(...)` | M3b (ADR-0016): a keyed type, one object per key per instance, in a sorted on-chain list. `f` is a `Bytes`, `Key` or `Hash` field (`JSC1241`); the options are `signed`, `maxKeyBytes = 1…64` (default 32; at least 28 with `signed`, `JSC1242`), `linkCooldownMs = 0 or 60000…3600000` (default 60,000) and `linkWindowMs = 20000…min(900000, maxValidityMs)` (default min(120,000, maxValidityMs), `JSC1243`) |
| `owned destroy T.m() only f retire { … }` | `@OwnedDestroy(retire = true)` | M3b: a keyed type's retiring exit, its escape hatch (`JSC1245`): the node stays retired, its key taken for good; signed by `only f` and needing nobody else |
| `withdraw m(amount: Int, args…) aud { … }` | `@Withdraw public static JulcList<Send> m(Config params__, BigInteger amount, args…[, Ctx ctx])` | M3c (ADR-0010): the contract's rewards withdrawn; its only effect is `send`, and its sends allocate the amount exactly in lovelace. `aud` is `quorum` or `authorized` over `params.*` (`JSC1312`, `JSC1313`); no state (`JSC1318`), no `received` or `balance` (`JSC1315`); its redeemer is `Rewards(74, amount, args…)` |
| `certify m(cert: TxCert) aud = expr` | `@Certify public static boolean m(Config params__, TxCert cert)` | M3c: decides a certificate the processor's filter admits (a script credential's registration, delegation, DRep registration or update); a Bool, no effects (`JSC1319`, `JSC1341`) |
| `vote m(voter: Voter, action: GovernanceActionId, vote: Vote) aud = expr` | `@Votes public static boolean m(Config params__, Voter voter, GovernanceActionId action, Vote vote)` | M3c: runs once per vote the voter (a script DRep or committee member) casts in the transaction; all must be allowed |
| `propose m(p: ProposalProcedure) = expr` | `@Propose public static boolean m(Config params__, ProposalProcedure p)` | M3c: a guardrail on a proposal; no modifiers (`JSC1313`) |
| `init migrate from params.p(old: V.State, args…) { … }` | `@Migrate(from = "params.p") public static State migrate(Config params__, V.State old, args…[, Ctx ctx])` | M3c (ADR-0011 D4): adopts an instance of the previous version `V` (an imported contract), whose policy `params.p` pins (a `Hash` or `Bytes`, `JSC1335`). No modifiers (`JSC1339`), nothing received and no effects (`JSC1338`): the new instance holds exactly the old one's lovelace. `old` is a checked input. One per contract; not beside owned objects, BigMap state or native assets (`JSC1334`) |
| `import contract { C } from "./C.jsc"` | `import <C's package>.C;` | M2c (ADR-0018 D9): another `.jsc` contract of the build, checked on its own; its state is `C.State` and its instances `Instance<C>`. One name, the file's contract (`JSC0740`, `JSC0742`); no cycle (`JSC0743`); not twice, nor its name for another declaration (`JSC0744`); `java:` contracts not yet (`JSC0741`). Not yet: a contract whose state, declared types, events or memos use a `.jsc` or `java:` library's type cannot be imported (`JSC0746`); a library type in its methods' parameters and results is fine. |

Method names are unique, and a `fn` may not share one (`JSC0202`); nor may an invariant (`JSC0224`). A method gets
`Ctx ctx` when it is a destroy, has a modifier other than `open`, `only`, `quorum` and `authorized`, or mentions
`caller`, `received`, `balance`, `validFrom`, `validTo`, `after` or `before`.

**Params** (ADR-0009 D1) are fixed when the contract is deployed: the script is applied to them, so each set of params is
its own script (pin `policyIdFor(params)`), and they are in no redeemer. An `init` takes them (first) whenever the
contract declares them; any other method or view takes them (directly after the state) when it reads them. `Config` is
then a reserved type name, as `Event` is in a contract with events (`JSC0225`). A batched action does not read them yet
(`JSC0437`). M2c: the init checks them as a checked input (`#params:`: every `Key` and `Hash` 28 bytes, maps canonical,
addresses the ledger's, every `Value` of lovelace's or 28-byte policies), so no instance is made under params whose
values a reader would refuse.

**Owned objects** (ADR-0003, M3a). An owned method names its type, `owned action Account.deposit()`. A parameter
`bank: shared` is the instance's state, read through a reference input (never spent, so owners do not queue behind each
other), and comes first (`JSC1205`, `JSC1206`); read its fields as `bank.paused`. In an owned action or destroy,
`received` is what the call pays into the object and `balance` what the object holds. A method with a `shared` parameter
takes `Ctx`, as the Java examples' owned methods do. An owned action or destroy without an audience warns (`JSC9010`:
anyone could call it on anyone's object); say `open` when that is meant. A contract may declare several owned types
(M3a2): each type's objects have their own datum constructor (`Holding_T`), so a method only ever runs on its own type's
objects, and each type needs its own owned init and escape hatch (`JSC1208`, `JSC1209`, at the type). An owned type may
keep `BigMap`s (the instance then keeps none, `JSC1211`), and an owned init may write them and `accept` native assets;
an owned destroy may be `payable`. An instance's `init` does not accept native assets (`JSC0426`). An owned action
with a parameter `to: into` moves its object to another instance, which consents with an action `admits T` in the same
transaction (first parameter the object's id, then optionally the arriving object, `obj: T`). Each half reads the
other's input, never its outcome; each half is its own call, with its own refusal class; the transaction is accepted
only if both halves are, and `Compose` reports the first refusal in the order its calls were added. An admission's
conditions hold for the object as it arrives (its input), not for the object that lands: if the move changes what the
admission reads, check it on the move's side too. A destination admits one object per transaction (it has one
redeemer), and an object that keeps a `BigMap` cannot move yet (`JSC1212`). `invariant T.name = …` holds for every
object of type `T`.

```text
contract Bank(maxDatumBytes = 160) {
  state { admin: Key, paused: Bool, withdrawLimit: Int }
  owned Account { owner: Key, saved: Int }
  init(withdrawLimit: Int) { return { admin: caller, paused: false, withdrawLimit } }
  owned init Account.open(bank: shared) payable {
    require(!bank.paused, "the bank is paused")
    return { owner: caller, saved: received }
  }
  owned action Account.withdraw(bank: shared, amount: Int) only owner {
    require(amount > 0 && amount <= bank.withdrawLimit && amount <= saved, "not that much")
    pay(owner, amount)
    return { ...state, saved: saved - amount }
  }
  owned destroy Account.close() only owner { pay(owner, balance) }
}
```

**Keyed objects** (ADR-0016, M3b). `owned Entry keyed by name (maxKeyBytes = 64) { name: Bytes, owner: Key, … }`
makes `Entry` unique by `name` within an instance: each key is its own UTxO, a node of a sorted list whose head the
instance's creation makes. An owned init inserts after the node whose gap the key falls into (the runtime finds it);
the key cannot be one already taken, live or retired. A keyed type's methods are an owned type's, with its rules:

- **The key is fixed** for the object's life (`JSC1248`): an action returns `{ ...state, … }` without it, or with it
  unchanged. To change a key, retire or remove the object and insert another.
- **`signed`**: the key is a 28-byte key hash that signs the insert, so nobody can take someone else's key. Without it,
  an initializer that does not take the key from `caller` warns (`JSC9011`: anyone may take a free key first).
- **Exits.** `retire` keeps the node, retired, with its key for good: the owner leaves with all but the deposit, and needs
  no neighbour, so this is the escape hatch every keyed type has (`JSC1245`). An owned destroy without `retire` removes
  the node and frees its key; it needs its predecessor, which anyone can delay, so it is never the escape hatch.
- **Audiences.** Every keyed action says who may call it with `only`, `quorum` or `authorized`; `open` is not enough
  (`JSC1246`), and an action authorized by someone other than the retire's signer warns (`JSC9013`).
- **Time.** An insert or a removal relinks a node: its window is at most `linkWindowMs` long and starts at least
  `linkCooldownMs` after that node's last relink (the runtime waits for it). `linkCooldownMs = 0` warns (`JSC9012`). A
  key is never set from a time value (`JSC1251`).
- **Limits** (the processor's, `JSC1244`): no native assets, batched actions or `BigMap`s in a contract with keyed types;
  at most 16 keyed types; `maxDatumBytes` at most 2048, and a retired node's worst case must fit it (`JSC1250`). Keyed
  objects do not move (`JSC1247`). The validator's generated names are reserved (`JSC1249`: `Link`, `Insert_m`,
  `Remove_T`, `Head_T`, `Keyed_T`, `Retired_T`; the client's `tList`, `tExists`, `tKeys`; the handle's members; the
  parameters `anchor`, `removed`, `instance`).

```text
contract Registry(maxDatumBytes = 384) {
  state { admin: Key, isOpen: Bool }
  owned Ballot keyed by voter (signed, maxKeyBytes = 28) { voter: Key, choice: Int }
  init() { return { admin: caller, isOpen: true } }
  owned init Ballot.cast(registry: shared, voter: Key, choice: Int) {
    require(registry.isOpen, "voting is closed")
    return { voter, choice }
  }
  owned action Ballot.change(pick: Int) only voter { return { ...state, choice: pick } }
  owned destroy Ballot.leave() only voter retire { pay(voter, balance) }
}
```

**Script purposes** (ADR-0010, M3c). A handler runs when the contract's script is used for a purpose other than a
spend or a mint: `withdraw` for its own staking credential's rewards, `certify` for a certificate, `vote` for its votes
as a DRep or committee member, `propose` for a proposal. No instance is spent, so a handler reads only its parameters,
the params and (a withdraw handler) the transaction, and the params say who may: `quorum params.council params.n` or
`authorized params.governor`. The purposes' data is the ledger's: `TxCert`, `Voter`, `Vote`, `GovernanceActionId`,
`ProposalProcedure`, `GovernanceAction` and the types they hold, with JuLC's constructors and fields, read by a field
or an exhaustive `match`; never stored, passed by a caller, encoded or compared (`JSC1320`–`JSC1325`). A
`LedgerMap<Credential, Int>` (a treasury withdrawal's, a committee update's) is read-only: `size`, `isEmpty`, `keys`,
`values`, `get`, `has`, `any`, `all`, `fold`. `std/certs` holds the exact certificate tests (`isRegistration`,
`delegatesOnlyTo`, `isDRepLifecycle`); a vote delegation to a given DRep is a `match` over the delegatee. Two limits:
`ParameterChange.parameters` is `PlutusData` in the ledger and is never read (`JSC1320`), so a constitution guardrail over
proposed parameter changes stays in Java; and a handler reads no `funds` (`JSC1315`). A withdraw handler's sends are
`Value.lovelace(n)` written as such (`JSC1340`), each positive. `stakeSelf` and a withdraw handler are not accepted
beside owned types yet (`JSC1305`).

A contract with a `vote` or `propose` handler compiles without a CIP-57 blueprint: JuLC's blueprint writer has no
vocabulary for those purposes yet, so pass `-Ajulc.blueprint=false` to `compileJava`, as examples/dsl and examples/staking
do (every validator's own `<Name>Validator.plutus.json` is still written).

```text
contract StakedVault(stakeSelf) {
  params { council: List<Key>, quorum: Int, pool: Bytes, payee: Key, cap: Int }
  state { deposits: Int }
  init() payable { return { deposits: received } }
  withdraw collect(amount: Int) quorum params.council params.quorum {
    if amount > 0 { send(wallet(params.payee), Value.lovelace(amount)) }
  }
  certify certificate(cert: TxCert) quorum params.council params.quorum =
    isRegistration(cert) || delegatesOnlyTo(cert, params.pool)
  vote vote(voter: Voter, action: GovernanceActionId, choice: Vote) quorum params.council params.quorum = true
  propose proposal(p: ProposalProcedure) = match p.governanceAction {
    TreasuryWithdrawals { withdrawals } => withdrawals.values.sum() <= params.cap,
    _ => true
  }
}
```

**Migration** (ADR-0011 D4, M3c). An instance moves into its successor version in one transaction: the old version's
`destroy upgrade() only admin migrates to successor { }` (a `Bytes` or `Hash` state field the admin sets; never a
params field, `JSC1331`) burns its token and moves its whole value, and the new version's
`init migrate from params.previous(old: CounterV1.State) { … }` mints the new instance for it, from the old state. A
migrating destroy has no effects (`JSC1332`) and an audience (`JSC1333`). An action that writes the successor field
warns (`JSC9014`: it can redirect the migration after users relied on it) unless it requires the field unset,
`require(successor == #, "the successor is set once")`, which fixes it once; check then that the new successor is a
28-byte policy (`require(length(next) == 28, …)`), since a set-once successor of another length could never migrate
(review F8). The adopting version
imports a previous version that declares a migrating destroy (`JSC1336`), and its ordinary `init` never consumes an
instance of that version: only `init migrate` adopts one.

**Invariants** (ADR-0009 D4) are checked by the validator on every state it accepts as an output (a creation and every
action; a destroy has none), and by the runtime before it submits. A state that breaks one can only be destroyed.

##### Modifiers

| Modifier | Annotation | Allowed on | Field type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `payable` | `@Payable` | `init`, `action`, an owned init, an owned action, an owned destroy (M3a2); not a keyed retiring exit (`JSC1245`), a handler (`JSC1313`) or an init migrate (`JSC1339`) | |
| `only f` | `@SignedBy("f")` | `action`, `destroy`, an owned action or destroy (M3a: `f` is the object's field), a keyed action and its retiring exit (M3b, its signer); not a handler (`JSC1313`) | `Key` (`JSC0311`) |
| `after f` | `@ValidAfter("f")` | `action`, `destroy`, an owned action or destroy (an owned destroy with it is no escape hatch, `JSC1209`); not a retiring exit (`JSC1245`) or a handler (`JSC1313`) | `Int` |
| `before f` | `@ValidBefore("f")` | as `after f` | `Int` |
| `open` | none | `action`, `destroy`, an owned action or destroy; not a keyed action (`JSC1246`) or a handler (`JSC1313`) | |
| `batched` | `@Batched` | `action` (`JSC0418`) | |
| `batched only` | `@Batched(only = true)`: intent-only, no direct call | `action` | |
| `quorum k t` | `@Quorum(keys = "k", threshold = "t")` | `action`, `destroy`, an owned action or destroy (the object's fields or `params.f`), a keyed action; a withdraw, certify or vote handler over `params.*` only (`JSC1312`, `JSC1313`); not a retiring exit (`JSC1245`), a propose handler (`JSC1313`) or a batched action (`JSC0417`) | `List<Key>` and `Int`, both state fields or both `params.f` (`JSC0439`) |
| `authorized c` | `@AuthorizedBy("c")` | as `quorum k t` | `Credential`, a state field (an owned method: the object's) or `params.f` |
| `receives`, `receives T` | `@Receives`, and the method takes `Funds` | `action` (`JSC0447`), not `batched` | `T`: the type of the deposits' memos, each a checked input |
| `admits T` | `@Admits("T")` | an instance `action`, not `batched` (`JSC1212`), whose first parameter is the arriving object's id (`Bytes`) and whose optional second is the object as it arrives (`T`; not for a type that keeps a `BigMap`, `JSC1212`); `T` an owned type with a move (`into`, `JSC1214`), never a keyed type (`JSC1247`) | |
| `retire` | `@OwnedDestroy(retire = true)` | an owned destroy of a keyed type (`JSC1245`) | |
| `migrates to f` | `@MigrateTo("f")` | an instance `destroy` (`JSC1330`) | `Bytes` or `Hash`, a state field, not a time value (`JSC1330`, `JSC1331`) |

`quorum k t` (ADR-0009 D2) holds when at least `t ≥ 1` of the transaction's signatories are in `k`, read from the
input state, never the result. Every state the validator accepts as an output keeps each state quorum *well formed*
(keys strictly ascending, so distinct, each 28 bytes, and 1 ≤ `t` ≤ their number), and a params quorum is checked at
creation, so no rotation can lock the contract. `authorized c` (ADR-0009 D3) holds when the key credential `c` signed, or
the script `c` is withdrawn from in the transaction with an `Approvals` redeemer listing `(policy, instance, action)` (a
native script, which has no redeemer, approves through its withdrawal alone); never this contract's own script or a JOUST
verifier. Both are an audience (J16). Neither is allowed in an `init`
(`JSC0405`) or a batched action (`JSC0417`), and neither field holds a time value (`JSC0524`). A contract with a quorum over
state fields has no batched actions (`JSC0440`, ADR-0009 r3): a batch's states are not checked, so a batched action could
make the quorum unreachable; a quorum over params may be combined with them. `quorum` and
`authorized` are modifier words only in a method's header: a state field may be called `quorum` (`quorum council quorum`).

Modifiers name state fields (`quorum` and `authorized` also `params.f`), never parameters (`JSC0310`). Each is given at most once (`JSC0416`). A `batched` action
cannot also have `only`, `after` or `before` (`JSC0417`): the batcher signs a batch and sets its window, so check the
caller or the time in the body. A paying one says `open` (`JSC0420`): an intent authorises its action until its
deadline, against the state a batcher applies it to, in the batcher's order, so keep deadlines short and bound
order-sensitive arguments. A contract with `BigMap` state cannot have batched actions (`JSC0419`). `batched only`
followed by an identifier that is not a modifier reads as `batched` plus `only f` (then refused), and the modifier
words are no field or binding name (`JSC0211`).

**Composition (M2c, ADR-0011).** A parameter `p: reads params.f` is the state of the instance the params field `f` (an
`Instance<C>`) names, read from a reference input the validator authenticates (`@Reads("params.f") C.State p`, placed
right after the params): in an action or a destroy (`JSC0443`), of a contract without `BigMap` state (`JSC0451`); the
state is a checked input (`#read:`). A field the other contract sets from its own window is a time value: check
staleness with `require(before(p.updatedAt + maxAge))`. An action that `receives` takes the deposits claimed on its
output, `funds.deposits` (`JSC0448` elsewhere), each with `d.value` and, for `receives T`, `d.memo` (each memo decoded and
checked where the action starts: `#memo:`). It also takes `Ctx`.

**What composition trusts.** Nothing on chain binds an `Instance<C>` to `C`: the deployer who sets the params must point
it at an instance of `C` (for a deposit, one whose contract receives), and a deposit into a script that ignores deposit
claims is value the transaction's builder can take. A read state is the datum of any script at that instance's policy
whose outer shape is `C.State`'s; its nested `Bool`, `Option` and enum tags are taken as `C` wrote them, which holds when
`C` is a `.jsc` build (its validator refuses malformed tags in what it stores). A deposit may come from any input of the
transaction, a wallet's included, and its memo is the depositor's claim, not proof of who deposited: credit by `d.value`,
never grant anything by the memo alone.

##### Statements

| Statement | Meaning | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `const x = e`, `const x: T = e` | binds `x` | must be used (`JSC0215`) |
| `require(cond, "msg")` | fails the call unless `cond` holds | the message is a string literal (`JSC0131`) |
| `pay(to, amount)` | a payout of `amount` lovelace to the `Key` `to` | only in an action or destroy, not in a value block, `fn`, view or lambda (`JSC0413`); 0 is skipped, negative fails |
| `if c { … } else { … }` | branches; `else if` chains | as a statement, its arms end in statements (`JSC0314`) |
| `match e { … }` | branches by case | exhaustive (`JSC0924`); as a statement, its arms end in statements |
| `for (const x of xs) { … }` | runs the body per element, in order | the body has no value (`JSC1011`); effects in it accumulate in list order |
| `send(to, v[, d])`, `mint`, `burn`, `accept`, `emit`, `deposit(i, v, m)` | the effects: see [Effects and audiences](#effects-and-audiences) | in an action or a destroy |

A block used as a value (a lambda's block, a value `if` or `match` arm) holds only `const` and `require` statements
(`JSC0315`).

##### Expressions

###### Operators and precedence

Lowest first. Binary operators are left-associative; comparisons do not chain (`JSC0134`).

| Level | Operators | Operands | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `c ? a : b` | `Bool` condition | lazy: only the taken arm runs |
| 2 | `o ?? d` | `Option<T>`, `T` | `d` runs only when `o` is `None`; not mixed with `&&`/`\|\|` without parentheses (`JSC0132`); `None ?? d` is `JSC0337` |
| 3 | `\|\|` | `Bool` | lazy |
| 4 | `&&` | `Bool` | lazy |
| 5 | `==`, `!=` | comparable values of one type | structural, through generated helpers; `===` is `JSC0133` |
| 6 | `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` | two `Int`s or two `Bytes` (`JSC0334`) | |
| 7 | `+`, `-` | `Int` | |
| 8 | `*`, `/`, `%` | `Int` | `/` truncates toward zero (`QuotientInteger`), `%` takes the dividend's sign (`RemainderInteger`), as JavaScript's `BigInt`; a zero divisor fails. `div` and `mod` in `std/math` floor |
| 9 | `!`, unary `-` | `Bool`, `Int` | |
| 10 | `x.f`, `x.m(args)`, `m[k]` | | a field, a property or a method; `m[k]` on a `BigMap<K, Int>` |

###### Equality

`==` and `!=` are defined on `Int`, `Bool`, `Bytes`, `Key`, `Hash`, lists, maps, options, records and enums whose
components are comparable. They lower to generated helpers: field by field, `ByteStringLib.equals` on bytes,
`compareTo == 0` on integers, element by element on lists and maps, tag then fields on enums and options. No `.jsc`
equality is Java `equals` or a reference comparison. `xs.contains`, `indexOf`, `m.get`, `m.has` use the same rules. A
`BigMap`, or a state holding one, is not comparable (`JSC0812`): it is a witness of a Merkle root, not its contents.

###### Laziness

Only the taken arm of `if`, `match` and `?:`, the needed side of `&&` and `||`, and the default of `??` when the
option is empty run, on the JVM and on chain. A division, a failing `require` or a map read in an untaken branch
never happens.

###### Lists, maps and options

| On | Members |
|---|---|
| `List<T>` | `length`, `isEmpty`, `head` (properties); `contains(x)`, `any(f)`, `all(f)`, `find(f)` (`Option`), `filter(f)`, `map(f)`, `fold(init, (acc, x) => …)`, `sum()` (`List<Int>`), `reverse()`, `concat(ys)`, `take(n)`, `drop(n)` (`n < 0` fails). Literals `[a, b]`, `[x, ...rest]` (the spread last) |
| `range(a, b)` | `any`, `all`, `fold`, `filter`, `map` and `for … of` only (`JSC1009`) |
| `Map<K, V>` | `Map.empty()`; `get(k)` (`Option`), `has(k)`, `set(k, v)`, `delete(k)`, `size`, `keys`, `values`, `isEmpty`, `any((k, v) => …)`, `all(…)`, `fold(init, (acc, k, v) => …)`, in key order. `set` checks the key's length |
| `BigMap<K, V>` | `get(k)`, `has(k)`, `m[k]` (`BigMap<K, Int>`: 0 when absent), `set(k, v)`, `delete(k)`, `isEmpty` (a destroy only), `BigMap.empty()` (an `init` only). See [BigMap rules](#bigmap-rules) |
| `Option<T>` | `Some(x)`, `None`, `o ?? d`, `match` |

Lambdas are only direct arguments of these methods: `x => e`, `(acc, x) => e`, or a value block. They capture
`const`s and cannot be stored or returned.

##### Values and funds

A `Value` is a multi-asset value: quantities by (policy, token name), lovelace under the empty policy and name. It is
canonical in the ledger's order, and every quantity stays within the signed 128-bit range; an operation that would
leave it fails, as the ledger's builtins do on-chain.

| Expression | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Value.none()`, `Value.lovelace(n)`, `Value.asset(policy, name, n)` | the empty value; lovelace; a token (`policy` a `Hash`, `name` at most 32 bytes) |
| `v + w`, `v - w`, `v == w`, `v != w` | entry by entry; equality of entries |
| `v.lovelace`, `v.of(policy, name)` | a quantity, 0 when absent |
| `v.covers(w)` | `v` holds at least `w` of every entry (fails on a negative quantity) |
| `isEmpty(v)`, `withoutLovelace(v)`, `scale(k, v)` | from [`std/value`](https://joust.julc.dev/languages/jsc-std/) |
| `paymentKey(a)`, `paymentScript(a)` | from [`std/address`](https://joust.julc.dev/languages/jsc-std/): the key or script an address pays to, as an `Option` |

`funds` is the native assets a call sees, in an `init`, action or destroy: `funds.received` (what the caller offers,
no lovelace: that is `received`), `funds.held` (what the instance holds besides lovelace and its own token),
`funds.policy` (the contract's policy) and `funds.self` (the instance's token name). A method that reads `funds`, or
sends, mints, burns, accepts or receives, is lowered with the processor's `Funds` parameter. `funds.deposits` (M2c) is a
receiving action's deposits.

**Stored values (M2c).** A field of the state, the params, a record or a variant may be a `Value`. It is stored in its
wire form (cardano-client-lib's canonical order) and read back in the ledger's: the lowering converts where the field is
read (`ValueAdapter.fromWire`, which also refuses a malformed one) and where the record is built (`ValueAdapter.toWire`),
so the datum the validator compares is the one the runtime writes.

##### Effects and audiences

| Statement | Effect | Generated check (key) |
|---|---|---|
| `pay(to, n)` | a payout of `n` lovelace to the key `to`; 0 is skipped | `n` is not negative (`#pay:`) |
| `send(to, v)`, `send(to, v, d)` | an output of `v` to the address `to`; M2c: with the inline datum `d`, any value of the contract's own types, built by a generated encoder | every quantity positive, no reserved name of the own policy, never to the contract's own script (`#send:`) |
| `deposit(i, v, m)` | M2c (ADR-0011 D3): `v` into the instance `i` (an `Instance<C>` from the params), which `C`'s receiving action takes in the same transaction; `m` the memo, any value of the contract's own types | `v` not empty, every quantity positive, no reserved-kind name under any policy (`#deposit:`). The target's contract must receive (`JSC0449`), and one of its receiving actions decode the memo (`JSC0450`); no time value in `v` (`JSC0526`) |
| `mint(name, n)`, `burn(name, n)` | `n` more, or fewer, of the own policy's `name`; the net is what the transaction mints | `n` positive, `name` a user token of at most 32 bytes (`#mint:`) |
| `accept(v)` | the method takes in `v` | native assets only, every quantity positive (`#accept:`); at the end, the sum accepted equals `funds.received` (`#funds:`) |
| `emit(e)` | an event (a value of the contract's `Event`), in source order | none in the method; the validator requires the redeemer to carry exactly these events (ADR-0009 D5) |

Each kind accumulates **in source order** (in a `for`, in list order; an effect in an untaken branch does not happen);
`mint` and `accept` are net sums. An `init` takes no effect but may read `funds` (`JSC0404`; `accept` in an init is
not supported yet, `JSC0426`). `accept` needs `payable` (`JSC0422`), and a payable method that reads `funds`, sends,
mints or burns must state what it takes in, `accept(Value.none())` for nothing (`JSC0423`). A method that can reach a
`pay`, `send`, `mint`, `burn` or `deposit` in any arm or loop must have `only <field>` or `open` (`JSC0408`). A deposit
alone takes no `Funds` (a payable method that only deposits takes ADA). An action that deposits returns `Outcome` with
`deposits`; a destroy that deposits returns `Settled`. A contract with native
assets has no `batched` actions (`JSC0424`). An action with effects returns `Outcome`, or `Received` when it takes native
assets; a destroy that sends, mints, burns or emits returns `Settled` (the processor's result records). A batched action
never returns events: when a direct action's `Outcome` holds them, a batched action that pays returns
`Stepped(state, payouts)`. These names, and the annotations the lowering imports (`Invariant`, `Params`, `Quorum`,
`AuthorizedBy`), are reserved. Events (M2b) come
last in each record, and a method whose record has them carries them last in its redeemer (empty when it emits none). An
`emit` is allowed in an action or a destroy (`JSC0413`), not in a batched action (`JSC0425`); the contract must declare
an event (`JSC0438`).

##### Time (D11)

`validFrom` and `validTo` are the only sources of *time values*. A value is a time value if it depends on one through
any expression (`min`, `max` and `abs` included), a `const`, a `fn` argument, a record, list, map or option, a lambda
or `match` binding, or a **time field**: a state field any method sets to a time value, contract-wide (the ABI
manifest lists them as `timeFields`).

- **Deciding.** A time value may not be a condition of `if`, `?:` or `require`, an operand of `&&`, `||` or `!`, a
  collection predicate, or a comparison whose result is used (`JSC0502`, `JSC0514`). The only comparisons with time
  are `after(t)` and `before(t)`, which hold for the whole window and are allowed only as the condition of a `require`
  or an operand of `&&` or `||` at its top (`JSC0506`); never under `!`, in an `if`, a `?:`, a `const`, a `fn` or a
  lambda (`JSC0504`), nor in a view (`JSC0503`). `t` may be a stored time, but not one computed from this call's window (`JSC0505`:
  `after(validFrom - 1)`).
- **Shapes are never time values**: a value's constructor, an option's presence, a list's length and a map's keys.
  So `match` may scrutinise a value holding a time value (its bindings stay time values), and `xs.isEmpty`,
  `m.has(k)` and `== None` are ordinary.
- **Failing.** A time value may not be a divisor (`JSC0515`), a domain-checked `std` argument (`JSC0509`), a map key
  (`JSC0517`), a range bound (`JSC0516`), a `take`/`drop` count (`JSC0512`), an `nth` index (`JSC0510`), a `Key` or
  `Hash` conversion (`JSC0507`), a `BigMap<K, Int>` value (`JSC0518`), a `Value`'s quantity (`JSC0519`), any part of a
  sent or accepted value (`JSC0520`, `JSC0522`) or a mint or burn quantity (`JSC0521`), and it never decides whether
  `paymentKey` or `paymentScript` is `Some` (`JSC0523`). A field that holds a time value is never a quorum's keys or
  threshold or an authorized credential (`JSC0524`), and an invariant never depends on one (`JSC0525`). A `fn` called with a time argument is checked with that
  parameter as a time value.
- **Flowing.** Arithmetic on time values is allowed, and they may set state and amounts. A payout set by one must be
  exactly `pay(to, max(0, …))` (`JSC0501`). Warnings name the bias: a stored window value (`JSC9003`), a value derived
  from a stored time (`JSC9004`), a payout (`JSC9005`), an event that carries one (`JSC9008`).

The submitter chooses the window, within `maxValidityMs`: `validFrom` can be that much early, `validTo` that much late.
For accrual that pays the caller, measure from `validFrom` (`elapsedSince(t)`); for a charge the caller pays, from
`validTo` (`elapsedSinceAtMost(t)`).

##### BigMap rules

- A field of the state only (`JSC0803`), with `Int` or `Bytes` values (`JSC0804`).
- Its new value is its own field transformed by `set` and `delete`, in that field of the next state:
  `{ ...state, balances: balances.set(to, v) }` (`JSC0811`, `JSC0827`). `set` and `delete` appear nowhere else.
- Never bound to a `const`, passed to a `fn`, held in an option or a list, captured by a lambda (`JSC0814`), compared,
  chosen by a condition or `match`, or used as a fold accumulator (`JSC0813`). A state whose `BigMap` is written is
  never bound, chosen or accumulated either.
- `BigMap.empty()` only as a field's value in an `init` (`JSC0810`, `JSC0817`); `m.isEmpty` ("empty before this call")
  only in a destroy (`JSC0808`).
- `Int` values are non-negative and `set(k, 0)` removes the entry; an `Int` value is stored in at most 8,192 bytes.
  `BigMap<K, Bytes>` tells absence from empty bytes. Keys of `set` and `delete` are at most 64 bytes.
- A method reads its own writes through the chain: `balances.set(caller, left)[to]`.

Every read and write is proven against the root by the shared map verifier ([MerkleMaps](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/merklemaps/)).

##### Libraries

A file headed `library <package>` is a **`.jsc` library** (ADR-0018 D9): imports, types, enums and fns, and no contract
(`JSC0711`). Contracts and other libraries import from it by its path relative to the importing file:

```jsc
// contracts/app/fees.jsc
jsc 1
library app

type Line = { to: Key, bps: Int }
enum Tier { Basic, Gold { since: Int } }

fn fee(amount: Int, bps: Int): Int = amount * bps / 10_000
fn rate(t: Tier): Int = match t { Basic => 100, Gold { since } => since >= 10 ? 25 : 50 }
```

```jsc
// contracts/app/Shop.jsc
jsc 1
package app

import { Line, Tier, fee, rate } from "./fees.jsc"

contract Shop {
  state { owner: Key, price: Int, lines: List<Line>, tier: Tier }
  init(price: Int, lines: List<Line>) { return { owner: caller, price, lines, tier: Basic } }
  action buy() payable {
    require(received >= price + fee(price, rate(tier)), "pay the price and the fee")
    return state
  }
}
```

| Rule | |
|---|---|
| The class | A library lowers to a JuLC `@OnchainLibrary` class of its package, named by its file: `fees.jsc` is `app.Fees` (`JSC0705` when the file name makes no class name). Its fns are `public static`, its types nested records and sealed interfaces (`Fees.Line`, `Fees.Tier`), so **Java contracts call it** as they call any on-chain library (`examples/dsl`'s `JavaShop.java`). Its generated helpers are package-private, named with `__`. A Java caller skips `.jsc`'s ingress checks: the library's fns assume a `Key` of 28 bytes, a `Hash` of 28 or 32 and canonical maps, which only `.jsc` callers guarantee, so a Java contract that builds `new Fees.Line(bytes, …)` checks those lengths itself |
| Imports | `./x.jsc` and `../dir/x.jsc`, resolved from the importing file and never outside the source folder (`JSC0706`). Only a library can be imported (`JSC0708`), and only names it declares (`JSC0708`). Libraries may import libraries, without cycles (`JSC0707`) |
| Scope | A file sees its own declarations and the names it imports; importing an enum brings its variants. A library's other declarations are not in scope (`JSC0710`), but its values flow: a fn may return a record whose type the caller did not import, and the caller reads its fields. `std` imports are per file |
| One namespace | The declarations of a build (a contract and every library it imports, transitively) share one namespace: no two of them, in any of its files, have the same name (`JSC0709`), and none takes a library's class name. No binding (a parameter, const, lambda parameter or match binding) takes a library's class name either, and two libraries of a build never share a file name, even in different packages (`JSC0709`): the generated Java names a library by its class. A method of the contract named like a library variant is refused as for its own (`JSC0203`). Known limit: two third-party libraries that declare one name cannot be combined, as there is no aliasing yet |
| Checking | A library is checked on its own, and again in each contract that imports it. The time rule (D11) runs through library calls: a library fn called with a time value is checked with that parameter marked, so a division or a `require` on it is refused at the call. An error in a library is reported at the import that brings it into the build, naming the library's own position (`JSC0712`) |
| Inputs | A library's types are checked inputs like the contract's: a `Line` in a redeemer has its `Key` checked to 28 bytes before the method runs |
| Artifacts | A library has no ABI manifest of its own: each contract's manifest states the library types its datum and redeemers reach (`"kind": "library"`, with the library's class). Each contract's IR export carries the libraries it imports (format 2), so the JavaScript reference interpreter evaluates their fns, and its message map lists a library's messages with the library's file (`"file": "fees.jsc"`) |
| Identity | A library's package and file name are its class, which importing files and Java contracts name: renaming either is a code change of every importer, and may change the scripts that use it: JuLC's shape-check ids follow library class names (JuLC ADR-078) |

###### Library packages and `joust.lock`

An npm package ships libraries under its `joust-lib/` folder: `.jsc` libraries, and the on-chain sources of Java
libraries (`joust-lib/<package path>/<Class>.java`). A `.jsc` file imports a package's `.jsc` library by the package
name and the path under `joust-lib/`, and a Java library by its class:

```jsc
import { fee } from "@acme/fees/fees.jsc"        // node_modules/@acme/fees/joust-lib/fees.jsc
import { cap } from "java:acme.allow.Limits"      // node_modules/<any package>/joust-lib/acme/allow/Limits.java
```

A package library's own relative imports stay inside its package (`JSC0706`). A Java library from a package is
certified like one from Gradle's `joustLibrary`, and the same codes apply. Of a package's Java sources, a build compiles
only the source closure of each library a `.jsc` file imports with `java:` or a hand-written Java contract imports; no
other package source reaches the build. Links under `joust-lib/` are not followed, and two packages that ship one Java
path are refused, as is a library that declares a class in one of the project's own packages.

**`joust.lock`** (committed at the project's root) pins every library that comes from **outside the project's sources**
by the SHA-256 of its on-chain sources: a package's `.jsc` library (with the libraries it imports), or a Java library's
source closure (every source file its class's file names, transitively; keyed by its path inside `joust-lib/`), whether
a `.jsc` file imports it with `java:` or a hand-written Java contract imports it (ADR-0018 J12). `joust build` lists every library it used with its hash. It fails with `JSC0731` when
such a library is not pinned, and with `JSC0732` when its sources differ from the pin. Review the library, then run
`joust build --accept-lock`, which writes the lock to commit. The project's own `.jsc` libraries are part of its sources
and are not pinned. On Gradle, `generateJsc` checks `joust.lock` for the `joustLibrary` libraries, and `acceptJoustLock`
writes it.

```json
{ "lock": 1, "libraries": { "@acme/fees/fees.jsc": "…64 hex…", "java:acme.allow.Limits": "…64 hex…" } }
```

##### Java libraries (`java:`)

A `.jsc` file may import the public static methods and records of a Java (JuLC) on-chain library whose **on-chain
sources** are on the library path and **certified** (ADR-0018 D9, M4b):

```jsc
import { Entry, isAllowed, limitOf, entry } from "java:org.example.compliance.AllowList"
```

On Gradle, the library's jar goes in the `joustLibrary` configuration, as sources only:

```groovy
dependencies {
    joustLibrary 'org.example:compliance:1.0'   // its META-INF/plutus-sources
}
```

The build extracts the library's `META-INF/plutus-sources`, compiles them into the project (the JVM side runs these
sources, never the jar's classes), and certifies them before any import is admitted. Certification covers:

- each signature's exact Java types, mapped to `.jsc` or refused;
- every reachable body, checked with `SubsetLint`;
- no casts and no reference equality;
- only calls into the trusted base (D8's table, JOUST's `Require` and adapters, an allow-list of `BigInteger`, `JulcList`,
  `JulcMap` and `Optional` operations);
- none of the catalogue of known JVM/on-chain differences.

`checkJoustLibraries` fails when a library class also reaches the runtime class path from a jar. When a contract is
loaded, the runtime checks the bytes of each library class against the build's.

| Rule | Code |
|---|---|
| No sources of the class on the library path | `JSC0720` |
| The library is not certified (each problem, with its file and line) | `JSC0721` |
| A fn whose signature does not map (`PlutusData`, maps, values, `void`, generics, fixed-width numbers) | `JSC0722` |
| An overloaded name | `JSC0723` |
| A Java record is read-only: built by the library's fns, never by an object literal | `JSC0724` |
| An opaque record (a field that does not map) is never written as a type, read or compared | `JSC0725` |
| A time value never reaches a Java fn (D11) | `JSC0726` |
| A library class also on the runtime class path (Gradle) | `JSC0727` |

`byte[]` maps to `Bytes` (a Java signature cannot say `Key`): make a `Key` of a result with `asKey(b)`. The reference
interpreters do not evaluate a Java library's body: a call that reaches one has no answer there, and such calls are
differential-tested on the JVM, the transition program and the validator, beside the library's own per-function vectors.
The details, and the catalogue, are in
[jsc-2-java-libraries.md](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/docs/reference/jsc-2-java-libraries.md).

##### The ABI manifest

For every `.jsc` contract the lowering writes `<Contract>.abi.json` (format `"abi": 2`), which the project commits
beside the `.jsc` file:

| Key | Content |
|---|---|
| `contract`, `source` | the qualified contract name and the `.jsc` file |
| `datum` | the `State` constructor, its fields in order, each with its `.jsc` type and data shape |
| `params` (M2b) | the `Config` constructor the script is applied to, when the contract declares params |
| `redeemers.spend` | one constructor per action, then per destroy, in source order, with its index and fields (the generated `ctx`, M2's `assetsIn` and M2b's `events` included) |
| `redeemers.mint` | `CreateInstance` (`seed`, `ctx`) and `BurnInstance` |
| `types` | every schema the datum and the redeemers reach: records, enums, imported library types (`"kind": "library"`, with the library's class), and API and ledger types such as `Ctx`, `TxOutRef`, `MerkleMap` |
| `timeFields` | the state's time fields |

Views are not encoded, so moving or adding a view does not change the manifest.

**The gate.** Every build compares the lowering's manifest with the committed one. Equal passes. A missing manifest
fails with `JSC0003`; a different one with `JSC0002`, naming the first line that differs; and Java lowered from a file
whose manifest is refused is not written. The only ways to accept a new or changed manifest are explicit:

| Path | Accept |
|---|---|
| npm | `joust build --accept-abi`, `joust dev --accept-abi` |
| Gradle (plugin `org.julclang.joust`) | `./gradlew acceptJscAbi` |
| JVM | `JscMain <srcDir> <outDir> --accept-abi` |

No Gradle property, system property or `gradle.properties` line switches the gate off. Review the diff and commit
the manifest: a change means a deployed instance's datum or redeemers would be read differently, so the new contract
must be deployed as a new script.

**The cross-check.** Each manifest is also compared, structurally, with the processor's description of the same
contract (constructor indices, field names and order, data shapes, every reachable schema): at every npm build, and on
Gradle in `checkJscAbi`, after `compileJava`, as part of `check`. A difference is `JSC0004`, an internal error of the
lowering; please report it.

##### Diagnostics

Every error and warning has a stable code and a position, on both build paths. Gradle (`JscMain`) prints, with the
file relative to `src/main/jsc`:

```text
Ledger.jsc:34:13: error[JSC0502]: a time value cannot decide here: compare times only with after(t) or before(t) in a require (ADR-0018 D11)
Ledger.jsc:72:3: warning[JSC9001]: settle never reads balance; a destroy must pay out everything the instance holds
```

`joust build` prints the same shape, the file relative to the contracts folder (ADR-0021 D9: one shape, which the VS Code
extension's `$joust` problem matcher reads).

A code names one rule and is never reused; a message may change wording, its code does not. The full list, checked
against the sources by a test, is the
[diagnostics catalogue](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/docs/reference/jsc-2-diagnostics.md). The ranges:

| Codes | Area |
|---|---|
| `JSC0001`–`JSC0004` | files and the ABI manifest |
| `JSC01xx` | syntax and JavaScript habits |
| `JSC02xx` | names and declarations |
| `JSC03xx` | types and expressions |
| `JSC04xx` | methods, modifiers, effects |
| `JSC05xx` | time (D11) |
| `JSC06xx` | recursion |
| `JSC07xx` | imports |
| `JSC08xx` | maps |
| `JSC09xx` | enums and `match` |
| `JSC10xx` | lists, loops and lambdas |
| `JSC9xxx` | warnings |

A diagnostic of javac or the JOUST processor on generated Java is reported at the `.jsc` line and column the source
map gives, with the generated file and line as a note.

##### Running the lowering

| Entry point | Use |
|---|---|
| `org.julclang.state.dsl.JscMain <srcDir> <outDir> [--accept-abi]` | Lowers every `.jsc` under `srcDir` into `outDir` (emptied first), with each `.jsc` file's source map; checks (or with `--accept-abi` writes) the ABI manifests. A file's `./x.jsc` imports resolve to other files of `srcDir`. Exits 1 on an error, 2 on bad usage. Gradle's `generateJsc` and `acceptJscAbi` run it |
| `JscMain --check-abi <srcDir> <descriptionsDir>` | Checks every manifest against the processor's descriptions (`checkJscAbi`) |
| `JscMain.lowerWithWarnings(source, fileName)` | `Lowered(java, diagnostics, fileName, sourceMapJson, abiJson)` for one file, on its own (it imports no libraries and no contracts) |
| `JscMain.lowerWithWarnings(source, fileName, id, modules)` | The same for the file `id` of a build whose other files `modules` (`JscModules.of(files)`) finds: its libraries (M4) and the contracts it imports (M2c, `import contract`) |
| `Toolchain.build(files, options)` (`julc-state-toolchain`) | Lowers `.jsc` entries, then compiles everything as Gradle does; used by `joust build` |

### .jsc standard library

URL: https://joust.julc.dev/languages/jsc-std/

A `.jsc` contract calls three kinds of functions: the **prelude** (always in scope), the **`std` modules** (imported
by name), and its own `fn`s. List and map methods (`xs.fold`, `m.get`) are on the
[language reference](https://joust.julc.dev/languages/jsc-reference/#lists-maps-and-options).

```jsc
import { blake2b_224 } from "std/crypto"
import { slice, length } from "std/bytes"
```

An import names functions of one module. A function used without its import is an error (`JSC0704`, which names the
module to import it from); a name imported from the wrong module is `JSC0702`; a `fn` with an imported name is
`JSC0703`.

> **A preview:** 
`.jsc` is a preview ([ADR-0018](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/docs/adr/0018-jsc-2-immutable-contract-language.md)).

##### How a row is bound

Each `std` function is a row of a binding table
([`Std.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-dsl/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/dsl/v2/Std.java),
ADR-0018 D8): a `.jsc` signature, a Java target, a conversion policy and a domain. The generated Java calls the target,
so the same function runs on the JVM and, compiled by JuLC, on chain.

| Policy | Meaning |
|---|---|
| direct | Every argument and the result have the same Java type on both sides (`byte[]`, `boolean`, `BigInteger`) |
| long result | The target returns a `long`, which goes straight into `BigInteger.valueOf`; no `Int` argument is narrowed |
| adapter | The target is a JOUST API adapter (`BytesAdapter`, `MathAdapter`, `BitsAdapter`, `CryptoAdapter` in `julc-state-api`) that takes `BigInteger`s, checks the domain with a `require` on both sides, then narrows and calls JuLC's stdlib |
| generated | No library target: the lowering generates the code, and the reference interpreter implements it independently |

**Domain:** the arguments a function accepts. Outside it the call fails, on the JVM before anything is submitted and on
chain alike. **A time value as an argument:** whether a value that depends on `validFrom` or `validTo` may reach the
function. Only functions that are total and whose cost does not depend on the window accept one
([the time rule](https://joust.julc.dev/languages/jsc-reference/#time-d11)); passing a time value to any other is an error at the call
(`JSC0509`).

A test (`JscV2BindingTest` in `julc-state-toolchain`) resolves every row's Java target with javac and compares it with
the table, so a JuLC upgrade that renames or retypes a function fails JOUST's build, never your contract. The tables
below are generated from the same table and checked by `JscV2StdDocTest`.

##### The prelude

No import needed.

| Function | Signature | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `min`, `max` | `min(Int, Int): Int` | The smaller or larger of two `Int`s |
| `abs` | `abs(Int): Int` | The absolute value |
| `utf8` | `utf8("text"): Bytes` | The UTF-8 bytes of a string literal (the only place a string is a value) |
| `asKey` | `asKey(Bytes): Key` | A checked conversion to a 28-byte key hash: a literal is checked when the file compiles (`JSC0323`), any other value at run time. A time value cannot reach it (`JSC0507`) |
| `asHash` | `asHash(Bytes): Hash` | The same, to a 28-byte script hash or policy id |
| `range` | `range(a, b)` | The `Int`s from `a` up to `b`, exclusive; empty when `b <= a`. Only the receiver of `any`, `all`, `fold`, `filter` or `map`, or the list of a `for` loop: no list is built (`JSC1009`). A bound cannot be a time value (`JSC0516`) |
| `Some` | `Some(x): Option<T>` | A present `Option`; `None` is the absent one. `Some(None)` is refused (`JSC0322`) |
| `after`, `before` | `after(Int): Bool` | The whole validity window is after (before) the time. Only at the top of a `require`, alone or under `&&` or `\|\|` ([time](https://joust.julc.dev/languages/jsc-reference/#time-d11)). Also importable from `std/time` |

##### The modules

`std/list` functions are generic: `T` is the element type of the list they get, and `indexOf` compares with the
structural equality of `==`.

{/* std:begin: generated from JscV2.bindings() by JscV2StdDocTest; do not edit */}
###### `std/crypto`

| Function | Signature | Domain | A time value as an argument | Target (policy) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sha2_256` | `sha2_256(Bytes): Bytes` | any bytes | yes | `CryptoLib.sha2_256` (direct) |
| `sha3_256` | `sha3_256(Bytes): Bytes` | any bytes | yes | `CryptoLib.sha3_256` (direct) |
| `blake2b_256` | `blake2b_256(Bytes): Bytes` | any bytes | yes | `CryptoLib.blake2b_256` (direct) |
| `blake2b_224` | `blake2b_224(Bytes): Bytes` | any bytes | yes | `CryptoLib.blake2b_224` (direct) |
| `verifyEd25519` | `verifyEd25519(Bytes, Bytes, Bytes): Bool` | key of 32 bytes and signature of 64 bytes, else a failure (where the builtin fails); then true or false by libsodium's rules: a small-order key or R, a non-canonical key or S, a key off the curve are false | no | `CryptoAdapter.verifyEd25519` (adapter) |

###### `std/bytes`

| Function | Signature | Domain | A time value as an argument | Target (policy) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `length` | `length(Bytes): Int` | any bytes; the result is in [0, 2^63) | yes | `ByteStringLib.length` (long result) |
| `concat` | `concat(Bytes, Bytes): Bytes` | any bytes | yes | `ByteStringLib.append` (direct) |
| `slice` | `slice(Bytes, Int, Int): Bytes` | start and length in [0, 2^31), else a failure; the result is clamped to b as the builtin does | no | `BytesAdapter.slice` (adapter) |
| `take` | `take(Bytes, Int): Bytes` | n in [0, 2^31), else a failure; at most length(b) bytes | no | `BytesAdapter.take` (adapter) |
| `drop` | `drop(Bytes, Int): Bytes` | n in [0, 2^31), else a failure (F18: the stdlib's drop wraps on the JVM); empty past the end | no | `BytesAdapter.drop` (adapter) |
| `byteAt` | `byteAt(Bytes, Int): Int` | index in [0, length(b)) and below 2^31, else a failure; the result is in [0, 255] | no | `BytesAdapter.at` (adapter) |
| `toInt` | `toInt(Bytes): Int` | any bytes, read as an unsigned big-endian integer (empty is 0) | yes | `ByteStringLib.byteStringToInteger` (direct) |
| `toHex` | `toHex(Bytes): Bytes` | any bytes; lower-case ASCII hex, two characters a byte | yes | `ByteStringLib.toHex` (direct) |

###### `std/math`

| Function | Signature | Domain | A time value as an argument | Target (policy) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `div` | `div(Int, Int): Int` | b != 0, else a failure; rounds toward negative infinity | no | `MathAdapter.div` (adapter) |
| `mod` | `mod(Int, Int): Int` | b != 0, else a failure; the result has b's sign | no | `MathAdapter.mod` (adapter) |
| `pow` | `pow(Int, Int): Int` | exponent in [0, 1024], else a failure (the cost grows with it) | no | `MathAdapter.pow` (adapter) |
| `expMod` | `expMod(Int, Int, Int): Int` | exponent >= 0 and modulus > 0, else a failure; the result is in [0, modulus); the ExpModInteger builtin of protocol version 11 (CIP-109), which the toolchain's PLUTUS_V3_PV11 target provides | no | `MathAdapter.expMod` (adapter) |
| `sign` | `sign(Int): Int` | any Int; -1, 0 or 1 | yes | `MathLib.sign` (direct) |

###### `std/bits`

| Function | Signature | Domain | A time value as an argument | Target (policy) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `andBytes` | `andBytes(Bool, Bytes, Bytes): Bytes` | any bytes; with pad the result is as long as the longer, else as the shorter | yes | `BitwiseLib.andByteString` (direct) |
| `orBytes` | `orBytes(Bool, Bytes, Bytes): Bytes` | any bytes; with pad the result is as long as the longer, else as the shorter | yes | `BitwiseLib.orByteString` (direct) |
| `xorBytes` | `xorBytes(Bool, Bytes, Bytes): Bytes` | any bytes; with pad the result is as long as the longer, else as the shorter | yes | `BitwiseLib.xorByteString` (direct) |
| `complement` | `complement(Bytes): Bytes` | any bytes | yes | `BitwiseLib.complementByteString` (direct) |
| `readBit` | `readBit(Bytes, Int): Bool` | index in [0, 8 * length(b)), else a failure; bit 0 is the last byte's lowest | no | `BitsAdapter.readBit` (adapter) |
| `shift` | `shift(Bytes, Int): Bytes` | n in (-2^31, 2^31), else a failure; positive shifts left, zero bits fill | no | `BitsAdapter.shift` (adapter) |
| `rotate` | `rotate(Bytes, Int): Bytes` | n in (-2^31, 2^31), else a failure; positive rotates left | no | `BitsAdapter.rotate` (adapter) |
| `countSetBits` | `countSetBits(Bytes): Int` | any bytes | yes | `BitwiseLib.countSetBits` (long result) |
| `findFirstSetBit` | `findFirstSetBit(Bytes): Int` | any bytes; -1 when no bit is set | yes | `BitwiseLib.findFirstSetBit` (long result) |

###### `std/list`

| Function | Signature | Domain | A time value as an argument | Target (policy) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `last` | `last(List<T>): Option<T>` | any list; None when empty | yes | none (generated) |
| `nth` | `nth(List<T>, Int): Option<T>` | index >= 0, else a failure; None past the end | no | none (generated) |
| `indexOf` | `indexOf(List<T>, T): Option<Int>` | any list and value (structural equality, D6); the first index, or None | yes | none (generated) |

###### `std/value`

| Function | Signature | Domain | A time value as an argument | Target (policy) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `isEmpty` | `isEmpty(Value): Bool` | any value; true when it holds nothing | yes | `ValueAdapter.isEmpty` (direct) |
| `withoutLovelace` | `withoutLovelace(Value): Value` | any value; its native assets | yes | `ValueAdapter.withoutLovelace` (direct) |
| `scale` | `scale(Int, Value): Value` | every product within the 128-bit range, else a failure (the ledger's scaleValue); 0 gives the empty value | no | `ValueAdapter.scale` (adapter) |

###### `std/address`

| Function | Signature | Domain | A time value as an argument | Target (policy) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `paymentKey` | `paymentKey(Address): Option<Key>` | any address; the key it is paid to, or None for a script's | no | `AddressAdapter.paymentKey` (direct) |
| `paymentScript` | `paymentScript(Address): Option<Hash>` | any address; the script it is paid to, or None for a key's | no | `AddressAdapter.paymentScript` (direct) |

###### `std/certs`

| Function | Signature | Domain | A time value as an argument | Target (policy) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `isRegistration` | `isRegistration(TxCert): Bool` | any certificate; true for RegStaking (with or without a deposit), else false | yes | `Certs.isRegistration` (direct) |
| `delegatesOnlyTo` | `delegatesOnlyTo(TxCert, Bytes): Bool` | any certificate and pool; true for DelegStaking or RegDeleg whose delegatee is exactly Stake of that pool (a StakeVote delegation is false), else false | yes | `Certs.delegatesOnlyTo` (direct) |
| `isDRepLifecycle` | `isDRepLifecycle(TxCert): Bool` | any certificate; true for RegDRep or UpdateDRep, else false | yes | `Certs.isDRepLifecycle` (direct) |

###### `std/time`

| Function | Signature | Domain | A time value as an argument | Target (policy) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `elapsedSince` | `elapsedSince(Int): Int` | max(0, validFrom - t): a lower bound of the time elapsed since t | yes | none (generated) |
| `elapsedSinceAtMost` | `elapsedSinceAtMost(Int): Int` | max(0, validTo - t): an upper bound of the time elapsed since t | yes | none (generated) |
| `windowStart` | `windowStart(): Int` | validFrom: the window's start, to store | yes | none (generated) |
| `windowEnd` | `windowEnd(): Int` | validTo: the window's end, to store | yes | none (generated) |

{/* std:end */}

##### Not bound

- `keccak_256`, ECDSA and Schnorr signatures, RIPEMD-160: the JVM's crypto provider lacks them, and a function is
  bound only when every runtime fails exactly where the ledger's builtin fails (ADR-0018 D8, F18).
- `integerToByteString` and `writeBits`: their domains need checks `.jsc` does not have yet.
- Functions over raw `PlutusData`, and JuLC's transaction libraries (`ContextsLib`, `OutputLib`): the processor owns
  the transaction checks.

For anything else, write the contract, or that part of it, in [Java](https://joust.julc.dev/languages/java/).
