- [.jsc guide](https://joust.julc.dev/languages/jsc/)
- [.jsc reference](https://joust.julc.dev/languages/jsc-reference/)

### TypeScript

URL: https://joust.julc.dev/languages/typescript/

> **Experimental:** 
The npm path runs JOUST's toolchain and runtime as WebAssembly built with GraalVM Web Image, which is itself experimental. Java with Gradle and cardano-client-lib is the supported, first-class path: see [Quick start: Java](https://joust.julc.dev/start/quick-start-java/).

JOUST contracts are written in Java or `.jsc`, not TypeScript. But every contract comes with TypeScript types for the
code that calls it: `joust build` (or `joust-gen`) writes `<Contract>.d.ts` next to the generated client, from the
contract's description. Your editor then knows each method, its arguments and the shape of the state, and `tsc`
catches a misspelt argument or a `number` where bytes were expected.

##### The generated `.d.ts`

The template's Counter:

```java title="contracts/app/Counter.java (abridged)"
public record State(BigInteger count, byte[] owner) {}

@Init public static State init(Ctx ctx) { ... }
@Action public static State increment(State s, BigInteger by) { ... }
@Action @OnlyOwner public static State reset(State s) { ... }
@Destroy @OnlyOwner public static JulcList<Payout> close(State s, Ctx ctx) { ... }
```

gives:

```ts title="build/joust/Counter.d.ts"
// GENERATED by joust-gen from app.Counter. Do not edit.
import type { JoustContract, JoustOptions, CallResult, Cip30Api, Pay, Int, Hex, DataHex } from '@julclang/state-client';

export type Ctx = { "caller": Hex; "received": bigint; "balance": bigint; "validFrom": bigint; "validTo": bigint };
export type CtxIn = { "caller": Hex; "received": Int; "balance": Int; "validFrom": Int; "validTo": Int };
export type CounterValidatorCalls = { $variant: "Increment"; "by": bigint } | { $variant: "Reset" } | { $variant: "Close"; "ctx": Ctx };
export type CounterValidatorCallsIn = { $variant: "Increment"; "by": Int } | { $variant: "Reset" } | { $variant: "Close"; "ctx": CtxIn };
export type TxOutRef = { "txId": Hex; "index": bigint };
export type TxOutRefIn = { "txId": Hex; "index": Int };
export type CounterValidatorLifecycle = { $variant: "CreateInstance"; "seed": TxOutRef; "ctx": Ctx } | { $variant: "BurnInstance" };
export type CounterValidatorLifecycleIn = { $variant: "CreateInstance"; "seed": TxOutRefIn; "ctx": CtxIn } | { $variant: "BurnInstance" };
export type CounterState = { "count": bigint; "owner": Hex };
export type CounterStateIn = { "count": Int; "owner": Hex };
export declare const description: unknown;

export declare class Counter {
  constructor(o: JoustOptions);
  readonly contract: JoustContract;
  deploy(wallet: Cip30Api, args: Record<string, never>): Promise<CallResult & { instance: CounterInstance }>;
  at(instanceId: Hex): CounterInstance;
}
export declare class CounterInstance {
  readonly id: Hex;
  read(): Promise<{ ref: string; state: CounterState; lovelace: bigint } | null>;
  state(): Promise<CounterState | null>;
  increment(wallet: Cip30Api, args: { "by": Int }): Promise<CallResult>;
  reset(wallet: Cip30Api, args?: Record<string, never>): Promise<CallResult>;
  close(wallet: Cip30Api, args?: Record<string, never>): Promise<CallResult>;
}
```

There is one type per definition in the description (the state, the redeemers, `Ctx` and the ledger types they use),
then the client's classes.

###### Type names

Each definition gets the shortest name that is unique: its key without the contract's package, with dots removed
(`app.Counter.State` becomes `CounterState`, `app.CounterValidator.Calls` becomes `CounterValidatorCalls`). Types from
other packages keep their simple name (`org.julclang.state.api.Ctx` becomes `Ctx`). A clash gets a leading `_`.

###### Output types and `In` types

Every type comes twice:

- **`T`**, what JOUST gives you back (decoded state, reports): integers are `bigint`.
- **`TIn`**, what you may pass in (arguments): integers are `Int`, that is `bigint | number | string`.

So `increment(wallet, { by: 5n })`, `{ by: 5 }` and `{ by: '5' }` all type-check, and `state().count` is always a
`bigint`. A `number` must be a safe integer and a string a decimal integer; anything else is refused when the call is
encoded.

###### Schemas to TypeScript

| Description schema | Java | TypeScript (`T`) | TypeScript (`TIn`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `integer` | `BigInteger` | `bigint` | `Int` |
| `bytes` | `byte[]` | `Hex` (lowercase hex `string`) | `Hex` |
| `list` | `JulcList<X>` | `Array<X>` | `Array<XIn>` |
| `map` | `JulcMap<K, V>` (kept sorted: `SortedMaps`) | `Array<[K, V]>` | `Array<[KIn, VIn]>` |
| constructor (record) | a record | `{ "field": ... }` | the same, with `In` fields |
| sum (sealed interface) | sealed variants | a union of `{ $variant: "Name"; ... }` | the same, with `In` fields |
| `Bool` | `boolean` | `boolean` | `boolean` |
| `Optional` | `Optional<X>` | `X \| null` | `XIn \| null` |
| anything else (`Data`) | `PlutusData` | `DataHex` (hex CBOR) | `DataHex` |

These follow the [JSON conventions](https://joust.julc.dev/apps/javascript-clients/#json-conventions) the client encodes with. A `$variant`
is the variant's constructor title, for example `{ $variant: "Increment", by: 1n }`.

###### Methods

| Contract element | Generated |
|---|---|
| `@Init` | `C.deploy(wallet, args, pay?)`: `Promise<CallResult & { instance: CInstance }>` |
| `@Action`, `@Destroy` | `CInstance.<name>(wallet, args, pay?)`: `Promise<CallResult>` |
| `@Payable` | a required `pay: Pay` parameter |
| `@Quorum`, `@AuthorizedBy` | a further `opts?: { cosigners?: Cip30Api[]; governor?: { governor: { script, hash }; signers?: Cip30Api[] } }` |
| `@Batched` | the method submits an intent |
| owned types | creation methods returning `{ object: C<Type>Object }`, a lookup method, `objects()`, and a class `C<Type>Object` |

`args` is optional (`args?`) when the method takes no arguments and is not payable. For an owned type, `examples/bank`
gives:

```ts title="Bank.d.ts (excerpt)"
export declare class BankInstance {
  readonly id: Hex;
  read(): Promise<{ ref: string; state: BankState; lovelace: bigint } | null>;
  state(): Promise<BankState | null>;
  setPaused(wallet: Cip30Api, args: { "paused": boolean }): Promise<CallResult>;
  setLimit(wallet: Cip30Api, args: { "withdrawLimit": Int }): Promise<CallResult>;
  open(wallet: Cip30Api, args: Record<string, never>, pay: Pay): Promise<CallResult & { object: BankAccountObject }>;
  account(objectId: Hex): BankAccountObject;
  objects(): Promise<Array<{ id: Hex; type: string; value: unknown; lovelace: bigint }>>;
}
export declare class BankAccountObject {
  readonly id: Hex;
  read(): Promise<{ ref: string; type: string; value: BankAccount; lovelace: bigint } | null>;
  deposit(wallet: Cip30Api, args: Record<string, never>, pay: Pay): Promise<CallResult>;
  withdraw(wallet: Cip30Api, args: { "amount": Int }): Promise<CallResult>;
  close(wallet: Cip30Api, args?: Record<string, never>): Promise<CallResult>;
}
```

##### The packages' types

`@julclang/state-client` and `@julclang/joust-runtime` ship declarations (`src/index.d.ts`, the `types` of their main
export). The ones you use most:

| Type | Package | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `Int`, `Hex`, `DataHex` | state-client | `bigint \| number \| string`; hex strings |
| `Pay` | state-client | `{ lovelace?: Int; assets?: AssetsJson }` |
| `Cip30Api` | state-client | the CIP-30 calls the client uses |
| `JoustOptions` | state-client | `{ deployment, service, chain, limits?, onReview? }` |
| `CallResult`, `Report`, `Review` | state-client | a call's result, the verifier's report, what `onReview` gets |
| `Deployment` | both | a contract's deployment |
| `ChainProvider`, `ProviderUtxo`, `Chain` | state-client | a chain provider, its UTxO, the chain view |
| `VerificationError` | state-client | `problems: string[]; report: Report` |
| `JoustRuntime`, `Clock`, `BuiltContract`, `BuiltValidator`, `Governor`, `MapMirror`, `MirrorCache` | joust-runtime | the Node runtime and its parts |

##### Typing a page

Vite transpiles `.ts` files (it does not type-check them: run `tsc --noEmit` for that), so a page can be TypeScript:
rename `page/main.js` to `main.ts` and point `index.html` at it. The generated client's types come from `../build/joust/Counter.d.ts`. Two modules a page imports
ship no declarations yet: `virtual:joust/network` (from the Vite plugin) and `@julclang/joust-runtime/page`. Declare
them yourself, from their documented shapes:

```ts title="page/joust-env.d.ts"
declare module 'virtual:joust/network' {
  import type { Deployment } from '@julclang/state-client';
  const net: {
    network: string;
    networkId: number;
    chain: string;
    clock: { zeroSlot: number; zeroTimeMs: number; slotLengthMs: number };
    ttlMs: number;
    explorer: string | null;
    deployments: Record<string, Deployment>;
    contracts: unknown[];
    validators?: unknown[];
    engine: { url: string; integrity?: { script: string; wasm: string } };
  };
  export default net;
}

declare module '@julclang/joust-runtime/page' {
  import type { Service } from '@julclang/state-client';
  export function engineWorker(worker: Worker, options: object): Service & {
    ready: Promise<unknown>;
    mapValue(root: string, key: string, units?: string[]): Promise<string | null>;
    deployments(d: object): Promise<unknown>;
    terminate(): void;
  };
}
```

Then the page type-checks against the generated client:

```ts title="page/main.ts"
import { blockfrostChain, type Cip30Api } from '@julclang/state-client';
import { engineWorker } from '@julclang/joust-runtime/page';
import { Counter, type CounterState } from '../build/joust/Counter.js';
import net from 'virtual:joust/network';

const chain = blockfrostChain(new URL(net.chain, location.href).href);
const service = engineWorker(new Worker(new URL('./engine.worker.js', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' }), net);
const counter = new Counter({ service, chain, deployment: net.deployments['app.Counter'] });

export async function bump(wallet: Cip30Api, id: string): Promise<bigint | undefined> {
  const inst = counter.at(id);
  await inst.increment(wallet, { by: 1n });
  const s: CounterState | null = await inst.state();
  return s?.count;
}
```

> **Gaps in the shipped declarations:** 
The packages' `index.d.ts` files cover the main API but not every export: in `@julclang/state-client`, for example,
`runComposed`, `verifyComposed`, `walletView` and the address helpers are exported but not declared, and
`JoustInstance` lacks `intent`, `cancelIntent`, `batch`, `pendingIntents` and the `opts` of `call`. `Service`
declares a `view` method that `engineService` and `engineWorker` do not have (only `httpService` does), which is why
the declaration above types `engineWorker` as a `Service`. In `@julclang/joust-runtime`, `JoustRuntime` lacks
`compose`. The [reference pages](https://joust.julc.dev/reference/state-client/) list every
export with its signature from the source.

### Editors

URL: https://joust.julc.dev/languages/editors/

`.jsc` has a language server, `joust-lsp`. It ships in the `@julclang/joust` npm package and analyses each file with
the same front end the build uses, so its errors are the build's ([ADR-0021](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/docs/adr/0021-jsc-language-server-and-vscode-extension.md)).
What each editor gets:

| | VS Code | Neovim, Helix, other LSP clients |
|---|---|---|
| Diagnostics as you type, with stable `JSC` codes | ✓ | ✓ |
| Hover, go to definition, references (across files and into `java:` libraries), symbols, folding, selection ranges, semantic tokens | ✓ | ✓ |
| Completion, quick fixes, rename, Format Document | ✓ | — |
| The build on save (in memory: the processor's and JuLC's errors, the ABI comparison, the `joust.lock` check) | ✓, in a trusted project | — |
| `joust fmt` from the command line | ✓ | ✓ |

The editing features are VS Code's only. The server offers an edit only to a client known to reject one when the text
changed after the answer was computed (ADR-0021 D4a), and the extension is that client. Other editors get the
read-only features. There, format with `joust fmt <file>` from the shell, or from an editor hook that runs it on save.

The server never writes into your project. It runs advisory, with its own bundled compiler, unless the project's own
compiler matches it.

##### VS Code

Install the JOUST extension, `julc.vscode-joust`. It has its own version, apart from JOUST's: each version bundles the
compiler of one JOUST release, and each JOUST release that publishes the extension bumps its patch. Its
[changelog](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/js/vscode-joust/CHANGELOG.md) names the JOUST release each
version bundles. It is published as a pre-release while JOUST is one, so pick one of these:

- **From the Visual Studio Marketplace.** In the Extensions view, search for `julc.vscode-joust` and install it
  (choose the pre-release version if VS Code offers both). Or from a terminal:

  ```sh
  code --install-extension julc.vscode-joust --pre-release
  ```

- **From a JOUST release on GitHub.** [Releases](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/releases) that include the
  extension list `vscode-joust-<ext>.vsix` among their assets (the release notes alone are no sign: look at the asset
  list). Optionally check that the release's own workflow built it from the release's tag (this needs the
  [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/)), then install it:

  ```sh
  gh attestation verify vscode-joust-<ext>.vsix -R bloxbean/joust \
    --signer-workflow bloxbean/joust/.github/workflows/editor-assets.yml \
    --source-ref refs/tags/v<joust-version>
  code --install-extension vscode-joust-<ext>.vsix
  ```

  If a maintainer attached the release's assets by hand, the check passes with `--source-ref refs/heads/main` instead.
  If neither passes, don't install the file.

  VSCodium and other editors that use Open VSX can install the `.vsix` the same way.

The extension bundles the server and its compiler, and it honours Workspace Trust:
- In Restricted Mode, it analyses with the bundled compiler and runs nothing from the workspace.
- In a trusted folder, it may use the project's own compiler: only that compiler's two engine files, after checking them.

Rename goes through **JOUST: Rename Symbol**. It renames locals, parameters, `fn`s, types, enums, variants, fields, state
fields, actions, destroys, views, events and owned types. Renaming an owned type also renames its methods' and invariants' qualifiers and its `admits`. A
field renamed in an owned type is renamed where the object is read: in its methods' bodies and modifiers, and in
`keyed by` for a keyed type's key. A params field is also renamed in `init migrate from params.f`. Owned methods, the
purposes' handlers and `init migrate` cannot be renamed: the rename refuses them. **JOUST: Show generated Java** opens the lowered class, and **Accept ABI…**
reviews a changed ABI manifest before accepting it. Format Document, and format on save if you turn it on, use the same
formatter as `joust fmt`. The formatting style belongs to the compiler's version (version 1 today). When the extension
analyses with its bundled compiler (advisory), it formats with that one too, so a project pinned to another JOUST version
may format differently in CI.

> **How the extension is published:** 
Each JOUST release builds the `.vsix` from its tag, with the compiler engine of the `@julclang/joust` package that npm
serves for that version, and attaches it to the GitHub release with its SHA-256 and a provenance attestation. The
Marketplace listing is that same file, published unchanged after a maintainer approves. An Open VSX listing is not
there yet.

##### Other editors: a server you installed

Editors other than VS Code have no workspace trust, so JOUST's configurations start **a `joust-lsp` you installed
yourself, by absolute path**. A repository you open never chooses the program that runs. Install a pinned version
globally and note the path:

```sh
npm install -g @julclang/joust@<version>
echo "$(npm prefix -g)/bin/joust-lsp"
```

`npx joust` is never used for an editor: it would run whatever version a project or the registry resolves.

###### Neovim (0.11 or later)

Put JOUST's module, [`editors/neovim/lua/joust.lua`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/editors/neovim/lua/joust.lua),
on your `runtimepath` (for example in `~/.config/nvim/lua/`), then in your `init.lua`:

```lua
require('joust').setup({ path = '/absolute/path/to/joust-lsp' })
```

The module checks the path, sets the `jsc` filetype and configures the server through `vim.lsp.config`. It refuses:
- a bare name or a relative path;
- `npx`;
- a project's `node_modules/.bin`;
- a server, or `node`, inside the project of the buffer you open. The project is the one JOUST's markers find:
  `joust.config.json`, `package.json` or `settings.gradle`, never your home directory itself. An install under your
  home directory (nvm, volta, asdf, an npm prefix of `~/.npm-global`) is your own, wherever Neovim is started.

The server runs on an absolute `node`. By default that is the first `node` on an absolute `PATH` entry; a relative entry
such as `./node_modules/.bin` is never used, since it would let a project choose the interpreter. On Windows, give
`node` explicitly; the module does not search `PATH` there. Elsewhere you can give it too:

```lua
require('joust').setup({ path = '/absolute/path/to/joust-lsp', node = '/absolute/path/to/node' })
```

With the tree-sitter package installed (below), it also starts tree-sitter highlighting and folding for `.jsc` buffers.

###### Helix

Add JOUST's [`editors/helix/languages.toml`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/editors/helix/languages.toml)
to `~/.config/helix/languages.toml` and replace its placeholders. The command is `node` itself, by absolute path. Helix
starts servers from the project, so a bare name could find a project's `node` through a relative `PATH` entry:

```toml
[language-server.joust]
command = "/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/node"
args = ["/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/joust-lsp", "--stdio"]

[[language]]
name = "jsc"
scope = "source.jsc"
file-types = ["jsc"]
roots = ["joust.config.json", "package.json", "settings.gradle", "settings.gradle.kts"]
comment-token = "//"
block-comment-tokens = { start = "/*", end = "*/" }
indent = { tab-width = 2, unit = "  " }
language-servers = ["joust"]
grammar = "jsc"

[[grammar]]
name = "jsc"
source = { path = "/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/tree-sitter-jsc" }
```

Then build the grammar, copy its queries and check the setup:

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.config/helix/runtime/grammars ~/.config/helix/runtime/queries
hx --grammar build
cp -R /ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/tree-sitter-jsc/helix/queries/jsc ~/.config/helix/runtime/queries/
hx --health jsc
```

:::caution[A project's Helix configuration]
Helix also reads a project's own `.helix/languages.toml`, and that file can redefine any language server's command.
JOUST cannot restrict that. Before you open a repository you do not trust in Helix, look for a `.helix/` directory.
:::

###### Any other LSP client

Start `/absolute/path/to/node /absolute/path/to/joust-lsp --stdio` for files ending in `.jsc`. Use the project root, the directory holding
`joust.config.json` or `package.json`, as its workspace folder.

###### The project's own server and compiler

Two variants run code from the repository you open. Use them only for repositories you trust:

:::caution[Runs the repository's code]
A project-local server runs the repository's whole `@julclang/joust` package:

```sh
./node_modules/.bin/joust-lsp --stdio
```

`--project-engine` makes a user-installed server load each project's own compiler engine. It reads only the engine's
two files, confined to the workspace folder, but it runs that engine's JavaScript for **every** repository you open,
because these editors have no workspace trust:

```sh
/absolute/path/to/joust-lsp --stdio --project-engine
```
:::

##### The tree-sitter grammar

Highlighting and folding in Neovim and Helix come from `tree-sitter-jsc`. Releases that include it list
`tree-sitter-jsc-<version>.tar.gz` among their assets, with its SHA-256 in the release's
`editor-assets-<joust-version>-SHA256SUMS.txt` and a provenance attestation. Download it, optionally check it, and
unpack it where you keep editor plugins:

```sh
gh release download v<joust-version> -R bloxbean/joust --pattern 'tree-sitter-jsc-*.tar.gz'
gh attestation verify tree-sitter-jsc-<version>.tar.gz -R bloxbean/joust \
  --signer-workflow bloxbean/joust/.github/workflows/editor-assets.yml \
  --source-ref refs/tags/v<joust-version>
mkdir -p ~/.local/share
tar xzf tree-sitter-jsc-<version>.tar.gz -C ~/.local/share
cd ~/.local/share/tree-sitter-jsc-<version>
```

As for the `.vsix`, assets a maintainer attached by hand pass with `--source-ref refs/heads/main` instead. That
directory is the `/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/tree-sitter-jsc` the Helix configuration above names. The archive holds:
- the grammar and the generated parser (`src/`);
- the queries (`queries/`, and `neovim/queries/jsc/`);
- Helix's highlights, with Helix's capture names (`helix/queries/jsc/`);
- `EDITORS.md`, the steps above in short.

For Neovim, build the parser into your runtimepath, from that directory:

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.local/share/nvim/site/parser ~/.local/share/nvim/site/queries
cc -O2 -shared -fPIC -Isrc src/parser.c src/scanner.c -o ~/.local/share/nvim/site/parser/jsc.so
cp -R neovim/queries/jsc ~/.local/share/nvim/site/queries/
```

To build the package from a checkout instead:

```sh
cd tree-sitter-jsc
npm ci
npm run package     # dist/tree-sitter-jsc-<version>.tar.gz
```

## Reference: Java

### Annotations

URL: https://joust.julc.dev/reference/annotations/

This page lists every annotation in `julc-state-api` (package `org.julclang.state.api`), grouped by what it is for.
For each one you get its target, its elements with their types and defaults, the method shape the processor accepts,
what the generated validator checks on chain, and a line from a real example. The source of each annotation is in
[`julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api);
the rules quoted below come from the processor's
[`ContractReader`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-processor/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/processor/ContractReader.java),
which reports each one as a compile error.

All annotations have `CLASS` retention: they exist for the annotation processor and are not read at run time.

##### At a glance

| Annotation | Target | Elements | Group |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`@StateContract`](#statecontract) | class | `minAda`, `maxDatumBytes`, `maxValidityMs`, `assetSlots`, `stakeSelf` | Contract |
| [`@Params`](#params) | record | none | Contract |
| [`@Init`](#init) | method | none | Lifecycle |
| [`@Action`](#action) | method | none | Lifecycle |
| [`@Destroy`](#destroy) | method | none | Lifecycle |
| [`@View`](#view) | method | none | Lifecycle |
| [`@SignedBy`](#signedby) | method | `value` | Authorization |
| [`@OnlyOwner`](#onlyowner) | method | none | Authorization |
| [`@Quorum`](#quorum) | method | `keys`, `threshold` | Authorization |
| [`@AuthorizedBy`](#authorizedby) | method | `value` | Authorization |
| [`@ValidAfter`](#validafter) | method | `value` | Time |
| [`@ValidBefore`](#validbefore) | method | `value` | Time |
| [`@Payable`](#payable) | method | none | Funds |
| [`@Receives`](#receives) | method | none | Funds |
| [`@Owned`](#owned) | record | `key`, `maxKeyBytes`, `signedKey`, `linkCooldownMs`, `linkWindowMs` (keyed types) | Owned objects |
| [`@OwnedInit`](#ownedinit) | method | none | Owned objects |
| [`@OwnedAction`](#ownedaction) | method | none | Owned objects |
| [`@OwnedDestroy`](#owneddestroy) | method | `retire` (keyed types) | Owned objects |
| [`@Shared`](#shared) | parameter | none | Owned objects |
| [`@Into`](#into) | parameter | none | Owned objects |
| [`@Admits`](#admits) | method | `value` | Owned objects |
| [`@Batched`](#batched) | method | `only` | Batching |
| [`@Reads`](#reads) | parameter | `value` | Composition and reads |
| [`@Withdraw`](#withdraw) | method | none | Purposes and governance |
| [`@Certify`](#certify) | method | none | Purposes and governance |
| [`@Votes`](#votes) | method | none | Purposes and governance |
| [`@Propose`](#propose) | method | none | Purposes and governance |
| [`@MigrateTo`](#migrateto) | method | `value` | Upgrades |
| [`@Migrate`](#migrate) | method | `from` | Upgrades |
| [`@Invariant`](#invariant) | method | none | Invariants |

> **Note:** 
Events are not an annotation. A method emits them by returning a result record with an `events` component
(see [Result records](#result-records)). Several names in the
[annotation catalogue](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/docs/research/annotation-catalog.md) (`@State`,
`@Param`, `@Event`, `@Upgradeable`, `@Calls`, `@Storage`, `@Anonymous`, `@MultiSig`) are proposals that did not ship
under those names; they are not in `julc-state-api`. The `@Param` you may see on a plain JuLC validator (such as
`examples/treasury/.../Guardian.java`) is JuLC's own annotation, not JOUST's.

##### Method kinds and parameter order

Every contract method carries exactly one kind annotation: `@Init`, `@Action`, `@Destroy`, `@View`, `@OwnedInit`,
`@OwnedAction`, `@OwnedDestroy`, `@Migrate`, `@Invariant` or one purpose handler (`@Withdraw`, `@Certify`, `@Votes`,
`@Propose`). Policy annotations (`@Payable`, `@SignedBy`, `@OnlyOwner`, `@ValidAfter`, `@ValidBefore`, `@Batched`,
`@Quorum`, `@AuthorizedBy`, `@Admits`, `@Receives`) need a kind annotation on the same method.

The processor enforces these rules on every kind:

- Contract methods are `public static`, not generic, and have unique names (no overloading).
- A method name cannot be a member of the generated client: `deploy`, `at`, `contract`, `state`, `instance`,
  `instanceId`, `lovelace`, `fullValue`, `SPEC`, `params`, `policyIdFor`, `checkedState`, `checkedObject` (and, for
  `@Batched` contracts, `INTENTS`, `batch`, `pendingIntents`, `intent`).
- Parameter names `callerAccount`, `payLovelace`, `payAssets`, `runtime`, `params`, `authorization`, `cosigners`,
  `ctx` and `maps` are reserved; `@Init` also reserves `seed` and `instance`.
- A `MerkleMap` or `MapEntry` can only be a component of the state (or owned) record, never an argument.

Parameters come in this order (each part optional unless the kind requires it):

```java
name(State s | Owned o,            // not in creations
     @Shared State shared,          // owned methods only
     @Into State destination,       // a move (@OwnedAction) only
     Config cfg,                    // the @Params record
     @Reads("params.x") Other.State x, ...,
     args...,
     Ctx ctx,                       // last, or last before Funds
     Funds funds)                   // always last
```

##### Contract

###### @StateContract

Marks a class as a JOUST state contract. The processor generates `<Name>Validator` (a JuLC `@MultiValidator`) and
`<Name>Client` in the same package. JuLC treats it exactly like its own `@OnchainLibrary` (a fixed alias,
bloxbean/julc#311), so JuLC compiles the class for on-chain use without a second annotation.

**Target:** a public top-level class. **Source:**
[`StateContract.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/StateContract.java)

| Element | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minAda` | `long` | `0` | Lovelace locked in the state UTxO as its min-ADA deposit, on top of the contract's funds. `0` derives it (below). An explicit value below the derived one is a compile error |
| `maxDatumBytes` | `int` | `512` | Largest serialised state the validator accepts; a transition that grows the datum past it is rejected, so no call can push the UTxO beyond what `minAda` covers. Must be 16 to 8192 |
| `maxValidityMs` | `long` | `3_600_000` | Widest validity interval (`validTo - validFrom`, POSIX ms) a call that reads `Ctx` may use. At least 60000 |
| `assetSlots` | `int` | `-1` | Native assets a state or object UTxO is expected to hold, for the deposit (about 80 bytes each). `-1` means 4 for contracts that handle native assets, 0 otherwise. Must end up 0 to 64 |
| `stakeSelf` | `boolean` | `false` | Stake the state UTxOs to this script (base addresses). Requires a `@Withdraw` and a `@Certify` handler |

The derived deposit is `4310 * (160 + 200 + maxDatumBytes + 80 * assetSlots)` lovelace, rounded up to 0.1 ADA
(`stakeSelf` counts as one more slot, for the longer base address). With the defaults that is 3.8 ADA.

The processor also requires exactly one `@Init`, and warns when a contract without owned objects has no `@Destroy`
(its deposit would be locked forever).

```java title="examples/dex/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/dex/Dex.java"
@StateContract(maxDatumBytes = 256, assetSlots = 2)
public class Dex {
```

Guides: [State and lifecycle](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/state-and-lifecycle/), [Fees and script size](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/fees-and-size/).

###### @Params

Marks the record of a contract's deploy-time parameters (ADR-0009 D1). They are applied to the script (JuLC partial
application), so each parameter set has its own policy id and address. A method receives them by declaring a
parameter of this type right after the state (or after `@Shared`; first in `@Init`).

**Target:** a record nested in the contract. **Elements:** none. **Source:**
[`Params.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Params.java)

Rules: at most one `@Params` record per contract; it cannot hold MerkleMaps. Other annotations name its fields as
`"params.field"` (`@Quorum`, `@AuthorizedBy`, `@Reads`, `@Migrate`, `@MigrateTo`). Purpose handlers take it as their
first parameter.

```java title="examples/treasury/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/treasury/Treasury.java"
@Params
public record Config(Credential guardian, BigInteger maxPayout) {}
```

Guide: [Params, invariants and events](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/params-invariants-events/).

##### Lifecycle

###### @Init

The constructor: `public static S init(args... [, Ctx])`. Exactly one per contract. Deploying an instance mints its
one-shot thread token and the validator checks the initial datum equals this method's result.

**Target:** method. **Elements:** none. **Source:**
[`Init.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Init.java)

- Returns the state record, or a result record with `state` and optionally `accepted` (an init cannot pay out, send,
  mint or deposit, and cannot emit events yet).
- Takes the `@Params` record first if the contract has one.
- `@SignedBy`, `@OnlyOwner`, `@ValidAfter`, `@ValidBefore`, `@Quorum` and `@AuthorizedBy` are rejected: they check the
  current state, which a creation does not have. Use `Ctx` and `Require.that` in the body.

```java title="examples/counter/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/counter/Counter.java"
@Init
public static State init(Ctx ctx) {
    return new State(BigInteger.ZERO, ctx.caller());
}
```

###### @Action

A state transition: `public static S name(S state, args... [, Ctx])`, or a result record with a `state` component and
any of `payouts`, `sends`, `deposits`, `mint`, `accepted`, `events`.

**Target:** method. **Elements:** none. **Source:**
[`Action.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Action.java)

The validator re-runs the method and requires exactly one continuing output with the thread token at the same address,
an inline datum equal to the result, and an exact value: what the UTxO held, plus what the call receives, minus what
it pays out. An action without `Ctx` needs no signature and is cheaper.

```java title="examples/counter/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/counter/Counter.java"
@Action
public static State increment(State s, BigInteger by) {
```

###### @Destroy

Ends the instance: `public static JulcList<Payout> name(S state, args..., Ctx)`, or a result record with any of
`payouts`, `sends`, `deposits`, `mint`, `accepted` and no `state`. The thread token is burned and the payouts must
allocate the contract's whole balance (`ctx.balance()`, deposit included).

**Target:** method. **Elements:** none. **Source:**
[`Destroy.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Destroy.java)

- Needs a `Ctx` parameter.
- A contract with `@Owned` objects cannot have a `@Destroy` (objects that read `@Shared` state would be locked).
- With MerkleMaps, the processor warns that a destroy discards the maps' contents: check `MerkleMaps.isEmpty(...)`.

```java title="examples/counter/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/counter/Counter.java"
@Destroy
@OnlyOwner
public static JulcList<Payout> close(State s, Ctx ctx) {
    return Payouts.of(s.owner(), ctx.balance());
}
```

###### @View

A read-only query, `public static T name(S state, args...)`. Runs off chain only: no transaction, no validator code.

**Target:** method. **Elements:** none. **Source:**
[`View.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/View.java)

The first parameter must be the state; the method must return a value and cannot take `Ctx`.

```java title="examples/token/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/token/Token.java"
@View
public static BigInteger balanceOf(State s, byte[] holder) {
```

Guide: [State and lifecycle](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/state-and-lifecycle/).

###### Result records

A method that does more than change state returns a record whose component names say what each part is. The processor
accepts only these names:

| Component | Type | Allowed in | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | the state (or owned) record | actions, creations (required in actions); never in destroys | The next state |
| `payouts` | `JulcList<Payout>` | actions, destroys | Lovelace to key hashes |
| `sends` | `JulcList<Send>` | actions, destroys | Outputs to any address with any datum, claimed in the output registry (ADR-0007) |
| `deposits` | `JulcList<Deposit>` | actions, destroys | Payments into another JOUST instance's `@Receives` action (ADR-0011 D3) |
| `mint` | `Value` | actions, destroys | Tokens minted (positive) or burned (negative) under the contract's own policy |
| `accepted` | `Value` | `@Payable` methods with `Funds` | Exactly the native assets the call takes in (required there) |
| `events` | `JulcList` of event records | not creations, not `@Batched` | Authenticated events, carried in the redeemer and checked equal (ADR-0009 D5) |

A destroy's record needs at least one of `payouts`, `sends`, `mint`, `deposits`.

```java title="examples/treasury/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/treasury/Treasury.java"
public record Spent(State state, JulcList<Payout> payouts, JulcList<Event> events) {}
```

##### Authorization

###### @SignedBy

The transaction must be signed by the key hash (`byte[]`) held in the named field of the current state (for owned
methods, of the owned record).

**Target:** method. **Source:**
[`SignedBy.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/SignedBy.java)

| Element | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `String` | required | Name of a `byte[]` component of the state record |

Not allowed on `@Init` or `@Batched` actions. The processor warns when an owned method has no `@SignedBy` (anyone could
call it on anyone's object).

```java title="examples/token/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/token/Token.java"
@Action
@SignedBy("admin")
public static State mint(State s, byte[] to, BigInteger amount) {
```

###### @OnlyOwner

Shorthand for `@SignedBy("owner")`: the state needs a `byte[] owner` component.

**Target:** method. **Elements:** none. **Source:**
[`OnlyOwner.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/OnlyOwner.java)

```java title="examples/vault/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/vault/Vault.java"
@Action @OnlyOwner @ValidAfter("unlockAt")
```

###### @Quorum

M-of-N signatures (ADR-0009 D2): at least `threshold` (and at least one) of the transaction's signatories are among
`keys`.

**Target:** method. **Source:**
[`Quorum.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Quorum.java)

| Element | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `keys` | `String` | required | A `JulcList<byte[]>` field of key hashes: of the state, the owned record, or `"params.x"` |
| `threshold` | `String` | required | A `BigInteger` field: of the state, the owned record, or `"params.x"` |

The generated check also requires distinct, strictly ascending 28-byte keys. Not allowed in creations or on `@Batched`
actions. Purpose handlers must name `params.*` fields.

```java title="examples/treasury/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/treasury/Treasury.java"
@Action @Quorum(keys = "council", threshold = "quorum")
public static Spent pay(State s, Config cfg, byte[] to, BigInteger amount, Ctx ctx) {
```

###### @AuthorizedBy

The method needs the approval of a credential (ADR-0009 D3), named by a `Credential` field of the state, the owned
record, or the `@Params` record (`"params.field"`). A key credential must sign. A script credential must run in the
transaction for a zero withdrawal (the withdraw-zero pattern) and approves by its own rules; a JOUST-aware governor
lists its approvals in an [`Approvals`](https://joust.julc.dev/reference/state-api/#approvals-and-approval) redeemer.

**Target:** method. **Source:**
[`AuthorizedBy.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/AuthorizedBy.java)

| Element | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `String` | required | A `Credential` field: `"field"` or `"params.field"` |

Not allowed in creations or on `@Batched` actions.

```java title="examples/treasury/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/treasury/Treasury.java"
@Action @AuthorizedBy("params.guardian")
public static Changed freeze(State s, boolean frozen) {
```

Guide: [Authorization](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/authorization/). Tutorial: [Multisig treasury](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/multisig-treasury/).

##### Time

###### @ValidAfter

The transaction's validity interval must start at or after the time (POSIX ms) held in the named `BigInteger` field
of the current state. The client sets the interval for you.

**Target:** method. **Source:**
[`ValidAfter.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/ValidAfter.java)

| Element | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `String` | required | Name of a `BigInteger` component of the state record |

```java title="examples/vault/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/vault/Vault.java"
@Destroy @OnlyOwner @ValidAfter("unlockAt")
```

###### @ValidBefore

The transaction's validity interval must end at or before the time held in the named `BigInteger` field of the
current state.

**Target:** method. **Source:**
[`ValidBefore.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/ValidBefore.java)

| Element | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `String` | required | Name of a `BigInteger` component of the state record |

```java
@Action @ValidBefore("deadline")
```

Both are rejected on `@Init` (no current state) and on `@Batched` actions (the batcher picks the interval). In those,
check time in the body with [`Clock`](https://joust.julc.dev/reference/state-api/#clock). Guide: [Time](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/time/).

##### Funds

###### @Payable

The `@Init` or `@Action` (or owned creation or action) may receive lovelace: `ctx.received() > 0`. Without it,
`received` must be zero. With a `Funds` parameter it may also take native assets, and must then return a result record
with `accepted`, exactly the native assets it takes.

**Target:** method. **Elements:** none. **Source:**
[`Payable.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Payable.java)

Needs a `Ctx` parameter.

```java title="examples/staking/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/staking/StakedVault.java"
@Action @Payable
public static State deposit(State s, Ctx ctx) {
```

Guide: [Ctx, funds and payouts](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/ctx-and-funds/).

###### @Receives

An action that takes deposits from other JOUST contracts in the same transaction (ADR-0011 D3). Its value equation
adds every deposit claimed on its continuing output, and the method sees them in `funds.deposits()`. An action without
it takes no deposits: its exact value check fails if anyone adds value to its output.

**Target:** method. **Elements:** none. **Source:**
[`Receives.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Receives.java)

Rules: only on an `@Action` or `@OwnedAction`; needs a `Funds` parameter; cannot be `@Batched`.

```java title="examples/fees/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/fees/Pot.java"
@Receives
public static State collect(State s, Ctx ctx, Funds funds) {
    BigInteger got = Deposits.lovelace(funds.deposits());
```

Guide: [Deposits](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/deposits/).

##### Owned objects

Owned objects (ADR-0003, ADR-0012) are records that live in their own UTxOs under an instance, so different objects
never contend. Guide: [Owned objects](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/owned-objects/). Tutorial:
[Bank: owned objects](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/bank-owned-objects/).

###### @Owned

Marks a record of the contract as an owned type. Each object is its own UTxO, touched only by owned methods.

**Target:** a record nested in the contract. **Elements:** none for a plain owned type; the keyed elements below
make it a keyed type. **Source:**
[`Owned.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Owned.java)

- A contract may have several owned types since ADR-0012 D1 (the Javadoc's "at most one" predates it); each gets its
  own datum variant `Holding_<Type>`, a single type keeps `Holding`.
- Each owned type needs at least one `@OwnedInit`, and an `@OwnedDestroy` without `@Shared` (an escape hatch that works
  whatever the instance state).
- MerkleMaps may be direct components of an owned record (ADR-0012 D2), but not of the instance state of a contract
  with owned objects.
- A contract with owned objects cannot `@Destroy` its instance.

```java title="examples/bank/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/bank/Bank.java"
@Owned
public record Account(byte[] owner, BigInteger balance) {}
```

**Keyed types** (ADR-0016). Naming a `byte[]`
component as `key` makes the type keyed: at most one object per key and instance, in a sorted on-chain list. Guide:
[Keyed objects](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/keyed-objects/).

| Element | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | `""` | The `byte[]` component that keys the object; empty for a plain owned type |
| `maxKeyBytes` | 32 | Longest key: 1 to 64 bytes |
| `signedKey` | `false` | The key is a 28-byte key hash that must sign the insert |
| `linkCooldownMs` | 60,000 | Least time between two relinks of a node: 0 (written explicitly) or 60,000 to 3,600,000 |
| `linkWindowMs` | -1, meaning `min(120,000, maxValidityMs)` | Widest validity window of a relink: 20,000 to `min(900,000, maxValidityMs)` |

A keyed type needs an `@OwnedDestroy(retire = true)` signed with `@SignedBy`, and every keyed `@OwnedAction` must carry
`@SignedBy`, `@Quorum` or `@AuthorizedBy`. Setting a keyed element on a type without `key` is an error.

```java title="examples/registry/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/registry/Registry.java"
@Owned(key = "voter", maxKeyBytes = 28, signedKey = true)
public record Ballot(byte[] voter, BigInteger choice) {}
```

###### @OwnedInit

Creates an owned object: `public static R name([@Shared S shared,] args... [, Ctx])`. The object belongs to the
instance it is created under. Returns the owned record (or a record with a `state` of it).

**Target:** method. **Elements:** none. **Source:**
[`OwnedInit.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/OwnedInit.java)

```java title="examples/bank/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/bank/Bank.java"
@OwnedInit
@Payable
public static Account open(@Shared State bank, Ctx ctx) {
```

###### @OwnedAction

Changes one owned object: `public static R name(R object, [@Shared S shared,] args... [, Ctx])`, or a result record
with `state` (the owned record) and effects. Spends only the object's UTxO.

**Target:** method. **Elements:** none. **Source:**
[`OwnedAction.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/OwnedAction.java)

```java title="examples/bank/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/bank/Bank.java"
@OwnedAction
@SignedBy("owner")
public static Withdrawal withdraw(Account a, @Shared State bank, BigInteger amount, Ctx ctx) {
```

###### @OwnedDestroy

Ends an owned object: `public static JulcList<Payout> name(R object, [@Shared S shared,] args..., Ctx)`. Burns its
token; the payouts must allocate everything it holds. The processor warns if the object has MerkleMaps (they are
discarded).

**Target:** method. **Elements:** `retire` (default `false`). **Source:**
[`OwnedDestroy.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/OwnedDestroy.java)

```java title="examples/bank/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/bank/Bank.java"
@OwnedDestroy
@SignedBy("owner")
public static JulcList<Payout> close(Account a, Ctx ctx) {
```

On a [keyed type](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/keyed-objects/), a plain `@OwnedDestroy` *removes* the object and frees its key, and
`@OwnedDestroy(retire = true)` *retires* it: the object stays as a retired node with its deposit and its key, taken for
good, and the payouts allocate exactly `ctx.balance()` (everything but the deposit). A retiring exit cannot take
`@Shared`, `@Reads`, `@Payable`, `@Quorum`, `@AuthorizedBy`, `@ValidAfter` or `@ValidBefore`.

```java title="examples/registry/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/registry/Registry.java"
@OwnedDestroy(retire = true)
@SignedBy("owner")
public static JulcList<Payout> retire(Entry e, Ctx ctx) {
```

###### @Shared

Gives an owned method the instance's state, read-only, through a reference input: the instance is not spent, so it
causes no contention (ADR-0003 D1).

**Target:** parameter. **Elements:** none. **Source:**
[`Shared.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Shared.java)

Rules: only on owned methods; the parameter's type must be the state record; it comes right after the owned record (first
in an `@OwnedInit`).

```java title="examples/bank/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/bank/Bank.java"
public static Account open(@Shared State bank, Ctx ctx) {
```

###### @Into

Marks the destination of a move (ADR-0012 D3): an `@OwnedAction` parameter of the state type, after the `@Shared`
source if any. The object moves to that instance, which is spent in the same transaction by an `@Admits` action naming
the object. The method gets the destination's state as it was before. The redeemer carries the destination's id, and
both validators check each other's redeemer (I43).

**Target:** parameter. **Elements:** none. **Source:**
[`Into.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Into.java)

Rules: only on `@OwnedAction`; a move returns the owned record (or a record with its `state`); it cannot take `@Reads`;
an `@Into` move needs an `@Admits` action for its type. Moves run only inside `Compose`.

```java title="examples/guild/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/guild/Guild.java"
@OwnedAction
@SignedBy("owner")
public static Hero transfer(Hero h, @Shared State source, @Into State destination, Ctx ctx) {
```

###### @Admits

An `@Action` through which an instance admits an object moving in from another instance of the same contract
(ADR-0012 D3). Its first argument after the state (and the params) is the object's id (`byte[]`). The validator
requires that object to be spent in the same transaction with a move naming this instance; the method decides whether
to admit it and may update the instance's state.

**Target:** method. **Source:**
[`Admits.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Admits.java)

| Element | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `String` | `""` | The owned record it admits (`"Hero"`). Required when more than one owned type has moves |

Rules: only on an instance `@Action`; cannot be `@Batched` or take `@Reads`; the contract needs an `@Owned` record and
an `@Into` move.

```java title="examples/guild/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/guild/Guild.java"
@Admits("Hero")
public static State admit(State s, byte[] heroId, Hero hero, Ctx ctx) {
```

##### Batching

###### @Batched

The `@Action` may also run as an intent (ADR-0004): a user locks a request in their own UTxO, and a batcher applies
many requests to the instance in one transaction, so concurrent writers do not contend.

**Target:** method. **Source:**
[`Batched.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Batched.java)

| Element | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `only` | `boolean` | `false` | Only as an intent: no direct call, so nobody can invalidate pending batches by spending the instance directly |

In a batch, `ctx.caller()` is the intent's owner, `ctx.received()` the amount the intent carries, `ctx.balance()` the
balance at that point of the fold, and `validFrom`/`validTo` the batch transaction's bounds. An intent runs against
whatever state the batch finds: take a bound (a minimum out, a maximum price) as an argument and check it.

Rules: only on `@Action`; needs `Ctx`; cannot use `@SignedBy`, `@OnlyOwner`, `@ValidAfter`, `@ValidBefore`, `@Quorum`,
`@AuthorizedBy`, events, the `@Params` record, `@Reads`, `Funds`, sends, mints or deposits. A contract with `@Batched`
actions cannot also have MerkleMap state, native assets or `@Invariant`s yet.

```java title="examples/pool/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/pool/Pool.java"
@Action
@Batched(only = true)
@Payable
public static Sale buy(State s, BigInteger maxPrice, Ctx ctx) {
```

Guide: [Batched intents](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/batched-intents/). Tutorial: [Pool: batched intents](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/pool-batched-intents/).

##### Composition and reads

###### @Reads

A method parameter that reads another JOUST contract's instance state through a reference input (ADR-0011 D2). The
validator checks the token kind, the single token, the script address and the inline datum's shape before decoding.

**Target:** parameter. **Source:**
[`Reads.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Reads.java)

| Element | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `String` | required | `"params.x"`, naming a [`ForeignInstance`](https://joust.julc.dev/reference/state-api/#foreigninstance) component of the `@Params` record |

Rules: the parameter's type is the other contract's state record; `@Reads` parameters come right after the `@Params`
record; the read state cannot hold MerkleMaps; not supported in creations, moves or `@Admits` actions yet. Freshness is
the reading contract's job (check a timestamp in the read state).

```java title="examples/oracle/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/oracle/Shop.java"
public static State buy(State s, Config cfg, @Reads("params.oracle") Oracle.State price, BigInteger qty, Ctx ctx) {
```

Guide: [Reads and composition](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/reads-and-composition/). Tutorial:
[Oracle and composition](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/oracle-composition/).

##### Purposes and governance

Purpose handlers (ADR-0010 D1) answer the ledger's other script purposes for the contract's own credential. They are
`public static`, take the `@Params` record first, are governed by `@Quorum` or `@AuthorizedBy` over `params.*` fields
(except `@Propose`), and cannot carry a lifecycle annotation. At most one handler per purpose. Contracts with `@Votes`
or `@Propose` handlers need `-Ajulc.blueprint=false` (a CIP-57 vocabulary gap in JuLC).

Guide: [Staking and governance](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/staking-and-governance/). Tutorial:
[Staked vault and governance](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/staked-vault/).

###### @Withdraw

Handles withdrawals of the contract's staking rewards: `(Params cfg, BigInteger amount, args..., [Ctx])` returning
`JulcList<Send>` totalling exactly `amount`, claimed in the output registry.

**Target:** method. **Elements:** none. **Source:**
[`Withdraw.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Withdraw.java)

```java title="examples/staking/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/staking/StakedVault.java"
@Withdraw @Quorum(keys = "params.council", threshold = "params.quorum")
public static JulcList<Send> collect(Config cfg, BigInteger amount) {
```

###### @Certify

Decides which certificates of the contract's credential are allowed: `(Params cfg, TxCert cert)` returning `boolean`.
Unregistration, committee and pool certificates are refused before it runs. Use the [`Certs`](https://joust.julc.dev/reference/state-api/#certs)
helpers for exact checks.

**Target:** method. **Elements:** none. **Source:**
[`Certify.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Certify.java)

```java title="examples/staking/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/staking/StakedVault.java"
@Certify @Quorum(keys = "params.council", threshold = "params.quorum")
public static boolean certificate(Config cfg, TxCert cert) {
```

###### @Votes

Decides the contract's votes as a DRep or committee member: `(Params cfg, Voter voter, GovernanceActionId action, Vote
vote)` returning `boolean`, called for every vote it casts.

**Target:** method. **Elements:** none. **Source:**
[`Votes.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Votes.java)

```java title="examples/staking/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/staking/StakedVault.java"
@Votes @Quorum(keys = "params.council", threshold = "params.quorum")
public static boolean vote(Config cfg, Voter voter, GovernanceActionId action, Vote vote) {
```

###### @Propose

A constitution guardrail: `(Params cfg, ProposalProcedure p)` returning `boolean`. The ledger runs it for
parameter-change and treasury-withdrawal proposals once a constitution names this script.

**Target:** method. **Elements:** none. **Source:**
[`Propose.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Propose.java)

```java title="examples/staking/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/staking/StakedVault.java"
@Propose
public static boolean proposal(Config cfg, ProposalProcedure p) {
```

##### Upgrades

Version migration (ADR-0011 D4) moves an instance's state and funds from one contract to its successor in one composed
transaction. Neither annotation is supported yet with MerkleMaps, owned objects or native assets. Guide:
[Upgrades and migration](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/upgrades/). Tutorial: [Upgrading a contract](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/upgrades/).

###### @MigrateTo

On a `@Destroy`: the instance migrates to its successor. The validator requires that the successor mints the instance
id `blake2b_256(own input)`, and that its output holds at least everything this instance holds, less the payouts.

**Target:** method (an instance `@Destroy`). **Source:**
[`MigrateTo.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/MigrateTo.java)

| Element | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `String` | required | A `byte[]` field holding the successor's policy: a state field an admin sets, or `"params.x"` |

```java title="examples/upgrade/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/upgrade/CounterV1.java"
@Destroy @SignedBy("admin") @MigrateTo("successor")
public static JulcList<Payout> upgrade(State s, Ctx ctx) {
```

###### @Migrate

A creation that adopts an instance of the previous contract version: `(Params cfg, Old.State old, args..., [Ctx])`
returning the new state. The seed is the old state UTxO, whose token must be burned in the same transaction; the new
instance holds exactly the old lovelace and the new token.

**Target:** method. **Source:**
[`Migrate.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Migrate.java)

| Element | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | `String` | required | `"params.x"`, a `byte[]` field of the `@Params` record holding the previous policy |

Rules: at most one `@Migrate` per contract; it is its own kind of creation (no other kind annotation); the parameter
after the params must be the previous contract's state record.

```java title="examples/upgrade/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/upgrade/CounterV2.java"
@Migrate(from = "params.previous")
public static State adopt(Config cfg, CounterV1.State old) {
```

##### Invariants

###### @Invariant

A rule every state must keep (ADR-0009 D4): a static method taking the state (or an owned record), optionally the
`@Params` record, and returning `boolean`. The validator checks it on every state it accepts as an output (creation
and every action); the runtime checks it before submitting.

**Target:** method. **Elements:** none. **Source:**
[`Invariant.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Invariant.java)

Rules: `static`, returns `boolean`, cannot combine with a lifecycle annotation; cannot read state (or an owned record)
with MerkleMaps; a contract with `@Batched` actions cannot have invariants yet.

```java title="examples/treasury/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/treasury/Treasury.java"
@Invariant
public static boolean reachable(State s) {
    return s.quorum().signum() > 0 && s.quorum().compareTo(BigInteger.valueOf(s.council().size())) <= 0;
}
```

Guide: [Params, invariants and events](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/params-invariants-events/).
