### State API (julc-state-api)

URL: https://joust.julc.dev/reference/state-api/

`julc-state-api` (package `org.julclang.state.api`) is the library your contract code calls. Every class here runs in
two places: on the JVM, when the generated client runs your method to compute the next state, and on chain, compiled
by JuLC into the validator. Both must give the same answer on the same inputs, so the API is written in the JuLC
subset of Java and a few classes ship a separate on-chain body (see [On-chain variants](#on-chain-variants)).

This page covers the records and helper classes. The annotations have their own page:
[Annotations](https://joust.julc.dev/reference/annotations/). Sources:
[`julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api).

Types such as `JulcList`, `JulcMap` and `PlutusData` come from JuLC (`org.julclang.core`), and `Value`, `Address`,
`Credential`, `OutputDatum`, `TxOutRef`, `TxCert` and `DRep` from JuLC's ledger types (`org.julclang.ledger`).

##### Overview

| Class | Kind | Used by | What it is for |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`Ctx`](#ctx) | record | contract methods | Verified transaction facts: caller, received, balance, validity bounds |
| [`Require`](#require-and-requireexception) | class | contract methods | Contract rules: `Require.that(cond, "msg")` |
| [`RequireException`](#require-and-requireexception) | exception | JVM callers | What a failed rule throws on the JVM |
| [`Clock`](#clock) | class | contract methods | Deadline checks against the validity interval |
| [`Payout`, `Payouts`](#payout-and-payouts) | record, class | actions, destroys | Lovelace paid to key hashes |
| [`Funds`](#funds) | record | asset-aware methods | Native assets: own policy, own token name, received, held, deposits |
| [`Send`, `Sends`](#send-and-sends) | record, class | actions, destroys, `@Withdraw` | Outputs to any address with any datum |
| [`Datum`](#datum) | class | contract methods | Output datums for sends |
| [`Assets`](#assets) | class | contract methods | Multi-asset `Value` arithmetic, canonical on both sides |
| [`Deposit`, `Deposits`, `DepositClaim`](#deposit-deposits-and-depositclaim) | records, class | depositors, `@Receives` | Payments into another JOUST instance |
| [`ForeignInstance`](#foreigninstance) | record | `@Params` | Another contract's instance, for `@Reads` and deposits |
| [`Approval`, `Approvals`](#approvals-and-approval) | records | governor scripts | Approvals a script grants for `@AuthorizedBy` |
| [`Certs`](#certs) | class | `@Certify` handlers | Exact certificate checks |
| [`MerkleMap`, `MapEntry`](#merklemap-and-mapentry) | records | state records | An unbounded map held as a 32-byte root |
| [`MerkleMaps`](#merklemaps) | class | contract methods | Reading and writing a `MerkleMap` |
| [`SortedMaps`](#sortedmaps) | class | contract methods | `JulcMap` state kept in canonical CBOR key order |
| [`OutputClaim`, `OutputClaims`](#outputclaim-and-outputclaims) | records | generated code | The shared output-claim registry |
| [`mpf.*`](#the-mpf-package) | package | generated code, verifier | Merkle Patricia Forestry proofs and map claims |

##### Ctx

```java title="Ctx.java"
public record Ctx(byte[] caller, BigInteger received, BigInteger balance, BigInteger validFrom, BigInteger validTo) {}
```

Transaction facts an `@Init`, `@Action` or `@Destroy` method (and owned methods) may read. Declare it as the method's
last parameter, or the last before `Funds`. The client supplies it; the generated validator verifies every field
against the transaction before calling your method (ADR-0001 D3).

| Component | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `caller` | Key hash of the party calling. The transaction is signed by it. In a `@Batched` run, the intent's owner |
| `received` | Lovelace this call adds to the contract. Zero unless the method is `@Payable` |
| `balance` | Funds the call may allocate. In actions: the contract's lovelace before the call minus the min-ADA deposit. In destroys: everything the state UTxO holds, deposit included. Zero in `@Init` |
| `validFrom` | Start of the transaction's validity interval (POSIX ms, inclusive) |
| `validTo` | End of the validity interval (POSIX ms, exclusive) |

The validator checks that `validFrom` and `validTo` equal the transaction's finite bounds, and that
`validTo - validFrom` is at most `@StateContract(maxValidityMs)` (default one hour). For deadlines prefer
[`Clock`](#clock). A method without `Ctx` needs no signature and costs less.

Source: [`Ctx.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Ctx.java).
Guide: [Ctx, funds and payouts](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/ctx-and-funds/).

##### Require and RequireException

```java title="Require.java"
public static void that(boolean condition, String message)
```

`Require.that(cond, "message")` fails the call when `cond` is false. On the JVM it throws `RequireException` with the
message, so the client reports why a call was rejected before submitting anything. On chain (the bundled source in
`src/onchain/java`) it traces the message and fails the script. Both fail on exactly the same inputs (ADR-0001 D7).
A third variant, `src/discovery/java`, is compiled only into the transition programs the runtime engine runs: it traces
`joust:require <message>` before failing, so the engine tells the contract's refusal from any other failure by that tag
(ADR-0020). Validators never use it.

```java title="RequireException.java"
public class RequireException extends RuntimeException {
    public RequireException(String message)
}
```

Thrown only on the JVM. Contract code never constructs it (JuLC has no `throw`): use `Require.that`.

```java title="examples/token/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/token/Token.java"
Require.that(fromBalance.compareTo(amount) >= 0, "insufficient balance");
```

Sources: [`Require.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Require.java),
[on-chain `Require.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/onchain/java/org/julclang/state/api/Require.java),
[`RequireException.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/RequireException.java).
Guide: [Require and errors](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/require-and-errors/).

##### Clock

Deadline checks against the transaction's validity interval `[ctx.validFrom(), ctx.validTo())`. They hold for every
moment the transaction could be valid, which makes them the safe way to use time.

| Method | Returns | True when |
|---|---|---|
| `static boolean after(Ctx ctx, BigInteger t)` | `boolean` | `ctx.validFrom() >= t`: the call happens at or after `t` |
| `static boolean before(Ctx ctx, BigInteger t)` | `boolean` | `ctx.validTo() <= t`: the call happens strictly before `t` |

```java title="examples/crowdfund/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/crowdfund/Crowdfund.java"
Require.that(Clock.before(ctx, s.deadline()), "the campaign has ended");
```

> **Caution:** 
`Clock.before` needs the whole validity window to end before the deadline. On Yaci DevKit, whose time horizon is
minutes, keep the transaction's TTL short (the DevKit runtime uses 20 s).

Source: [`Clock.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Clock.java).
Guide: [Time](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/time/).

##### Payout and Payouts

```java title="Payout.java"
public record Payout(byte[] to, BigInteger lovelace) {}
```

Lovelace the contract pays to a public-key payment credential: `to` is the recipient's payment key hash, `lovelace`
is greater than zero. The validator tags payouts against double satisfaction.

`Payouts` builds the payout list an action or destroy returns:

| Method | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `static JulcList<Payout> none()` | `JulcList<Payout>` | No payouts |
| `static JulcList<Payout> of(byte[] to, BigInteger lovelace)` | `JulcList<Payout>` | One payout |
| `static JulcList<Payout> add(JulcList<Payout> payouts, byte[] to, BigInteger lovelace)` | `JulcList<Payout>` | Prepends one payout |
| `static BigInteger total(JulcList<Payout> payouts)` | `BigInteger` | Sum of the payouts' lovelace |

```java title="examples/counter/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/counter/Counter.java"
return Payouts.of(s.owner(), ctx.balance());
```

> **Note:** 
The Java runtime pays a payout to the key's enterprise address unless you map the key to another address with
`StateRuntime.Builder.address(pkh, bech32)`. Never map it to the fee payer's address: CCL's QuickTx takes the fee
from an output there.

Sources: [`Payout.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Payout.java),
[`Payouts.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Payouts.java).

##### Funds

```java title="Funds.java"
public record Funds(byte[] policy, byte[] self, Value received, Value held, JulcList<DepositClaim> deposits) {}
```

Native assets seen by a method of an asset-aware contract (ADR-0007 D1). Declare it as the last parameter, after `Ctx`
if there is one. The client supplies it; the generated validator checks every field.

| Component | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `policy` | This contract's policy id (its script hash): name your own tokens with it |
| `self` | The token name of what the method acts on: the instance id, or the object id for owned methods |
| `received` | Native assets the caller adds in this call. No lovelace entry (that is `Ctx.received`), positive amounts only, empty unless the method is `@Payable` |
| `held` | Native assets the UTxO holds before the call, without lovelace and without its own thread token. Empty when creating |
| `deposits` | Deposits from other contracts into this call's continuing output, in registry order. Filled only for a `@Receives` action |

A `@Payable` method with `Funds` must return a result record with `accepted`: exactly the native assets it takes.

```java title="examples/dex/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/dex/Dex.java"
BigInteger reserveToken = Assets.quantity(funds.held(), p.tokenPolicy(), p.tokenName());
```

Source: [`Funds.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Funds.java).
Guide: [Native assets, mints and sends](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/assets-mints-sends/).

##### Send and Sends

```java title="Send.java"
public record Send(Address to, Value value, OutputDatum datum) {}
```

An output a method sends from the UTxO it acts on (ADR-0007 D5): to any address, key or script, with any datum. The
generated validator requires an output at `to` with exactly `datum`, no reference script and at least `value`, claimed
for this call in the shared output registry so no other obligation can count it. For lovelace to a key, `Payout` is
cheaper.

| `Sends` method | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `static JulcList<Send> none()` | `JulcList<Send>` | No sends |
| `static JulcList<Send> of(Address to, Value value, OutputDatum datum)` | `JulcList<Send>` | One send |
| `static JulcList<Send> add(JulcList<Send> sends, Address to, Value value, OutputDatum datum)` | `JulcList<Send>` | Prepends one send |

```java title="examples/dex/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/dex/Dex.java"
Sends.of(wallet(ctx.caller()), Assets.of(p.tokenPolicy(), p.tokenName(), tokenOut), new OutputDatum.NoOutputDatum())
```

Sources: [`Send.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Send.java),
[`Sends.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Sends.java).

##### Datum

Output datums for sends, the same on the JVM and on chain.

| Method | Returns |
|---|---|
| `static OutputDatum inline(PlutusData d)` | An inline datum |
| `static OutputDatum none()` | No datum |

> **Caution:** 
A record cannot be passed as data in shared code: `(PlutusData) (Object) record` works on chain but throws on the JVM.
Build the datum with `Builtins.constrData`, `bData`, `iData` and `mkCons`, which run on both. A record `R(a, b)` is
`constrData(0, mkCons(a, mkCons(b, mkNilData())))`.

```java title="examples/market/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/market/Market.java"
Datum.inline(royalty(l))
```

Source: [`Datum.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Datum.java).

##### Assets

Multi-asset values for contract code (ADR-0007), with the same results on the JVM and on chain. Every value these
functions return is canonical, as the ledger writes values: policies and token names in ascending byte order, no zero
quantities, no empty token maps. Lovelace is the entry with the empty policy and the empty token name.

| Method | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `static Value none()` | `Value` | The empty value |
| `static Value of(byte[] policy, byte[] name, BigInteger quantity)` | `Value` | `quantity` of `(policy, name)`; empty if the quantity is zero |
| `static Value lovelace(BigInteger quantity)` | `Value` | `quantity` lovelace |
| `static Value add(Value a, Value b)` | `Value` | Entry-wise sum; zero sums vanish |
| `static Value subtract(Value a, Value b)` | `Value` | Entry-wise `a - b`; zero differences vanish, negative ones stay |
| `static BigInteger quantity(Value v, byte[] policy, byte[] name)` | `BigInteger` | Quantity of `(policy, name)`, zero if absent |
| `static BigInteger lovelaceOf(Value v)` | `BigInteger` | The lovelace in `v` |
| `static Value withoutLovelace(Value v)` | `Value` | `v` without its lovelace |
| `static boolean isEmpty(Value v)` | `boolean` | True if `v` holds nothing |
| `static boolean covers(Value a, Value b)` | `boolean` | True if `a` holds at least `b` of every entry. Both must be non-negative: on chain a negative quantity fails the script, on the JVM it throws |
| `static void check(Value v, String what)` | `void` | **JVM only.** Throws unless `v` is canonical (sorted, no zero quantities, no empty token maps, keys at most 32 bytes). The runtime and the harness run it on every value a method returns |
| `static TreeMap<String, TreeMap<String, BigInteger>> read(Value v)` | `TreeMap` | **JVM only.** Entries by policy and token name, as lower-case hex, in ledger order |

On chain the functions use the PV11 native Value builtins (CIP-153), which reject a non-canonical argument; ledger
values and the results of these functions always are canonical. The JVM body normalises instead, and `check` makes
sure a JVM test never passes on a value the chain would reject.

> **Caution:** 
A native `Value` cannot be a JuLC loop accumulator (use recursion). A redeemer field typed `Value` mis-decodes in JuLC:
use `PlutusData` there.

Sources: [`Assets.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Assets.java),
[on-chain `Assets.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/onchain/java/org/julclang/state/api/Assets.java).
Guide: [Native assets, mints and sends](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/assets-mints-sends/).

##### Deposit, Deposits and DepositClaim

Deposits are payments from one JOUST contract's call into another instance's continuing output in the same
transaction (ADR-0011 D3).

```java title="Deposit.java"
public record Deposit(byte[] policy, byte[] instance, Value value, PlutusData memo) {}
```

`value` goes into the continuing output of instance `instance` of contract `policy`, which must be spent in the same
transaction by an action that `@Receives` deposits. `memo` is any data the receiver may read (a beneficiary, an order
id). A method returns its deposits in a `deposits` result component.

| `Deposits` method | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `static JulcList<Deposit> none()` | `JulcList<Deposit>` | No deposits |
| `static JulcList<Deposit> of(ForeignInstance target, Value value, PlutusData memo)` | `JulcList<Deposit>` | One deposit into `target` |
| `static JulcList<Deposit> add(JulcList<Deposit> deposits, ForeignInstance target, Value value, PlutusData memo)` | `JulcList<Deposit>` | Prepends one deposit |
| `static BigInteger lovelace(JulcList<DepositClaim> deposits)` | `BigInteger` | The lovelace of every deposit a receiver got (`funds.deposits()`) |

```java title="DepositClaim.java"
public record DepositClaim(BigInteger output, TxOutRef by, Value value, PlutusData memo) {}
```

A deposit in the shared output registry: output `output` receives `value` from the input `by`, with `memo`. The output
verifier checks the value is canonical and positive, free of reserved tokens, and that `by` is an input. The depositor
checks its own claims; the receiver counts every claim on its continuing output exactly once.

```java title="examples/fees/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/fees/Stall.java"
Deposits.of(cfg.pot(), Assets.lovelace(fee), Builtins.bData(ctx.caller()))
```

Sources: [`Deposit.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Deposit.java),
[`Deposits.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Deposits.java),
[`DepositClaim.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/DepositClaim.java).
Guide: [Deposits](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/deposits/).

##### ForeignInstance

```java title="ForeignInstance.java"
public record ForeignInstance(byte[] policy, byte[] instance) {}
```

Another JOUST contract's instance (ADR-0011 D2): its applied script hash (policy) and its 32-byte instance id. Held
only in a `@Params` record, so the script it trusts is fixed at deploy. `@Reads("params.x")` and `Deposits.of` take it.

```java title="examples/oracle/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/oracle/Shop.java"
public record Config(ForeignInstance oracle, BigInteger maxAgeMs) {}
```

Source: [`ForeignInstance.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/ForeignInstance.java).
Guide: [Reads and composition](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/reads-and-composition/).

##### Approvals and Approval

```java
public record Approval(byte[] policy, byte[] target, BigInteger action) {}
public record Approvals(JulcList<Approval> approvals) {}
```

`Approvals` is the Rewarding redeemer a Plutus governor script uses to approve JOUST actions for `@AuthorizedBy` with a
script credential (ADR-0009 r2). Each `Approval` says the JOUST contract `policy` may run its action with redeemer tag
`action` on `target` (an instance or object id). The governor's own rules decide which approvals it lists; each JOUST
validator accepts only the one naming itself, its target and its action.

Sources: [`Approval.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Approval.java),
[`Approvals.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Approvals.java).
Guide: [Authorization](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/authorization/).

##### Certs

Exact certificate checks for `@Certify` handlers (ADR-0010 r2), the same on the JVM and on chain.

| Method | True when |
|---|---|
| `static boolean isRegistration(TxCert cert)` | A stake registration (with or without a deposit) |
| `static boolean delegatesOnlyTo(TxCert cert, byte[] pool)` | A stake delegation (alone or with registration) to exactly `pool`, and only stake: no vote delegation |
| `static boolean delegatesVoteTo(TxCert cert, DRep drep)` | A vote delegation (alone or with registration) to exactly `drep`, and only votes |
| `static boolean isDRepLifecycle(TxCert cert)` | DRep registration or update of the contract's own credential |
| `static boolean sameDRep(DRep a, DRep b)` | DRep equality that also holds on the JVM |
| `static boolean sameCredential(Credential a, Credential b)` | Credential equality that also holds on the JVM |

Records with byte arrays do not compare by value on the JVM, which is why `sameDRep` and `sameCredential` exist.

```java title="examples/staking/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/staking/StakedVault.java"
return Certs.isRegistration(cert) || Certs.delegatesOnlyTo(cert, cfg.pool()) || Certs.isDRepLifecycle(cert);
```

Source: [`Certs.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/Certs.java).
Guide: [Staking and governance](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/staking-and-governance/).

##### MerkleMap and MapEntry

```java
public record MerkleMap(byte[] root, JulcList<MapEntry> reads, JulcList<MapEntry> writes) {}
public record MapEntry(byte[] key, boolean present, byte[] value) {}
```

A `MerkleMap` is a map stored as a Merkle Patricia Forestry root (ADR-0002). Use it as a component of the state record
(or of an owned record) to hold an unbounded map: the datum keeps only the 32-byte `root`, and each call proves the
keys it touches. `reads` and `writes` exist only while a contract method runs: the proven entries this call may read,
and this call's writes, latest first. In the datum both are empty.

A `MapEntry` is one key: present with a value, or absent (with an empty value).

> **Caution:** 
Use `MerkleMap` and `MapEntry` only as top-level components of the state or owned record. Never construct them, never
pass them as arguments, and never read `.reads()`, `.writes()` or `.root()` in contract code: go through
[`MerkleMaps`](#merklemaps).

Sources: [`MerkleMap.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/MerkleMap.java),
[`MapEntry.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/MapEntry.java).

##### MerkleMaps

Reading and changing a `MerkleMap` (ADR-0002 D2). A lookup sees this call's writes (latest first), then its read set.
Writes add to the map's pending writes; the root never changes inside a method. The verifier (a shared withdraw-zero
script) proves the reads and computes the new root.

| Method | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `static MerkleMap empty()` | `MerkleMap` | A new, empty map (for `@Init` and `@OwnedInit`) |
| `static boolean isEmpty(MerkleMap m)` | `boolean` | The map was empty before this call and this call wrote nothing. Check it before destroying |
| `static boolean contains(MerkleMap m, byte[] key)` | `boolean` | The key is present |
| `static byte[] get(MerkleMap m, byte[] key, byte[] otherwise)` | `byte[]` | The value, or `otherwise` |
| `static BigInteger getInt(MerkleMap m, byte[] key, BigInteger otherwise)` | `BigInteger` | The value as an unsigned big-endian integer, or `otherwise` |
| `static MerkleMap put(MerkleMap m, byte[] key, byte[] value)` | `MerkleMap` | Sets `key` to `value` |
| `static MerkleMap putInt(MerkleMap m, byte[] key, BigInteger value)` | `MerkleMap` | Stores a non-negative integer as its minimal big-endian bytes (zero is the empty byte string). Fails on a negative value |
| `static MerkleMap remove(MerkleMap m, byte[] key)` | `MerkleMap` | Removes `key` |
| `static MapEntry lookup(MerkleMap m, byte[] key)` | `MapEntry` | This call's latest write for `key`, else the read set |
| `static JulcList<MapEntry> netWrites(MerkleMap m)` | `JulcList<MapEntry>` | The latest write of each key (used by generated code) |

Methods are pure: always use the returned map.

```java title="examples/token/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/token/Token.java"
BigInteger balance = MerkleMaps.getInt(s.balances(), to, BigInteger.ZERO);
return new State(s.admin(), s.supply().add(amount), MerkleMaps.putInt(s.balances(), to, balance.add(amount)));
```

**A key outside the read set** behaves differently on each side, which is the only difference between the sources:

| Where | Source | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| JVM | `src/main/java` | Read from the `ReadSource` the runtime (or the test harness) binds, and recorded so it joins the read set |
| On chain | `src/onchain/java` | Fails the script (ADR-0002 D3) |
| Transition programs | `src/discovery/java` | Answered as absent and named in a `joust:read <root hex> <key hex>` trace, so the engine can prove every read and run again (ADR-0015 D3) |

The empty root holds no key, so lookups on an empty map need no proof (this lets `@Init` read the maps it creates).
The JVM source also has runtime hooks you do not call from contract code: the `ReadSource` interface
(`MapEntry read(byte[] root, byte[] key)`), `static <T> T withReads(ReadSource source, Supplier<T> body)`, and
`static MapEntry read(byte[] root, byte[] key)`.

Sources: [`MerkleMaps.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/MerkleMaps.java),
[on-chain](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/onchain/java/org/julclang/state/api/MerkleMaps.java),
[discovery](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/discovery/java/org/julclang/state/api/MerkleMaps.java).
Guide: [MerkleMaps](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/merklemaps/). Tutorial: [Token balances in a MerkleMap](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/token-merklemap/).

##### SortedMaps

Maps with `byte[]` keys kept in canonical CBOR key order (shorter key first, then byte-wise), on the JVM and on chain
alike. Use them for `JulcMap` fields of the state.

| Method | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `static boolean before(byte[] a, byte[] b)` | `boolean` | `a` sorts before `b` in canonical CBOR order |
| `static JulcMap<byte[], BigInteger> put(JulcMap<byte[], BigInteger> m, byte[] k, BigInteger v)` | `JulcMap` | `m` with `k` set to `v`, keeping canonical order |
| `static JulcMap<byte[], BigInteger> remove(JulcMap<byte[], BigInteger> m, byte[] k)` | `JulcMap` | `m` without `k` (order is kept) |
| `static BigInteger getOr(JulcMap<byte[], BigInteger> m, byte[] k, BigInteger otherwise)` | `BigInteger` | The value for `k`, or `otherwise` |

Why: a `JulcMap` is an ordered association list and `insert` prepends, but cardano-client-lib writes inline datums in
canonical CBOR, which sorts map keys. A state map not already in canonical order would be written differently from
what the validator recomputes, and the call would fail on chain. The runtime refuses to submit such a state.

```java title="examples/crowdfund/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/crowdfund/Crowdfund.java"
BigInteger before = SortedMaps.getOr(s.backers(), ctx.caller(), BigInteger.ZERO);
```

Source: [`SortedMaps.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/SortedMaps.java).
Tutorial: [Escrow and crowdfunding](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/escrow-crowdfund/).

##### OutputClaim and OutputClaims

```java
public record OutputClaim(BigInteger output, TxOutRef by) {}
public record OutputClaims(JulcList<OutputClaim> claims, JulcList<DepositClaim> deposits) {}
```

The shared output-claim registry (ADR-0007 D5). An `OutputClaim` says output `output` of the transaction is a `Send`
of the transition whose UTxO is `by`. `OutputClaims` is the redeemer of the JOUST output verifier: every send claim,
by strictly increasing output index (no output is claimed twice), and every deposit claim, by non-decreasing output
index (an output may receive several deposits). The runtime builds it; contract code does not.

Sources: [`OutputClaim.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/OutputClaim.java),
[`OutputClaims.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/OutputClaims.java).

##### The mpf package

`org.julclang.state.api.mpf` holds the Merkle Patricia Forestry code behind MerkleMaps. Generated validators, the
shared map verifier and the runtime use it; contract code uses [`MerkleMaps`](#merklemaps) instead.

###### Mpf

Roots and updates compatible with Aiken's `aiken-lang/merkle-patricia-forestry` and cardano-client-lib's `MpfTrie`
(blake2b-256, radix 16, keys and values hashed). A port of CCL's `WireProof` in the JuLC subset: it runs on chain and
on the JVM alike. Proofs are in the form `MpfTrie.getProofPlutusData` returns.

| Method | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `static byte[] emptyRoot()` | `byte[]` | The empty trie's root: 32 zero bytes |
| `static boolean has(byte[] root, byte[] key, byte[] value, JulcList<ProofStep> proof)` | `boolean` | `key -> value` is in the trie |
| `static boolean miss(byte[] root, byte[] key, JulcList<ProofStep> proof)` | `boolean` | `key` is absent |
| `static byte[] insert(byte[] root, byte[] key, byte[] value, JulcList<ProofStep> proof)` | `byte[]` | Root after inserting an absent key; fails if the proof does not show it absent |
| `static byte[] delete(byte[] root, byte[] key, byte[] value, JulcList<ProofStep> proof)` | `byte[]` | Root after deleting `key -> value`; fails if not present with that value |
| `static byte[] update(byte[] root, byte[] key, JulcList<ProofStep> proof, byte[] oldValue, byte[] newValue)` | `byte[]` | Root after changing `key` from `oldValue` to `newValue` |
| `static byte[] including(byte[] key, byte[] value, JulcList<ProofStep> proof)` | `byte[]` | Root of a trie holding `key -> value` at the position the proof describes |
| `static byte[] excluding(byte[] key, JulcList<ProofStep> proof)` | `byte[]` | Root of the trie the proof describes, without `key` |

###### Proof and claim records

| Type | Definition | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ProofStep` | `sealed interface ProofStep permits Branch, Fork, Leaf` | One proof step, in Aiken's Plutus encoding |
| `ProofStep.Branch` | `record Branch(BigInteger skip, byte[] neighbors)` | A branch node: the neighbour hashes along the path (4 x 32 bytes) |
| `ProofStep.Fork` | `record Fork(BigInteger skip, Neighbor neighbor)` | A branch with exactly one other child |
| `ProofStep.Leaf` | `record Leaf(BigInteger skip, byte[] key, byte[] value)` | A branch whose one other child is a leaf: its key hash and value hash |
| `ProofStep.Neighbor` | `record Neighbor(BigInteger nibble, byte[] prefix, byte[] root)` | The other child of a fork |
| `ReadProof` | `record ReadProof(MapEntry entry, JulcList<ProofStep> proof)` | A read-set entry and its proof against the pre-call root |
| `WriteProof` | `record WriteProof(MapEntry before, MapEntry after, JulcList<ProofStep> proof)` | One net write: the entry before and after, and the proof of its position at this step |
| `MapClaim` | `record MapClaim(byte[] policy, TxOutRef owner, BigInteger field, byte[] oldRoot, JulcList<ReadProof> reads, JulcList<WriteProof> writes, byte[] newRoot)` | What the verifier proves for one map of one instance; found by `(policy, owner, field)` (ADR-0014) |
| `MapClaims` | `record MapClaims(JulcList<MapClaim> claims)` | The map verifier's redeemer: every claim of the transaction |

###### MapWitnesses

MerkleMap checks, split between the generic map verifier (a withdraw-zero script that does the MPF work) and each
contract's validator (which only matches claims to its own maps). ADR-0002 D3 and D9.

| Method | Side | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `static boolean verify(MapClaim c)` | verifier | The claim's reads are proven against its old root, and its writes, applied in order, turn the old root into the new root |
| `static MapClaim claimFor(MapClaims claims, byte[] policy, TxOutRef owner, long field)` | contract | The claim for map `field` of the instance whose state input (or seed) is `owner`; fails if none |
| `static MerkleMap open(byte[] root, MapClaim c)` | contract | The map a method sees: the claim's verified reads over `root`, which must be the claim's old root |
| `static byte[] commit(byte[] root, MerkleMap after, MapClaim c)` | contract | The new root, once the claim's writes are exactly the method's net writes in order |

Sources: [`mpf/`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/julc-state-api/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/api/mpf).
The verifier itself is the `julc-state-verifier` module.

##### On-chain variants

A few classes need a different body on chain. Their on-chain sources live in `src/onchain/java` and replace the JVM
source in the bundle JuLC compiles; ADR-0001 D7 keeps that set tiny.

| Class | JVM body (`src/main/java`) | On-chain body (`src/onchain/java`) |
|---|---|---|
| `Require` | Throws `RequireException(message)` | `ContextsLib.trace(message)`, then `Builtins.error()`; transition programs (`src/discovery/java`): `ContextsLib.trace("joust:require " + message)`, then `Builtins.error()` |
| `Assets` | `TreeMap` arithmetic that normalises; adds `check` and `read` | PV11 native Value builtins (`insertCoin`, `unionValue`, `scaleValue`, `lookupCoin`, ...) |
| `MerkleMaps` | Reads missing keys from the bound `ReadSource` | A missing key fails the script |

`src/discovery/java` holds a third `MerkleMaps`, compiled only into transition programs (ADR-0015 D3), never into
validators.

The build's `bundleOnchainSources` task writes the JuLC library sources (`META-INF/plutus-sources/`) with these
overrides in place. A consumer puts them on its annotation processor path: inside the JOUST build as
`project(path: ':julc-state-api', configuration: 'onchainSources')` (a directory), and from the snapshot repository as
`org.julclang:julc-state-api:<version>:onchain`.

> **Caution:** 
Shared code (contracts and this API) must never compare `byte[]` with `==` or `.equals`: on chain that compares bytes,
on the JVM it compares references. Use `ByteStringLib.equals`.

### Java runtime API

URL: https://joust.julc.dev/reference/java-runtime-api/

The public API of `julc-state-runtime` (package `org.julclang.state.runtime`) and `julc-state-server` (package
`org.julclang.state.server`), from the sources in
[`julc-state-runtime/src/main/java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/julc-state-runtime/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/runtime).
For how to use them, see [Java off-chain runtime](https://joust.julc.dev/apps/java-runtime/).

Most applications use only the generated `<Name>Client`, `StateRuntime`, `Compose`, `WalletAccount`, `PreparedTx`
and the exceptions. The rest is what generated clients, the testkit and the JavaScript engines are built on; it is
public so that they can reach it, and it is marked **internal** below where you should not need it.

> **Caution:** 

JOUST is pre-release. These signatures can change before the first release.

##### Generated client: `<Name>Client`

Generated by the processor into the contract's package. Shown for a contract `Name` with state `S`.

| Member | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SPEC` | `static final ContractSpec<S>` | The contract's spec: name, validator class, state class, min-ADA, `maxDatumBytes`, `maxValidityMs` |
| `contract(StateRuntime runtime [, P params])` | static | The `StateContractHandle<S>` on that network (with `@Params`: for that parameter set) |
| `policyIdFor(P params)` | static | With `@Params` only: the policy id of that parameter set |
| `deploy(StateRuntime runtime, [P params,] Account callerAccount, args... [, BigInteger payLovelace] [, Value payAssets])` | static | Runs `@Init`, creates an instance, returns a client for it |
| `at(StateRuntime runtime, [P params,] String instanceId)` | static | Reconnects to an existing instance |
| `<action>(Account callerAccount, args... [, payLovelace] [, payAssets] [, Account... cosigners or Authorization authorization])` | instance | Runs an `@Action` or `@Destroy`; returns `CallResult<S>` |
| `<view>(args...)` | instance | Runs a `@View` on the current state, off chain |
| `state()` | instance | `S`: the current state |
| `lovelace()` | instance | `BigInteger`: lovelace held, deposit included |
| `fullValue()` | instance | `org.julclang.ledger.Value`: everything held |
| `instanceId()` | instance | `String`: the instance id (hex thread-token name) |
| `instance()` | instance | The underlying `StateInstance<S>` |

Contracts with owned objects also get, per owned type, a creation method returning a typed object wrapper
(for example `BankClient.open(Account, BigInteger)` returning `AccountObject` with `objectId()`, `value()`,
`lovelace()`, `fullValue()` and the owned actions), an accessor by id (`account(String objectId)`) and a
`<TYPE>_CODEC`. Contracts with `@Batched` actions also get `INTENTS` (an `IntentCodec<S>`), `<action>Intent(...)`
methods returning `IntentHandle<S>`, `batch(Account, int)`, `pendingIntents()` and `intent(String)`.
Contracts with keyed types (ADR-0016) get, per keyed type `T`, `<t>List()`, `<t>(byte[] key)`, `<t>Exists(byte[] key)`,
`<t>Keys()`, one insert method per `@OwnedInit`, a `<T>Object` wrapper and a `<T>_TYPE` constant: see
[Keyed objects](#keyed-objects).

##### StateRuntime

`public final class StateRuntime`: everything a client needs to talk to one network. Immutable.

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `static builder(BackendService backend)` | `Builder` | Starts a runtime over a CCL backend |
| `backend()` | `BackendService` | |
| `evaluator()` | `TransactionEvaluator` | May be null: QuickTx then uses the backend's evaluation endpoint |
| `network()` | `Network` | |
| `chainTime()` | `ChainTime` | |
| `ttlMs()` | `long` | |
| `maxRetries()` | `int` | |
| `confirmTimeout()` | `Duration` | |
| `mapVerifier()` | `VerifierHandle` | The shared MerkleMap verifier on this network (ADR-0002 D9) |
| `outputVerifier()` | `VerifierHandle` | The shared output verifier, carrying the output-claim registry (ADR-0007 D5) |
| `mapStore()` | `NodeStore` | Where MerkleMap mirrors keep trie nodes (opened on first use) |
| `mapProver()`, `mapProver(String unit)` | `MerkleSupport.Prover` | How map calls get reads and writes proven; with a unit, rebuilds a missing map from its chain history first |

###### StateRuntime.Builder

| Method | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `chainTime(ChainTime)` | **required** | Slot and POSIX time conversion and the tip; `build()` fails without it |
| `network(Network)` | `Networks.testnet()` | |
| `evaluator(TransactionEvaluator)` | none | Script budget evaluation, e.g. JuLC's `JulcTransactionEvaluator` |
| `ttl(Duration)` | 10 minutes | Validity window of calls that read `Ctx` or time annotations, clamped to the contract's `maxValidityMs`. Must stay inside the network's time horizon |
| `maxRetries(int)` | 3 | Rebuilds after the node rejected a call because the state moved |
| `confirmTimeout(Duration)` | 90 seconds | Wait for a submitted transaction to appear on chain |
| `address(byte[] pkh, String bech32)` | none | Pay this key hash at this address instead of its enterprise address |
| `log(Consumer<String>)` | no-op | Progress messages |
| `onBuilt(Consumer<BuiltTx>)` | none | Called with every transaction built, before it is submitted or returned |
| `referenceScript(Utxo)` | none | A known reference-script output; contracts with that script hash use it instead of scanning their address |
| `mapStore(NodeStore)` | RocksDB | Node store for MerkleMap mirrors |
| `mapStorePath(String)` | `joust.mapStore` system property, else `./.joust/mpf` | Directory of the default RocksDB store. The property value `memory` keeps it in memory (tests) |
| `mapProver(MerkleSupport.Prover)` | a trie over `mapStore` | Map proofs from elsewhere (the runtime engine's caller supplies them) |
| `relays(List<Relay>)` | the backend alone | Keyed calls only: every attempt goes to each relay; any acceptance or unknown answer dominates rejections |
| `relayTimeout(Duration)` | 60 seconds | Keyed calls only: how long an attempt waits for each relay before its answer counts as unknown |
| `settlementSlots(long)` | 2 | Keyed calls only: slots past the last attempt's window before a series may end in a definite failure (at most 100,000) |
| `topUpAllowance(long lovelace)` | 10 ADA | Keyed calls only: the most an operation adds to an output to reach the ledger minimum |
| `pageLimits(long maxStartSlots, long maxValiditySlots)` | none | Keeps keyed calls' windows within a page's limits (the verifier's defaults are 60 and 900 slots) |
| `build()` | | The `StateRuntime` |

`StateRuntime.BuiltTx` is `record BuiltTx(String what, Transaction tx, boolean prepared)`: what the transaction is
for, the transaction (signed when submitted, unsigned when prepared), and which.

##### ChainTime and SlotChainTime

`public interface ChainTime`

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `long slotToPosixMs(long slot)` | POSIX ms at the start of `slot` |
| `long posixMsToSlotFloor(long posixMs)` | The last slot starting at or before `posixMs` |
| `long slotLengthMs()` | Length of one slot |
| `long tipSlot()` | The current tip slot |

`public final class SlotChainTime implements ChainTime`: a linear clock (one slot length since `zeroSlot`), tip from
the backend.

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `SlotChainTime(long zeroSlot, long zeroTimeMs, long slotLengthMs, BackendService backend)` | DevKit: `(0, startTime * 1000, slotLength * 1000, backend)`. Preview: `(0, 1666656000000L, 1000, backend)` |
| `zeroSlot()`, `zeroTimeMs()`, `slotLengthMs()` | The configuration |

##### StateContractHandle

`public final class StateContractHandle<S>`: a contract on a network. Creates instances and reconnects to them.

| Member | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `StateContractHandle(StateRuntime runtime, ContractSpec<S> spec [, Object params])` | | With params: the validator with `params` applied (its own policy id and address) |
| `static scriptFor(ContractSpec<?> spec, Object params)` | `PlutusV3Script` | The applied script; refuses one too large to publish by reference |
| `static policyIdFor(ContractSpec<?> spec, Object params)` | `String` | The policy id for a parameter set |
| `static instanceIdOf(String seedTxHash, int seedIndex)` | `String` | `blake2b_256(txId ++ I2OSP(index, 2))`, hex |
| `policyId()`, `address()`, `rewardAddress()` | `String` | Script hash (= policy id), the state address, the script's reward address |
| `script()`, `spec()`, `runtime()`, `params()` | | |
| `at(String instanceId)` | `StateInstance<S>` | An existing instance |
| `deploy(Deploy<S> d)` | `DeployResult<S>` | Creates an instance (publishes the reference script first if needed) |
| `adopt(Deploy<S> d, Utxo prior)` | `DeployResult<S>` | Adopts an instance of a previous version; only inside a `Compose` with its `@MigrateTo` destroy (ADR-0011 D4) |
| `findReferenceScript()` | `Utxo` | The reference-script UTxO at the contract address, or null |
| `ensureReferenceScript(Account payer)` | `Utxo` | Finds it, or publishes it paid by `payer` |
| `prepareReferenceScript(String payerAddress)` | `Transaction` | The unsigned publishing transaction for a wallet, or null if already on chain |
| `registerStake(Account payer)` | | Registers the script's stake credential (ADR-0010) |
| `delegateTo(String poolId, Account caller, Account... cosigners)` | `String` | Delegates through the contract's `@Certify` handler |
| `rewardBalance()` | `BigInteger` | Rewards withdrawable from the script's stake credential |
| `withdrawRewards(Object rewardsRedeemer, BigInteger amount, JulcList<Send> sends, Account caller, Account... cosigners)` | `String` | Withdraws rewards through the `@Withdraw` handler |

`record DeployResult<S>(StateInstance<S> instance, String txHash, S state)`.

##### StateInstance

`public final class StateInstance<S>`: one live instance, by its thread-token name.

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `instanceId()` | `String` | Hex, lower case |
| `unit()` | `String` | Asset unit of the thread token: policy id + instance id |
| `contract()` | `StateContractHandle<S>` | |
| `utxo()` | `Utxo` | The current state UTxO; `InstanceNotFoundException` if none |
| `state()` | `S` | Decoded from the inline datum |
| `view(Function<S, T> f)` | `T` | Runs a read-only function of the state (MerkleMap lookups served from the mirror) |
| `lovelace()` | `BigInteger` | Deposit included |
| `value()` | `Value` | The full value (ADR-0007) |
| `call(Call<S> call)` | `CallResult<S>` | Runs an action or destroy: on the JVM, then on chain; retries only on contention or a stale input |

##### Call and Deploy (filled in by generated clients)

`public final class Call<S>`: one `@Action` or `@Destroy` call. `Call.Kind` is `ACTION` or `DESTROY`.

| Factory / builder method | Description |
|---|---|
| `static action(String name, Account caller)` | Starts an action call |
| `static destroy(String name, Account caller, Object burnRedeemer)` | Starts a destroy call |
| `received(BigInteger lovelace)` | `ctx.received()` (`@Payable`) |
| `usesCtx(boolean)` | The method declares `Ctx` (the caller signs; a validity interval is set) |
| `signedBy(String field, Function<S, byte[]> key)` | `@SignedBy`/`@OnlyOwner` |
| `validAfter(String field, Function<S, BigInteger> t)`, `validBefore(...)` | Time annotations |
| `run(BiFunction<S, Ctx, Transition<S>> run)` | Runs the method on the JVM |
| `runShared(SharedRun<S> run)` | An owned method that reads the instance state (`@Shared`) |
| `runAssets(boolean shared, AssetRun<S> run)` | A method of an asset-aware contract (Funds in) |
| `redeemer(ActRedeemer)`, `redeemerWith(BiFunction<Ctx, Transition<S>, Object>)` | The spend redeemer; the second form sees the result (events) |
| `receivedAssets(Value)` | Native assets the caller offers |
| `byAction(Function<TxOutRef, Object>)` | The `ByAction` mint redeemer for user-token mints |
| `cosigners(Account...)` | Further signers (`@Quorum`) |
| `authorization(Authorization)` | How `@AuthorizedBy` is proven |
| `migrates()` | A `@MigrateTo` destroy: funds move to the successor |
| `movesTo(String instanceId)` | An owned object moves to that instance (`@Into`) |
| `receives()` | The action takes deposits (`@Receives`) |
| `referenceInputs(Utxo...)` | Reference inputs the call reads (`@Reads`) |
| `build()` | The `Call` |

`public record Deploy<S>(Account caller, BigInteger received, boolean usesCtx, Function<Ctx, S> run,
CreateRedeemer redeemer, Value receivedAssets, AssetInit<S> assetRun)`, with a five-argument constructor for
contracts without assets.

`public record Transition<S>(S next, JulcList<Payout> payouts, JulcList<Send> sends, Value mint, Value accepted,
JulcList<?> events, JulcList<Deposit> deposits)`: the JVM result of a method. Factories `of(next)`,
`of(next, payouts)`, `end(payouts)`, `full(next, payouts, sends, mint, accepted)`; `withEvents(...)`,
`withDeposits(...)`.

##### CallResult

`public record CallResult<S>(String txHash, S state, List<Payout> payouts, List<Object> events)`

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `txHash()` | The transaction, included on chain |
| `state()` | The state after the call; `null` if it destroyed the instance |
| `payouts()` | What the contract paid out |
| `events()` | Events the method emitted, as the redeemer carried them (ADR-0009 D5) |
| `events(Class<E> type)` | The same, cast to `E` |

##### ContractSpec

`public record ContractSpec<S>(String name, Class<?> validatorClass, Class<S> stateClass, long minAda,
int maxDatumBytes, long maxValidityMs, boolean stakeSelf, String scriptCborHex, List<Integer> mapFields)`. Each
generated client holds one as `SPEC`. Shorter constructors leave `stakeSelf` false and the rest null.
`static described(...)` builds the spec of a contract known only by its description and compiled script, with its
state as `PlutusData` (ADR-0015 D4). `layout()` locates the state's MerkleMaps.

##### Compose

`public final class Compose`: several calls in one atomic transaction (ADR-0011 D1).

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `static of(StateRuntime runtime, Account payer)` | `Compose` | `payer` pays the fee |
| `add(Runnable call)` | `Compose` | Any client call: action, destroy, deploy, owned call |
| `allowSharedSigners()` | `Compose` | Lets one key's signature count for several calls (refused by default) |
| `submit()` | `String` | Builds, checks, submits and confirms; returns the hash |
| `prepare()` | `PreparedTx` | Builds for a wallet to sign; the payer and every caller must be `WalletAccount`s |
| `designate(String ref)` | `Compose` | For `prepare()` only: the wallet input (`txhash#index`) a page designated for a keyed call ([Keyed objects](#keyed-objects)) |

Refused before submitting: one UTxO spent by two calls; two calls minting under one policy; validity windows that do
not overlap; a key signing for more than one call (without `allowSharedSigners()`); a deposit into an instance whose
call in the transaction is not `@Receives`. Inside another composition, `submit()`/`prepare()` join the outer
transaction (`prepare()` cannot be nested).

##### WalletAccount

`public final class WalletAccount extends Account`: a caller known only by its address (ADR-0013 D1).

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `static of(String bech32, Network network)` | A base or enterprise address with a key payment credential, on `network`; script, pointer and Byron addresses are refused |
| `paymentKeyHash()` | The 28-byte key hash the wallet signs with |
| `address()` | The address as given |
| `baseAddress()`, `changeAddress()`, `enterpriseAddress()`, `stakeAddress()` | Answered from the address |
| `mnemonic()`, `hdKeyPair()`, `sign(...)`, every other key method | Throw `UnsupportedOperationException` |

##### PreparedTx

`public final class PreparedTx`: a balanced transaction waiting for wallet signatures.

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cbor()` | `String` | The unsigned transaction, hex CBOR, for CIP-30 `signTx(cbor, true)` |
| `txHash()` | `String` | |
| `requiredSigners()` | `List<String>` | Key hashes (hex) that must sign: the payer's and each caller's |
| `validTo()` | `long` | The last valid slot, or -1 if unbounded |
| `plan()` | `Map<String, Object>` | The portable plan of the transaction (`TxPlan`) |
| `transaction()` | `Transaction` | A copy, for inspection |
| `withWitnesses(String... witnessSetsCbor)` | `String` | The signed transaction, hex CBOR, after checking every signature |
| `submit(String... witnessSetsCbor)` | `String` | Adds the witnesses, submits, waits for inclusion |

Witness sets may carry vkey signatures only; each must be a valid signature of this transaction's hash, and together
they must cover `requiredSigners()`. Otherwise a `JoustException`.

##### Authorization

`public record Authorization(List<Account> signers, String rewardAddress, PlutusScript script, Object redeemer)`: how
a call proves `@AuthorizedBy` (ADR-0009 D3).

| Factory | Description |
|---|---|
| `static key(Account signer)` | A key credential: the key signs |
| `static script(String rewardAddress, PlutusScript script, Object redeemer, Account... signers)` | A script credential, run for a zero withdrawal; its redeemer must be an `Approvals` list naming the action |

##### Exceptions

| Class | Extends | Thrown when |
|---|---|---|
| `org.julclang.state.api.RequireException` | `RuntimeException` | A contract rule failed on the JVM; nothing was submitted |
| `JoustException` | `RuntimeException` | Base class of the runtime's failures |
| `SubmitException` | `JoustException` | The builder failed or the node rejected the transaction; nothing was accepted |
| `ContentionException` | `JoustException` | The state kept moving; gave up after `maxRetries`. For a keyed operation, `attempts()` and `designatedInput()` name what was tried |
| `PendingTransactionException` | `JoustException` | Submitted but not seen on chain in time; `txHash()` gives the hash. Do not resubmit blindly. For a keyed operation, `attempts()` lists every attempt handed out and `designatedInput()` the input they all spend |
| `InstanceNotFoundException` | `JoustException` | No UTxO holds the instance's thread token |

##### Helpers

| Class | Members | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Keys` | `static byte[] pkh(Account)` | The payment key hash of an account (a `WalletAccount`'s from its address) |
| `LedgerAddresses` | `static Address toLedger(String bech32)`, `static String toBech32(Address, Network)` | Between bech32 and JuLC's ledger `Address` (for `Send` recipients) |
| `ForeignReads` | `static <T> Read<T> read(StateRuntime, ForeignInstance, Class<T>)`; `record Read<T>(Utxo utxo, T state)` | Reads another contract's instance for `@Reads` |
| `TxPlan` | `static Map<String, Object> of(Transaction)` | A portable summary of a transaction (inputs, outputs, mints, redeemers...) that pages compare against the CBOR |
| `CclCryptoProvider` | implements JuLC's `CryptoProvider` | Hash and signature builtins for contract code on the JVM; installed by `StateRuntime` |

##### Owned objects, intents and batches

| Class | Key members | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `OwnedObject<S, R>` | `static at(StateInstance<S>, String objectId, Codec<R>)`, `static create(StateInstance<S>, Create<R>, Codec<R>)`, `static objectIdOf(String seedTxHash, int seedIndex)`, `objectId()`, `unit()`, `instance()`, `utxo()`, `value()`, `lovelace()`, `fullValue()`, `call(Call<R>)` | One owned object (ADR-0003, ADR-0012). Object ids are `0x4F ++ blake2b_224(txId ++ I2OSP(index, 2))` |
| `IntentHandle<S>` | `DEFAULT_DEPOSIT` (2 ADA), `static create(StateInstance<S>, IntentCodec<S>, Account owner, Object call, BigInteger received, BigInteger deposit, Instant deadline)`, `static at(...)`, `static intentIdOf(...)`, `intentId()`, `unit()`, `isPending()`, `data()`, `cancel(Account owner)` | One intent (ADR-0004) |
| `Batcher<S>` | `Batcher(StateInstance<S>, IntentCodec<S>)`, `pending()`, `run(Account batcher, int max)`, `DEFAULT_MAX` (8), `static fold(...)`, `LEDGER_ORDER` | Folds pending intents into one batch transaction; halves the batch if it does not fit |
| `IntentCodec<S>` | interface, implemented by the generated `INTENTS` | Builds and reads the validator's intent types; `step(...)` is one step of the fold |

`Batcher.BatchResult<S>(String txHash, S state, List<String> applied, Map<String, String> skipped)`: `txHash` is null
when nothing could be applied; `skipped` gives each skipped intent's reason.

##### Keyed objects

ADR-0016. Guide:
[Keyed objects](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/keyed-objects/).

| Class | Key members | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `KeyedList<S, R>` | `KeyedList(StateInstance<S>, KeyedType<R>)`, `type()`, `instance()`, `unit(byte[] key)`, `find(byte[] key)` (`Optional`), `get(byte[] key)`, `exists(byte[] key)`, `keys()`, `insert(Insert<R>)` | One keyed type's list in one instance. `find` and `get` validate the node; "not found" means the provider returned nothing. `keys()` walks from the head and reports a broken walk as an inconsistent snapshot. `insert` is refused on the JVM if the key is taken |
| `KeyedList.Entry` | `record Entry(byte[] key, boolean retired)`, `keyHex()` | One key of a walk |
| `KeyedList.Insert<R>` | record, filled in by generated clients | An insert: the method's name, caller, payment, and how to run the method and build its redeemer |
| `KeyedObject<S, R>` | `key()`, `keyHex()`, `unit()`, `list()`, `utxo()`, `value()`, `retired()`, `lovelace()`, `call(Call<R>)`, `remove(Call<R>)`, `retire(Call<R>)`, `RUNTIME_BURN` | One keyed object, live or retired. `remove` burns the token and relinks the predecessor; `retire` needs no neighbour |
| `KeyedType<R>` | record: `name()`, `headTag()`, `keyIndex()`, `maxKeyBytes()`, `signedKey()`, `cooldownMs()`, ...; `typeId()`, `keyId(byte[] instance, byte[] key)`, `keyOf(R)`, `MAX_ARGUMENT_BYTES` (4,096) | A keyed type's tags, key, bounds, cooldown and window (the generated `<T>_TYPE`) |
| `Relay` | `Outcome submit(byte[] cbor)`; `static of(BackendService)`, `static classify(Result)`; `Answer` (`ACCEPTED`, `REJECTED`, `UNKNOWN`), `Outcome` | Where a keyed operation's attempts are sent (`StateRuntime.Builder.relays`) |

Every keyed operation designates one ordinary (ADA-only, at least 5 ADA) UTxO of the payer and spends it in every
attempt, so at most one attempt can land. A composition with a keyed call does the same; `Compose.designate(ref)`
names the input a page chose before `prepare()`, which refuses a keyed call without one or composed with other calls.

##### MerkleMaps (advanced)

| Class | Description |
|---|---|
| `MerkleSupport` | Runs a contract method with map reads served by a `Prover`, and prepares the map claims for the verifier. `Prover` (interface), `TrieProver` (over a `NodeStore`), `Layout`, `Prepared` |
| `VerifierHandle` | A shared verifier script: `script()`, `rewardAddress()`, `hash()`, `holder()`, `reference()`, `ensure(Account payer)`, `prepare(String payerAddress)` |
| `MapHistory` | `static int rebuild(StateRuntime, String unit)`: replays a unit's map history from the chain into the node store |
| `InMemoryNodeStore` | A `NodeStore` in memory |

See [MerkleMap mirrors](https://joust.julc.dev/apps/map-mirrors/).

##### Internal: snapshots and described contracts

These serve the runtime engine and the prepare service (ADR-0015). Applications do not need them.

| Class | Description |
|---|---|
| `snapshot.Snapshot` | The chain as a call sees it: tip, protocol parameters, UTxOs by address, outputs by reference, scripts. JSON in and out |
| `snapshot.SnapshotBackend` | A CCL `BackendService` answering from a `Snapshot`; throws `Need` for anything missing |
| `snapshot.Need` | What a call needs from the chain next (`kind()`, `key()`) |
| `snapshot.SuppliedProver`, `snapshot.SnapshotNodeStore` | Map proofs and nodes supplied by the caller |
| `described.DescribedContract` | A contract known by its description, compiled script and transitions; runs call requests through the runtime core |
| `described.TransitionFn`, `described.UplcTransitions` | A transition's off-chain meaning, and its implementation by JuLC's VM over the toolchain's transition programs, obtained with `UplcTransitions.verified(manifest, description, script, programs)` (the manifest is checked first); a failed run is the contract's refusal only when it carries the `joust:require` tag |
| `described.TransitionInputs` | Checks every evaluation's inputs against the description's declared types first (ADR-0020); `DescribedContract` wraps its transitions in it |
| `described.ProgramManifest`, `described.CanonicalJson` | The program manifest's format (version 2) and its check (ADR-0020 D8), and the canonical JSON its description hash is over |
| `described.SchemaCodec`, `described.DataFidelity` | JSON and Plutus data by a description's schema |

##### julc-state-server: JoustServer

`public final class JoustServer` (package `org.julclang.state.server`): the prepare service (ADR-0013 D2).

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `static builder(StateRuntime runtime)` | Starts a server over a runtime |
| `start(String host, int port)` | Starts listening (port 0: any free port); returns the server |
| `port()` | The port it listens on |
| `stop()` | Stops it |
| `prepare(JsonNode request)` | Prepares a call request directly (what `POST /api/prepare` does) |

| Builder method | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `contract(Class<?> generatedClient)` | | Serves a generated `<Name>Client` (at least one) |
| `allowOrigin(String origin)` | none | A browser origin allowed by CORS (exact match) |
| `staticFiles(Path dir)` | none | Also serves a built page at `/` (single-page app fallback to `index.html`) |
| `handler(String path, HttpHandler handler)` | none | An extra handler; paths under `/api/` are refused |
| `preparesPerMinute(int)` | 30 | Per-client rate limit on prepares |
| `viewsPerMinute(int)` | 120 | Per-client rate limit on views |
| `concurrentPrepares(int)` | 4 | Prepares running at once |
| `onPrepared(BiConsumer<JsonNode, JsonNode>)` | no-op | Observes each prepared request and answer |
| `build()` | | Fails if no contract is served |

| Endpoint | Body | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/contracts` | | `{ contracts: [deployment...] }` |
| `GET /api/description?contract=<class>` | | The contract's description |
| `POST /api/prepare` | `{ contract, kind, method, instance, object, args, pay: { lovelace, assets }, address }` | `{ cbor, txHash, validTo, signers, plan, instance?, object? }` |
| `POST /api/view` | `{ contract, instance, view, args }` | `{ value }` |

Requests are limited to 64 KiB. `kind` is one of `init`, `action`, `destroy`, `ownedInit`, `ownedAction`,
`ownedDestroy`.

## Reference: JavaScript

### @julclang/state-client

URL: https://joust.julc.dev/reference/state-client/

> **Experimental:** 
The npm path runs JOUST's toolchain and runtime as WebAssembly built with GraalVM Web Image, which is itself experimental. Java with Gradle and cardano-client-lib is the supported, first-class path: see [Quick start: Java](https://joust.julc.dev/start/quick-start-java/).

`@julclang/state-client` is the JavaScript client for JOUST contracts: it encodes calls from a contract's description,
verifies prepared transactions before a CIP-30 wallet signs them, and reads the chain. It has no engine and no Wasm,
so it is what a page bundles. Ledger formats go through cardano-js-sdk (`@cardano-sdk/core` 0.47.1, pinned exactly);
Plutus data through its own model and CBOR (`pdata.js`). Source:
[`js/state-client/src/index.js`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/js/state-client/src/index.js), types in
`src/index.d.ts`.

| Entry point | Contents |
|---|---|
| `@julclang/state-client` | everything below, unless marked otherwise |
| `@julclang/state-client/devwallet` | `devWallet`, `deriveAccount`, `DEVKIT_MNEMONIC` |
| `@julclang/state-client/codegen` | `generate` |
| `@julclang/state-client/ledger` | the cardano-js-sdk adapter (ledger helpers) |
| `@julclang/state-client/pdata` | Plutus data: `Data`, `decodeData`, `encodeData`, `dataHex`, `dataEqual`, `CborError` |
| bin `joust-gen` | generates typed clients from descriptions |

Functions that once took cardano-serialization-lib (`CSL`) as their first argument still accept it, and ignore it.

##### Verification

Each verifier returns `{ problems: string[], report }`; no problems means the wallet may sign.

| Export | Signature | Verifies |
|---|---|---|
| `verifyPrepared` | `await verifyPrepared({ description, deployment, txHex, call, wallet, chain, limits? })` | a creation, action, destroy or owned call (keyed calls go on to `verifyKeyed`) |
| `verifyComposed` | `await verifyComposed({ steps, txHex, wallet, chain, limits? })` | several calls in one transaction; `steps`: `[{ description, deployment, call }]` |
| `verifyIntent` | `await verifyIntent({ description, deployment, txHex, call, wallet, chain, limits? })` | an intent lock (ADR-0004) |
| `verifyCancel` | same | an intent's cancellation |
| `verifyBatch` | same | a batch, from the batcher's side |
| `verifyPurpose` | `await verifyPurpose({ description, deployment, txHex, wallet, chain, op, pool?, amount?, args?, cosignerKeys?, limits? })` | a delegation or a reward collection |
| `verifyRegistration` | `verifyRegistration({ txHex, governor: { hash }, wallet, chain: { params, tip }, networkId, limits? })` | a stake credential's registration |
| `runComposed` | `await runComposed({ service, chain, api, steps, limits?, onReview? })` | prepares, verifies, signs and submits a composition; `steps`: `[{ contract, method, args, pay?, instance, object?, into?, cosigners? }]` |
| `DEFAULT_LIMITS` | constant | the verifiers' limits (below) |

`wallet` is a `walletView`; `chain` is `{ tip, params, utxo }` (the tip slot, protocol parameters, an output reader).

`DEFAULT_LIMITS`:

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `maxCollateral` | `5_000_000n` |
| `maxValiditySlots` | `900` |
| `maxStartSlots` | `60` |
| `maxBackdateSlots` | `120` |
| `feeMargin` | `500_000n` |
| `maxFee` | `3_000_000n` |

Plans and helpers the verifiers use:

| Export | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `planOf` | `planOf(cbor)` | the transaction's plan (ADR-0013 D4): what it spends, reads, creates, mints, runs, requires |
| `planDifference` | `planDifference(a, b, path = 'plan')` | the first difference between two plans, `""` when equal |
| `redeemerDefs` | `redeemerDefs(codec, description)` | the description's spend and mint redeemer definitions |

### @julclang/joust-runtime

URL: https://joust.julc.dev/reference/joust-runtime/

> **Experimental:** 
The npm path runs JOUST's toolchain and runtime as WebAssembly built with GraalVM Web Image, which is itself experimental. Java with Gradle and cardano-client-lib is the supported, first-class path: see [Quick start: Java](https://joust.julc.dev/start/quick-start-java/).

`@julclang/joust-runtime` calls JOUST contracts from JavaScript with no JVM. It holds the **runtime engine**: JOUST's
off-chain runtime compiled to Wasm (a GraalVM Web Image), a pure function of a call request and a snapshot of the
chain, with no I/O and no keys. The JavaScript layer fetches what the engine asks for from a chain provider, keeps
MerkleMap mirrors, and hands the result to `@julclang/state-client`, which verifies it before a wallet signs. Source:
[`js/joust-runtime/src`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/js/joust-runtime/src).

It needs Node 22 or newer; on Node 22 the package enables Wasm exception references itself
(`--experimental-wasm-exnref`, set only where exnref is off, so newer Node prints no warning), so you pass no flag.

| Entry point | Contents |
|---|---|
| `@julclang/joust-runtime` | `joustRuntime`, `engineService`, mirrors, snapshots, DevKit helpers, and re-exports from `@julclang/state-client` |
| `@julclang/joust-runtime/worker` | imported in a module worker, serves the runtime there |
| `@julclang/joust-runtime/page` | `engineWorker`: a prepare service backed by that worker (no dependencies) |
| `@julclang/joust-runtime/load` | `loadImage(jsFile)`: loads a JOUST engine image in Node |

In a browser build, two internal modules switch to their browser twins through `package.json` `imports` with the
`browser` condition: `#engine` (fetches and evaluates the engine with SRI) and `#file-map-store` (throws: no file
system).

##### `joustRuntime(options)`

```js
import { joustRuntime } from '@julclang/joust-runtime';

const rt = joustRuntime({ chainUrl, contracts, clock, networkId: 0, deployments, ttlMs: 20_000 });
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `provider` | `blockfrostProvider(chainUrl, { projectId, fetchImpl })` | a chain provider; backs both the engine's reads and `rt.chain` |
| `chainUrl` | | instead of a provider: a Blockfrost-style API (Blockfrost, Yaci Store's `http://localhost:8080/api/v1`) |
| `projectId` | | Blockfrost's project id, for `chainUrl` |
| `fetchImpl` | `fetch` | the `fetch` for `chainUrl` |
| `contracts` | (required) | `build/joust/contracts.json` |
| `validators` | `[]` | `build/joust/validators.json`: plain JuLC validators, such as governors |
| `clock` | (required) | `{ zeroSlot, zeroTimeMs, slotLengthMs }` |
| `networkId` | `0` | `0` (test networks) or `1` (mainnet) |
| `deployments` | `{}` | `{ [contract]: deployment }`, as `joust deploy` writes them |
| `ttlMs` | `120_000` | how long a prepared transaction stays valid |
| `mapMirror` | a new `mapMirror({ provider })` | MerkleMap mirrors |
| `mapStore` | | instead of mirrors: the earlier node store (`memoryMapStore`, `fileMapStore`) |
| `engine` | this package's `engine/` | where the engine is: `{ dir }` in Node, `{ url, integrity }` in a browser |
| `prefetch` | on | `false` turns off fetching the up-front needs (tip, parameters, wallet, reference scripts, the target UTxO) before the first engine run |
| `record` | | `(fixture) => void`: each prepared call as a replayable fixture (ADR-0015 I3) |
| `CSL` | | ignored (earlier versions read transactions with it) |

Contracts built by an incompatible toolchain are refused when the runtime is made: a description version other than
2, or another major version (another minor while the major is 0) than the runtime's.

###### The runtime

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `provider`, `api` | | the chain provider |
| `chain` | | `chainOf(provider)`: the chain view a client verifies with |
| `service` | | the engine as a prepare service; adds each call's deployment `params` and every pinned reference script to the request; also `deployment`, `publish`, `governor`, `mirror`, `rounds` (as `engineService`) |
| `deployments` | | the deployments by contract title; `ensureDeployment` adds to it |
| `options` | `options(contract, extra = {})` | `{ service, chain, deployment, ...extra }` for a generated client; `contract` is the title or the simple name |
| `ensureDeployment` | `await ensureDeployment(contract, wallet, params?)` | the deployment, publishing the reference script first if needed (checked before signing), and JOUST's map or output verifier when the contract needs one |
| `ensureGovernor` | `await ensureGovernor(name, params, wallet)` | `{ name, script, hash, rewardAddress }`: a plain validator from `validators` with its parameters applied (by name or in order), its stake credential registered once (checked by `verifyRegistration` before signing) |
| `compose` | `compose(wallet, steps, extra = {})` | several calls in one transaction (`runComposed`); `steps`: `[{ contract, method, args, pay?, instance, object?, into?, cosigners? }]`, `extra`: `{ onReview?, limits? }` |

`wallet` is a CIP-30 API object. A governor is used as `opts.governor = { governor, signers }` on the call it approves.

##### `engineService(options)`

The engine as a prepare service, without the deployment handling `joustRuntime` adds. `joustRuntime` builds one.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `api` | (required) | a chain provider, or `blockfrostApi(url)`'s raw API |
| `contracts` | (required) | `contracts.json` |
| `clock` | (required) | the slot clock |
| `networkId` | `0` | |
| `ttlMs` | `120_000` | TTL of prepared transactions |
| `maxRounds` | `64` | chain reads (one per engine run) before giving up |
| `mapMirror` | `mapMirror({ provider: api })` | MerkleMap mirrors |
| `unitsOf` | | `(call) => units`: the tokens a call touches, whose history rebuilds a map |
| `mapStore` | | the earlier node store, instead of mirrors |
| `prefetch` | | `async (call, snapshot) => void`: fills the up-front needs |
| `record` | | fixtures, as above |
| `engine` | | where the engine is |

| Member | Signature | Resolves to |
|---|---|---|
| `prepare` | `prepare(request)` | `{ cbor, txHash, validTo, signers, plan }`, plus `instance` (init), `object` (ownedInit), `created` (intents, batches, compositions) |
| `deployment` | `deployment(contract, address, params?)` | `{ contract, policy, address, networkId, referenceScripts }` |
| `publish` | `publish(contract, address, params?)` | the unsigned transaction publishing the reference script, or `null` if published |
| `governor` | `governor(kind, script, params, address)` | `deployment`: `{ script, hash, rewardAddress }`; `register`: the unsigned registration |
| `mirror` | property | the `mapMirror`, or `null` with a `mapStore` |
| `rounds` | property | how many engine runs each prepare took |

Set `JOUST_DEBUG_NEEDS=1` to log each chain read the engine asks for.

##### The page worker

###### `@julclang/joust-runtime/worker`

Importing it in a module worker makes the worker serve the runtime:

```js title="page/engine.worker.js"
import '@julclang/joust-runtime/worker';
```

It announces `{ joust: 'listening' }` once it takes messages, then answers `{ id, op, args }` messages with
`{ id, ok: true, value }` or `{ id, ok: false, error }`. Its operations are what `engineWorker` calls: `init`,
`prepare`, `mapValue` and `deployments`.

###### `engineWorker(worker, options)`

From `@julclang/joust-runtime/page`:

```js
import { engineWorker } from '@julclang/joust-runtime/page';

const service = engineWorker(new Worker(new URL('./engine.worker.js', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' }), options);
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `engine` | `{ url, integrity: { script, wasm } }`: where `joust-runtime.js` is served, its `.wasm` beside it, and their sha384 SRI hashes; a plain URL loads unchecked |
| `contracts` | `contracts.json` |
| `validators` | `validators.json` (optional) |
| `chain` | a Blockfrost-style chain API, absolute or relative to the page |
| `projectId` | a project id, only for a chain API that needs one and may see it |
| `clock`, `networkId`, `ttlMs` | as for `joustRuntime` |
| `deployments` | `{ [contract]: deployment }` |
| `mirrorCache` | the IndexedDB database for mirrors (default `"joust-mirrors"`); `false`: in memory |

`virtual:joust/network` from `@julclang/joust/vite` has every one of these fields.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ready` | promise | resolves once the engine has loaded |
| `prepare` | `prepare(request)` | as a prepare service |
| `mapValue` | `mapValue(root, key, units = [])` | a MerkleMap value (hex), or `null` when absent; rebuilds an unknown root from the history of `units` |
| `deployments` | `deployments(d)` | new deployments for the calls that follow |
| `terminate` | `terminate()` | stops the worker; pending and later calls reject |

See [Pages](https://joust.julc.dev/apps/pages/).

###### `loadEngine(o)`

`loadEngine({ dir })` in Node, `loadEngine({ url, integrity })` in a browser: the engine's API, loaded once per process
or worker. `joustRuntime` calls it; you rarely need it.

##### MerkleMap mirrors

| Export | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `mapMirror` | `mapMirror({ provider?, cache? } = {})` | mirrors over Aiken's MPF: `get(root, key)`, `known(root)`, `answer(need, units)`, `stage(txHex)`, `sync(unit)`, `states` |
| `levelMirrorCache` | `await levelMirrorCache(location)` | a persistent cache over `level`: LevelDB in Node (a directory), IndexedDB in browsers (a name); `close()` |
| `claimsOf` | `claimsOf(data)` | the map claims in a map-verifier redeemer (Plutus data), or `null` |
| `EMPTY_ROOT` | constant | the empty map's root: 32 zero bytes, hex |
| `memoryMapStore` | `memoryMapStore(initial = {})` | the earlier node store, in memory |
| `fileMapStore` | `fileMapStore(file)` | the earlier node store, in a JSON file (Node only) |

See [MerkleMap mirrors](https://joust.julc.dev/apps/map-mirrors/).

##### Snapshots and providers

| Export | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `blockfrostApi` | `blockfrostApi(baseUrl, { projectId?, fetchImpl? })` | raw reads `{ base, get(path, { allow404 }), provider }` (kept for earlier callers) |
| `asProvider` | `asProvider(source)` | a provider for a provider or a `blockfrostApi` |
| `emptySnapshot` | `emptySnapshot()` | `{ utxos, assetUtxos, outputs, absent, scripts }` |
| `fetchNeed` | `await fetchNeed(source, snapshot, kind, key)` | fetches one engine need (`tip`, `protocolParams`, `utxos`, `assetUtxos`, `output`, `script`) into a snapshot |
| `utxoJson` | `utxoJson(utxo)` | a provider's UTxO in Blockfrost's JSON, the snapshot's format |

A keyed insert or remove ([keyed objects](https://joust.julc.dev/apps/keyed-objects-js/)) needs
the whole listing of the contract's state address, so the runtime fetches it before asking the engine. For a
keyed contract, `ensureDeployment` and `rt.options(...)` also pin the slot clock in the deployment (`slotConfig`),
which the page verifier requires for keyed calls.

##### DevKit helpers

For Yaci DevKit: its admin API defaults to `http://localhost:10000`.

| Export | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `devkitClock` | `await devkitClock(adminUrl?, { fetchImpl? })` | the DevKit's slot clock |
| `devkitTopUp` | `await devkitTopUp(address, ada, adminUrl?, { chain?, fetchImpl? })` | funds an address from the faucet; with `chain`, from the default mnemonic's genesis accounts when the faucet is dry |
| `devkitMint` | `await devkitMint(chain, wallet, name, quantity)` | mints a test token under a single-key native script of the wallet's key; `{ policy, unit }` |
| `devkitSweep` | `await devkitSweep(chain, wallet)` | moves what contracts sent to the wallet key's enterprise address to its base address; the hash, or `null` |
| `devWallet`, `deriveAccount`, `DEVKIT_MNEMONIC` | | re-exported from `@julclang/state-client/devwallet` |

##### Re-exports from `@julclang/state-client`

`JoustContract`, `VerificationError`, `blockfrostChain`, `chainOf`, `blockfrostProvider`, `ogmiosProvider`, `toJson`,
`runComposed`, `verifyComposed`. See [`@julclang/state-client`](https://joust.julc.dev/reference/state-client/).

##### `@julclang/joust-runtime/load`

`loadImage(jsFile)` loads a JOUST engine image (a GraalVM Web Image on julc-wasm) in Node, serialising loads across
every engine in the process, since images announce themselves through one global callback (`onJulcReady`). The
toolchain in `@julclang/joust` loads through it too.
