### @julclang/joust (CLI, Vite)

URL: https://joust.julc.dev/reference/joust-cli/

> **Experimental:** 
The npm path runs JOUST's toolchain and runtime as WebAssembly built with GraalVM Web Image, which is itself experimental. Java with Gradle and cardano-client-lib is the supported, first-class path: see [Quick start: Java](https://joust.julc.dev/start/quick-start-java/).

`@julclang/joust` is JOUST's command line and Vite plugin. It carries the **toolchain engine**: JOUST's annotation
processor and JuLC's compiler, compiled to Wasm, which build `.java` and `.jsc` contracts in Node exactly as the
Gradle build does. Source: [`js/joust`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/js/joust). For a guided tour, see
[The joust CLI and projects](https://joust.julc.dev/apps/cli-and-projects/). It needs Node 22 or newer.

| Entry point | Contents |
|---|---|
| bin `joust` | the CLI |
| `@julclang/joust` | `build`, `deploy`, `loadConfig`, `network`, `loadToolchain`, `VERSION` (the commands as functions) |
| `@julclang/joust/vite` | the Vite plugin, `joust(options)` (also the default export) |

##### Commands

Every command reads `joust.config.json` from the working directory (see [`joust.config.json`](https://joust.julc.dev/reference/config/)).
`--network <name>` defaults to the config's `network` (`devkit`).

| Command | Flags | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `joust build` | `--src <dir>` (default config `contracts`), `--out <dir>` (default config `out`), `--accept-abi`, `--accept-lock`, `--traces` | compiles every `.java` and `.jsc` file under the source folder into the output folder, with the libraries of the project's npm packages (`joust-lib/`); exits 1 on a compile error, on a `.jsc` ABI manifest that is missing or changed unless `--accept-abi` writes it ([the ABI manifest](https://joust.julc.dev/languages/jsc/#the-abi-manifest)), or on a library from a package that `joust.lock` does not pin at its hash unless `--accept-lock` writes it ([library packages](https://joust.julc.dev/languages/jsc-reference/#library-packages-and-joustlock)). `--traces` keeps the contracts' traces in the scripts (larger scripts; for debugging) |
| `joust fmt` | `[--check]`, `[<file or dir>...]` (default: the configured contracts directory, only inside the project) | formats `.jsc` files in place, changing only whitespace (style version 1: [editors](https://joust.julc.dev/languages/editors/)). A file that does not parse, is not valid UTF-8, or is read-only is refused and left as it was; a formatted file keeps its permissions. `--check` writes nothing and lists the files that are not formatted. Exits 0 formatted (with `--check`: already was), 1 not formatted (`--check`), 2 a file refused, 3 a usage error. Gradle projects use `JscMain --fmt [--check]`, with the same codes |
| `joust test` | `[-- <node --test args>]` | builds, then runs `test/*.test.js` with Node's test runner (one file at a time). Tests that use `@julclang/joust/test` run offline: see [offline tests](#offline-tests) |
| `joust deploy` | `--network <name>` | publishes each contract's reference script (once) and writes `<out>/deployments.<network>.json` |
| `joust dev` | `--network <name>`, `--port <port>` (default config `dev.port`, else 5178), `--accept-abi` | attaches to the chain (starting it with the network's `start` command if needed), builds, deploys, serves the page; rebuilds and redeploys on save |
| `joust serve` | `--network <name>`, `--dir <dir>` (default `dist`), `--port <port>` (default as `dev`) | serves a built page as static files, with the chain API at `/chain` and on DevKit the faucet |
| `joust version` | (also `joust --version`, `-V`, `-v`) | prints `joust <version> (npm)` |
| `joust help` | (also `--help`, `-h`, `<command> --help`) | the usage; never runs a command |
| `joust new` | | prints the `npm create joust` command to run (Gradle projects come from the native `joust`); creates nothing |

In a project, a project command (`build`, `test`, `deploy`, `dev`, `serve`) runs at the project's root (the nearest directory
with `joust.config.json`, or a `package.json` that depends on `@julclang/joust`), and by the project's own
`@julclang/joust`: a global or other copy hands over to it, as [the native `joust`](#the-native-joust) does.

`joust` with no command prints the usage; an unknown command prints it and exits 1. Errors are printed as
`joust: <message>` with exit status 1. `joust dev` and `joust serve` bind to `127.0.0.1` and stop on `SIGINT` or
`SIGTERM`.

###### Outputs of `joust build`

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `contracts.json` | `[{ description, script, transitions, manifest, built: { joust } }]` for the runtime |
| `<Contract>.json` | the description (CIP-57 + `x-joust`, version 2) |
| `<Contract>.plutus` | the validator, CBOR hex |
| `<Contract>.js`, `<Contract>.d.ts` | the typed client and its types |
| `generated/<package path>/<Contract>.java`, `.jscmap.json` | the Java a `.jsc` file lowered to, and its source map (`.jsc` only) |
| `validators.json` | plain JuLC validators: `[{ name, package, purpose, script, scriptHash, params, built }]` (only if there are any) |
| `<Validator>.plutus` | each plain validator's script, parameters not applied |
| `joust.lock.json` | `{ joust, descriptionVersion, contracts: { <title>: { scriptHash } }, validators? }` |

###### Offline tests

`@julclang/joust/test` runs a project's contracts without a chain (ADR-0018 D14):

```js
import { offline } from '@julclang/joust/test';
import contracts from '../build/joust/contracts.json' with { type: 'json' };
import { Counter } from '../build/joust/Counter.js';

const net = await offline({ contracts });
const owner = await net.wallet(100);                       // a funded key wallet, in ADA
const counter = new Counter(await net.options('app.Counter', owner));
const { instance } = await counter.deploy(owner, {});
await instance.increment(owner, { by: 5n });
assert.deepEqual(net.ledger.acceptedAttacks(), []);        // every mutation of the offline attack suite was refused
```

`net.ledger` is an in-memory ledger behind the same provider interface as Yaci Store or Blockfrost. Before it applies
a transaction it checks these phase-1 rules (each refusal names the node's error):

- the transaction is tagged valid, is at most `max_tx_size` bytes, and its inputs, reference inputs and collateral exist
  and are unspent; at protocol versions 9 and 10 an output is not both spent and referenced (the ledger lifts that at 11);
- the validity interval holds at the ledger's slot (`ledger.advance(ms)` moves its clock);
- withdrawals come from registered reward accounts and take exactly their balance (always 0: no rewards are paid);
- the transaction balances, with the fee and the deposits, and every output holds its minimum ADA, the collateral
  return included;
- the fee is at least the size's, the declared execution units' and the reference scripts' fee;
- every key that must sign has a verifying witness, every script credential that must authorise (a script-locked input,
  a mint policy, a script withdrawal or certificate) has its script, witnessed or referenced; native scripts are
  evaluated; each Plutus purpose has a redeemer and no redeemer is extra; a Plutus-locked input's datum hash has its
  datum (a key-locked output with a datum hash needs none), and a witness datum is either needed or named by an output
  (the collateral return included) or a reference input;
- certificates: a stake registration (once, paying `key_deposit`) and a deregistration (when registered, refunding the
  deposit held); a certificate that states another amount is refused;
- with Plutus scripts: the collateral is key-locked, at most `max_collateral_inputs`, ADA only unless returned, at least
  `collateral_percent` of the fee, and matches `total_collateral` when it is declared; the script integrity hash
  matches; the declared units are within the per-transaction limit;
- phase 2: every Plutus script that must run, evaluated by the runtime engine (`joust.evaluate`, the evaluator that
  prices transactions), within its redeemer's declared units.

Concurrent submissions are applied one at a time. A transaction carrying what the ledger does not model is refused
(`NotModelled`): votes, proposals, treasury donations and values, and every certificate but stake registration and
deregistration (delegation to a pool or a DRep, DRep, committee and pool certificates); test those on DevKit. Not modelled otherwise: rewards (withdrawals take 0), PlutusV1's integrity hash, and the collateral loss of a
failing script (an invalid-tagged transaction is refused; a failing script refuses the whole transaction).

A refusal is a `LedgerRefusal`. For each transaction a script ran in, the ledger also runs the attack suite
(`joust.attacks`, a subset of the JVM testkit's `Attacks`) on it: the state datum replaced or hashed, one lovelace
skimmed, token dust added, the output sent to a key address or given a stake credential, the output dropped, the
required signer replaced, the validity bounds moved or removed. Only a script's refusal counts as refused; any other
failure of a mutation is reported as accepted, with its reason, so that it fails the test. `ledger.attacks()` lists
every attack with its outcome; `ledger.acceptedAttacks()` lists those the scripts accepted, which should be none. Pass
`{ attacks: false }` to `offline` to skip the suite. `joust test` runs offline: a network provider (Blockfrost, Yaci
Store, Ogmios) refuses to start under it.

The template's `test/counter.test.js` is such a test: `npm test` runs `joust test`. Its DevKit test is in `test/devkit/`.

###### `joust deploy`

`<out>/deployments.<network>.json` is `{ network, networkId, chain, clock, contracts: { <title>: deployment } }`, each
deployment `{ contract, policy, address, networkId, referenceScripts }` plus `params`, `mapVerifier` and
`outputVerifier` when the contract has them. The deployer is `JOUST_MNEMONIC`'s key; without it, on a network with an
`admin` API (DevKit), a key kept in `.joust/<network>-wallet.json`, topped up with 1000 ADA when it holds less than
200 ADA. A contract with `@Params` is deployed with the config's `params` for it (by title or simple name) and skipped
without them.

##### Environment variables

| Variable | Read by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `JOUST_MNEMONIC` | `joust deploy`, `joust dev` | the deployer's mnemonic; required on networks without an `admin` API |
| `BLOCKFROST_PREVIEW_PROJECT_ID` | any command on `preview` | the Blockfrost project id (the built-in `preview`'s `projectIdEnv`) |
| (a network's `projectIdEnv`) | any command on that network | its chain API's project id |
| `JOUST_NETWORK` | the Vite plugin, in `vite build` | the network a build is for, unless the plugin's `network` option names one |
| `JOUST_VITE_LOG` | `joust dev` | Vite's log level (default `warn`); `info` shows dependency bundling and reloads |
| `JOUST_DEBUG_NEEDS` | `@julclang/joust-runtime` | logs each chain read the engine asks for |

A command on a network whose `projectIdEnv` is not set stops and names the variable.

##### The dev server

`joust dev` serves one origin (default `http://127.0.0.1:5178`):

| Route | Method | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| `/chain/<path>` | GET, POST (`/chain/tx/submit`) | the network's chain API, proxied with its project id; one upstream session (Blockfrost's affinity cookie) |
| `/joust/network.json` | GET | `{ network, networkId, chain: "/chain", engine: { url, integrity: { script, wasm } }, contracts: "/joust/contracts.json", service: "/joust/service", clock, ttlMs, explorer, deployments }` |
| `/joust/engine/<file>` | GET | the runtime engine (`joust-runtime.js`, `joust-runtime.js.wasm`), streamed, with an ETag |
| `/joust/service/prepare` | POST | the engine in the dev server as a prepare service (`httpService('/joust/service')`); 422 `{ error }` on a contract's refusal |
| `/joust/<file>` | GET | files of the build folder |
| `/dev/topup` | POST `{ address, ada? }` | DevKit only: funds the address from the faucet (default 1000 ADA) |
| anything else | | the page: Vite in middleware mode when the project has `vite` and an `index.html` in the page folder, else the page folder's files |

Responses carry `access-control-allow-origin: *`. The page folder is the config's `page`, else `page/` if it exists,
else the project root.

`joust serve` answers `/chain/<path>`, `/dev/topup` (DevKit only) and the files of its folder (`/` is `index.html`).
It has no `/joust` routes.

##### The Vite plugin

```js title="vite.config.js"
import { joust } from '@julclang/joust/vite';

export default { root: 'page', plugins: [joust({ root: process.cwd() })] };
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `root` | the working directory | the project: where `joust.config.json` and the build folder are |
| `network` | `JOUST_NETWORK`, else Vite's mode if it names a network, else the config's `network` | the network a `vite build` is for |

It returns a list of plugins that:

- alias Node's `buffer`, `events`, `util`, `stream`, `process` and `assert` to browser versions, resolved from the
  plugin's own package by absolute path, and inject the `Buffer` (one class, `src/shims/buffer.js`) and `process`
  globals;
- set `global` to `globalThis` and target es2022 for the dev server's dependency bundling and for builds;
- build workers as ES modules with the same aliases and globals (injected `post` in workers);
- scan `**/*.html` and `**/*.worker.{js,mjs,ts}` for dependencies (unless the config sets `optimizeDeps.entries`), and
  pre-bundle `node:buffer`;
- allow the project root in `server.fs.allow`, so a page imports `build/joust/*.js`;
- provide `virtual:joust/network`.

`vite-plugin-node-polyfills` and `@rollup/plugin-inject` are dependencies of the package; `vite` (5 or newer) is an
optional peer dependency.

###### `virtual:joust/network`

The default export, in a build:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `network` | the network's name |
| `networkId` | the network's `networkId`, else the deployments file's |
| `chain` | the network's `pageChain`, else `"/chain"` |
| `clock` | the deployments file's clock, else the network's |
| `ttlMs` | the config's `dev.ttlMs`, else 20 000 on a DevKit, 180 000 elsewhere |
| `explorer` | the network's `explorer`, or `null` |
| `deployments` | the deployments file's `contracts` |
| `contracts` | `contracts.json` |
| `validators` | `validators.json`, or `[]` |
| `engine` | `{ url: "<base>joust/engine-<id>/joust-runtime.js", integrity: { script, wasm } }` |

A build emits the engine's two files to `joust/engine-<id>/` (`id`: 8 hex characters from the files' hashes) and fails
without `contracts.json` or `deployments.<network>.json`. Under `joust dev`, the module instead fetches
`/joust/network.json` and then its `contracts` when the page loads (the fields of the dev server's `network.json`,
above).

##### The native `joust`

ADR-0017 adds a native `joust` (no Node, no JDK needed to run it): `brew install bloxbean/tap/joust`, or the release
archives (macOS arm64, Linux x86_64 and arm64). It creates projects and hands project commands to the project:

| Command | Native `joust` |
|---|---|
| `joust new <dir> [-t gradle\|node\|web] [-l java\|jsc] [-p <package>]` | `gradle` (default, `java` by default): a Gradle project with the plugin `org.julclang.joust`; `node`, `web`: what `npm create joust` writes, fetched with `npm pack create-joust@<its version>` and run by its own `node`, isolated from the directory's npm configuration |
| `joust version` | `joust <version> (native)`, and in an npm project `project: @julclang/joust <version> (npm)` |
| `joust help`, `<command> --help` | the usage; never runs a command |
| any other command, in an npm project | the project's own `@julclang/joust` (`node_modules`), at the project's root, with the arguments unchanged and its exit code; `run npm install first` if it is missing, never a stand-in |
| `joust build`, `test`, `run`, in a Gradle build | the build's `./gradlew <task>` (a subproject's directory selects the subproject); `deploy`, `dev` and `serve` explain that they are npm commands |

Both `joust` commands answer `new`, `version` and `help` themselves, and both hand project commands to the project's
own `@julclang/joust`. So `joust build` does the same, whichever binary `PATH` finds. Install the native one globally and
`@julclang/joust` per project (both global at once is not supported: with Homebrew's Node they share one path).

The walk up to a project does not enter directories owned by another user (a planted `package.json` in `/tmp` is
ignored); list directories you trust, such as a container bind mount, in `JOUST_SAFE_DIRS` (`:`-separated). Both CLIs
apply this rule, as git's `safe.directory` does: in a container or CI job that runs as another user than the one owning
the checkout (for example root over a mounted workspace), run as its owner, or set `JOUST_SAFE_DIRS`. Its entries are
absolute paths and trust those exact directories, not their subdirectories: `JOUST_SAFE_DIRS=/workspace` works for
`joust build` run in `/workspace`; run from `/workspace/contracts`, list that directory too. Otherwise `joust build`
reports that it found no project.

To check a downloaded archive before using it: `shasum -a 256 -c joust-<version>-SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing`, then
`gh attestation verify joust-<version>-<platform>.zip -R bloxbean/joust`; on macOS, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine joust`
(the binary is not notarized; Homebrew installs need none of this).

##### `create-joust`

```sh
npm create joust@latest [dir] -- [--template node|web] [--lang jsc|java]
```

Writes a new project into `dir` (default `joust-app`), which must be empty or absent, and names the package after the
folder. Every project has a `Counter` contract, `joust.config.json` for DevKit, a DevKit test
(`test/counter.test.js`) and `.gitignore`.

| Option | Values |
|---|---|
| `--template`, `-t` | `node` (default): `index.js`, a Node script that deploys and calls the contract; scripts `start`, `build`, `deploy`, `test`. `web`: a page (`page/`) with the Cardano Foundation's connect button and an in-page DevKit key, and `vite.config.js`; the scripts listed under [A browser page](https://joust.julc.dev/start/quick-start-npm/#a-browser-page) |
| `--lang`, `-l` | `jsc` (default): `contracts/app/Counter.jsc` in `.jsc` (a language preview), with its ABI manifest `Counter.abi.json`. `java`: `contracts/app/Counter.java`. Both give the same description and client |
| `--help`, `-h` | the usage |

Options go after `--` with `npm create` (npm passes them on); `npx create-joust my-app --lang java` takes them
directly.

##### Functions

The commands are also functions, for scripts and tests:

| Export | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `build` | `await build({ root?, src?, out?, options?, log?, keep? })` | `{ ok, contracts, validators, diagnostics }` |
| `deploy` | `await deploy({ root?, config, networkName?, log?, fetchImpl? })` | the deployments written |
| `loadConfig` | `loadConfig(root = process.cwd())` | the config, merged over the defaults |
| `network` | `await network(config, name?)` | the network with its clock resolved (a DevKit's from its admin API) and `projectId` read |
| `loadToolchain` | `loadToolchain({ dir? } = {})` | the toolchain engine (`engine.joust.build({ files, options })`) |
| `VERSION` | constant | the package version |

##### Next steps

  - [joust.config.json](https://joust.julc.dev/reference/config/)
  - [The joust CLI and projects](https://joust.julc.dev/apps/cli-and-projects/)
  - [Pages: worker, Vite, static builds](https://joust.julc.dev/apps/pages/)
  - [@julclang/joust-runtime](https://joust.julc.dev/reference/joust-runtime/)

### joust.config.json

URL: https://joust.julc.dev/reference/config/

> **Experimental:** 
The npm path runs JOUST's toolchain and runtime as WebAssembly built with GraalVM Web Image, which is itself experimental. Java with Gradle and cardano-client-lib is the supported, first-class path: see [Quick start: Java](https://joust.julc.dev/start/quick-start-java/).

`joust.config.json`, at the project's root, tells the `joust` CLI and the Vite plugin where the contracts are, where
the build goes, which networks to use and how to deploy. Every key is optional: a missing file means the defaults.
The source of truth is [`js/joust/src/config.js`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/js/joust/src/config.js);
this page lists every key the package reads.

The template's config:

```json title="joust.config.json"
{
  "contracts": "contracts",
  "out": "build/joust",
  "network": "devkit",
  "networks": {
    "devkit": { "chain": "http://localhost:8080/api/v1", "admin": "http://localhost:10000", "networkId": 0 }
  }
}
```

##### Top-level keys

| Key | Default | Read by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `contracts` | `"contracts"` | `build`, `dev` | the folder of `.java` and `.jsc` sources (`dev` watches it) |
| `out` | `"build/joust"` | every command, the Vite plugin | the build folder: `contracts.json`, clients, deployments |
| `network` | `"devkit"` | every command, the Vite plugin | the default network; `--network` overrides it |
| `networks` | `devkit`, `preview` | every command, the Vite plugin | the networks, by name (below) |
| `params` | none | `deploy`, `dev` | `@Params` values per contract, by full title or simple name: `{ "<contract>": { ... } }` in the description's JSON form |
| `dev.port` | `5178` | `dev`, `serve` | the port to serve on; `--port` overrides it |
| `dev.ttlMs` | 20 000 on a DevKit, 180 000 elsewhere | `dev`, the Vite plugin | the TTL of transactions prepared for pages (the page worker, `joust dev`'s prepare service) |
| `page` | `"page"` if it exists, else `"."` | `dev` | the page folder `joust dev` serves (with Vite when it holds `index.html` and the project has `vite`) |

`joust build`'s `--src` and `--out` flags override `contracts` and `out` for one run.

##### Networks

Each entry of `networks` describes one chain:

| Key | Default | Read by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | (required) | every command | a Blockfrost-style chain API: Blockfrost, or Yaci Store's `/api/v1`. `dev` and `serve` probe it and proxy it at `/chain` |
| `networkId` | none (runtimes then use `0`) | every command, the Vite plugin | `0` for test networks, `1` for mainnet; give it always |
| `admin` | none | every command | a Yaci DevKit admin API. Marks the network as a DevKit: its clock is read from it, `deploy` may use a local key topped up from its faucet, `/dev/topup` is served, and page TTLs are short |
| `clock` | from `admin` | every command, the Vite plugin | `{ "zeroSlot", "zeroTimeMs", "slotLengthMs" }`; required when there is no `admin` |
| `projectIdEnv` | none | every command | the environment variable holding the chain API's project id (sent as the `project_id` header); a command stops if it is not set |
| `projectId` | none | every command | the project id itself, when `projectIdEnv` is not given. Avoid it: the config file is easy to commit |
| `explorer` | none | `dev`, the Vite plugin | a block explorer's transaction page, `{tx}` standing for the hash; pages link their transactions there |
| `pageChain` | `"/chain"` | the Vite plugin | the chain API a **built** page calls: a URL a browser may use directly. Without it, the page uses `/chain` on its own origin |
| `start` | none | `dev`, `serve` | a shell command that starts the network when its APIs do not answer (for example `"yaci-devkit up --enable-yaci-store"`); they wait up to three minutes |
| `provider` | Blockfrost-style | `deploy` | `"ogmios"` makes `joust deploy` read the chain through Ogmios |
| `ogmios` | `"http://localhost:1337"` | `deploy` | Ogmios' URL, with `"provider": "ogmios"` |

> **Ogmios is for deploy only:** 
`provider` and `ogmios` change only how `joust deploy` reads the chain. `joust dev` and `joust serve` always attach to
the network's `chain` and proxy it at `/chain`, and their runtimes read it. In your own code, pass
`ogmiosProvider(url)` to `joustRuntime({ provider })`.

##### Built-in networks

```js title="js/joust/src/config.js"
export const DEFAULTS = {
  contracts: 'contracts',
  out: 'build/joust',
  network: 'devkit',
  networks: {
    // Yaci DevKit: Yaci Store's Blockfrost-compatible API, and the admin API (slot clock, faucet).
    devkit: { chain: 'http://localhost:8080/api/v1', admin: 'http://localhost:10000', networkId: 0,
      explorer: 'http://localhost:5173/transactions/{tx}' },   // DevKit's Yaci Viewer
    // Cardano preview through Blockfrost (its project id from the environment, never the config). Clock from preview's
    // genesis: system start 1666656000, one-second slots from slot 0 (checked against the tip, 2026-11-08).
    preview: {
      chain: 'https://cardano-preview.blockfrost.io/api/v0', projectIdEnv: 'BLOCKFROST_PREVIEW_PROJECT_ID', networkId: 0,
      clock: { zeroSlot: 0, zeroTimeMs: 1666656000000, slotLengthMs: 1000 },
      explorer: 'https://preview.cardanoscan.io/transaction/{tx}',
    },
  },
};
```

##### The merge rule

`loadConfig` merges in two levels:

1. **Top level:** the project's keys replace the defaults' (`{ ...DEFAULTS, ...config }`). Keys the defaults do not
   have, such as `params`, `dev` and `page`, are taken as they are.
2. **Networks:** each network in the project's `networks` is merged **over the built-in network of the same name**,
   key by key (`{ ...builtIn, ...yours }`). Networks you do not mention stay as built in; a new name is taken as it is.

So this config keeps all of DevKit's built-in keys, adds `start`, and leaves `preview` untouched:

```json title="joust.config.json"
{
  "networks": {
    "devkit": { "start": "yaci-devkit up --enable-yaci-store" }
  }
}
```

The merge is shallow within a network: giving `clock` replaces the whole clock object.

##### Resolving a network

When a command uses a network, `network(config, name)`:

1. fails with `no network <name> in joust.config.json` if it is not defined;
2. takes its `clock`, or reads it from its `admin` API, or fails with
   `network <name>: give its clock { zeroSlot, zeroTimeMs, slotLengthMs } in joust.config.json`;
3. reads the project id from the variable `projectIdEnv` names (failing if it is unset), else takes `projectId`.

`joust dev` and `joust serve` first check that the chain API answers (`/blocks/latest`) and, for a DevKit, that the
admin API does, running `start` if they do not.

##### Next steps

  - [Networks and chain providers](https://joust.julc.dev/apps/networks-and-providers/)
  - [@julclang/joust (CLI, Vite)](https://joust.julc.dev/reference/joust-cli/)
  - [Deploy to preview](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/deploy-preview/)
  - [The joust CLI and projects](https://joust.julc.dev/apps/cli-and-projects/)

## Reference

### Contract description

URL: https://joust.julc.dev/reference/description-format/

Every `@StateContract` (and every `.jsc` contract) gets a **description**: one JSON document that tells a client
everything it needs to encode calls, decode state and verify a prepared transaction, without the Java classes. The
JavaScript client, the typed clients `joust-gen` writes, the runtime engine, the prepare service and the JVM's
described dispatcher all read it.

The description is a [CIP-57](https://joust.julc.dev/reference/glossary/#cip-57) blueprint (`preamble`, `validators`, `definitions`) with
one extra key, `x-joust`, that describes the contract's model: its creations, actions, views, owned types, policies,
intents and purposes. This page documents every key, as `DescriptionWriter` writes it
([`julc-state-processor/.../gen/DescriptionWriter.java`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/julc-state-processor/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/processor/gen/DescriptionWriter.java)).

##### Where it is written

**Java:**

The annotation processor writes the description as a class-output resource:

```text
META-INF/joust/<package>.<Contract>.json
```

In a Gradle module it lands in `build/classes/java/main/META-INF/joust/` and ships inside the jar. For example,
`examples/counter` produces `META-INF/joust/org.julclang.state.examples.counter.Counter.json`.

**.jsc:**

A `.jsc` contract is lowered to a Java `@StateContract` first, so it gets the same description from the processor
(Gradle) or from the toolchain (npm). `examples/dsl` writes descriptions for `Jar`, `Points` and `Guards`.

**JavaScript:**

`joust build` (from `@julclang/joust`) compiles `contracts/**/*.java` and `*.jsc` into `build/joust/`:

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `<Contract>.json` | The description (CIP-57 plus `x-joust` version 2) |
| `<Contract>.plutus` | The compiled validator, CBOR hex |
| `<Contract>.js`, `<Contract>.d.ts` | The typed client (`joust-gen`), with the description inlined |
| `contracts.json` | What the runtime loads: `[{ description, script, transitions, manifest, built: { joust } }]` |
| `joust.lock.json` | The versions that built it, including `descriptionVersion: 2` |

The Gradle build and the npm toolchain run the same generators, so they produce the same description byte for byte
(`ToolchainParityTest` checks it). See [The joust CLI and projects](https://joust.julc.dev/apps/cli-and-projects/).

> **Note:** 
Deployment facts (the applied policy, the script address, the reference-script UTxOs, the network) are **not** in
the description. `joust deploy` writes them separately, to `build/joust/deployments.<network>.json`. A description is
the same on every network.

##### A real description

This is the description of `examples/counter`'s `Counter`, a state of `count` and `owner` with an `increment` anyone
may call, a `reset` and a `close` for the owner, and a `count` view. The file has about 430 lines; the parts below are
taken from it unchanged, with repeated entries left out.

```java title="examples/counter/src/main/java/org/julclang/state/examples/counter/Counter.java"
@StateContract(maxDatumBytes = 128)
public class Counter {
    public record State(BigInteger count, byte[] owner) {}

    @Init public static State init(Ctx ctx) { ... }
    @Action public static State increment(State s, BigInteger by) { ... }
    @Action @OnlyOwner public static State reset(State s) { ... }
    @Destroy @OnlyOwner public static JulcList<Payout> close(State s, Ctx ctx) { ... }
    @View public static BigInteger count(State s) { ... }
}
```

The CIP-57 part: the mint validator takes the `Lifecycle` redeemer, the spend validator takes the state as its datum
and the `Calls` redeemer.

```json title="build/classes/java/main/META-INF/joust/org.julclang.state.examples.counter.Counter.json (preamble, validators)"
{
  "preamble": {
    "title": "org.julclang.state.examples.counter.Counter",
    "description": "JOUST contract Counter (ADR-0013 D3)",
    "version": "0.0.0",
    "plutusVersion": "v3",
    "compiler": { "name": "joust" }
  },
  "validators": [
    {
      "title": "CounterValidator.mint",
      "redeemer": { "title": "redeemer",
        "schema": { "$ref": "#/definitions/org.julclang.state.examples.counter.CounterValidator.Lifecycle" } }
    },
    {
      "title": "CounterValidator.spend",
      "datum": { "title": "datum",
        "schema": { "$ref": "#/definitions/org.julclang.state.examples.counter.Counter.State" } },
      "redeemer": { "title": "redeemer",
        "schema": { "$ref": "#/definitions/org.julclang.state.examples.counter.CounterValidator.Calls" } }
    }
  ]
}
```

The model: `x-joust` with the `reset` action (an `@OnlyOwner` action, so `signedBy` names the state's `owner` field,
at index 1 of `State`).

```json title="x-joust (creations and two actions left out)"
{
  "version": 2,
  "contract": "Counter",
  "package": "org.julclang.state.examples.counter",
  "validator": "CounterValidator",
  "client": "CounterClient",
  "state": { "$ref": "#/definitions/org.julclang.state.examples.counter.Counter.State" },
  "stakeSelf": false,
  "minAda": 2200000,
  "maxDatumBytes": 128,
  "assetAware": false,
  "owned": [],
  "actions": [
    {
      "name": "reset",
      "kind": "action",
      "redeemer": { "purpose": "spend", "constructor": "Reset", "index": 1 },
      "fields": [],
      "args": [],
      "ctx": false,
      "payable": false,
      "takesAssets": false,
      "policies": {
        "signedBy": ["owner"], "validAfter": [], "validBefore": [], "quorum": null, "authorizedBy": [],
        "shared": false, "into": false, "admits": null, "receives": false, "batched": false, "migrateTo": null
      },
      "returns": {
        "state": true, "payouts": false, "sends": false, "mint": false,
        "accepted": false, "events": false, "deposits": false
      },
      "needsService": false,
      "recipe": {
        "transition": "reset",
        "redeemerFields": [],
        "target": "org.julclang.state.examples.counter.Counter.State",
        "shared": false,
        "signers": [{ "field": "owner", "index": 1 }],
        "validAfter": [],
        "validBefore": [],
        "params": false,
        "reads": [],
        "transitionArgs": [],
        "stepEvents": false
      }
    }
  ],
  "views": [
    { "name": "count", "returns": { "dataType": "integer" }, "args": [] }
  ]
}
```

The types: every record, sealed interface and generated redeemer, keyed by its fully qualified Java name.

```json title="definitions (Ctx, TxOutRef and Lifecycle left out)"
{
  "org.julclang.state.examples.counter.CounterValidator.Calls": {
    "title": "Calls",
    "anyOf": [
      { "title": "Increment", "dataType": "constructor", "index": 0,
        "fields": [{ "title": "by", "dataType": "integer" }] },
      { "title": "Reset", "dataType": "constructor", "index": 1, "fields": [] },
      { "title": "Close", "dataType": "constructor", "index": 2,
        "fields": [{ "title": "ctx", "$ref": "#/definitions/org.julclang.state.api.Ctx" }] }
    ]
  },
  "org.julclang.state.examples.counter.Counter.State": {
    "title": "State",
    "anyOf": [
      { "title": "State", "dataType": "constructor", "index": 0,
        "fields": [{ "title": "count", "dataType": "integer" }, { "title": "owner", "dataType": "bytes" }] }
    ]
  }
}
```

##### Top level

| Key | What it is |
|---|---|
| `preamble` | CIP-57's preamble: `title` (`<package>.<Contract>`), `description` (`"JOUST contract <Name> (ADR-0013 D3)"`), `version` (`"0.0.0"`), `plutusVersion` (`"v3"`), `compiler` (`{ "name": "joust" }`) |
| `validators` | The generated validator's two purposes (below). No compiled code: the script is a separate output (`<Contract>.plutus`, or JuLC's `META-INF/plutus/` blueprint) |
| `x-joust` | The contract's model (below) |
| `definitions` | Every schema the document refers to, keyed by fully qualified Java name |

###### validators

| Entry | Present | Datum | Redeemer |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<Validator>.mint` | Always | None | `<package>.<Validator>.Lifecycle` |
| `<Validator>.spend` | When the contract has any spend call | The state; with `@Owned` types, a `Datum` schema whose `anyOf` is the state followed by each owned type's `Holding` | `<package>.<Validator>.Calls` |

The spend validator tells the state and an owned object's `Holding` apart by token kind (32-byte instance tokens,
29-byte `0x4F` object tokens), so the datum's `anyOf` is not tagged further.

###### definitions

Keys are fully qualified Java names: the state (`org.julclang.state.examples.counter.Counter.State`), owned records,
the `@Params` record, records the arguments use, `org.julclang.state.api.Ctx`, `org.julclang.ledger.TxOutRef`, and the
redeemers the processor generates:

| Key | Present | Constructors |
|---|---|---|
| `<package>.<Validator>.Calls` | When there are spend calls | One per action and destroy, then one per owned action and owned destroy, in the generated validator's `permits` order. With `@Batched` actions, three more: `Batch(validFrom, validTo)`, `InBatch`, `CancelIntent` |
| `<package>.<Validator>.Lifecycle` | Always | `CreateInstance(seed, ...)` at 0, `BurnInstance` at 1, then one per `@OwnedInit` (`seed`, `instance`, ...), `CreateIntent(seed, intent)` with `@Batched`, `ByAction(by)` when the contract mints, `Adopt(seed, ...)` with `@Migrate` |
| `<package>.<Validator>.<Holding>` | Per `@Owned` type | `Holding(instance, value)`: the owning instance id and the owned record. With one owned type the name is `Holding`; with several, `Holding_<Type>` (ADR-0012), each at its own tag |
| `<package>.<Validator>.Intent` | With `@Batched` | `Intent(instance, owner, refund, deadline, received, call)` |
| `<package>.<Validator>.IntentCall` | With `@Batched` | One per batched action, its arguments as fields |
| `<package>.<Validator>.IntentRefund` | With `@Batched` | `IntentRefund(intent)`: the tag on an intent's refund output |

A `$ref` is `#/definitions/<key>`, with `~` written `~0` and `/` written `~1` (JSON Pointer).

###### Redeemer field order

Each `Calls` and `Lifecycle` constructor lays out its fields as the validator generator does:

1. `seed` (a `TxOutRef`), for creations: the input whose spending makes the token name unique;
2. `instance` (bytes), for an `@OwnedInit`: the instance that will own the object;
3. `into` (bytes), for an `@Into` move: the destination instance;
4. the method's own arguments, in declaration order;
5. `ctx` (`Ctx`), when the method takes `Ctx`;
6. `assetsIn` (`Value`), when the call takes native assets in;
7. `events`, when the method's result carries events.

##### Type mapping

The schemas follow JuLC's encodings: records are constructor 0, sealed variants their `permits` position, `Bool`
False/True 0/1, `Optional` Some/None 0/1.

| Java type | Schema |
|---|---|
| `boolean`, `Boolean` | `Bool`: `anyOf` `False` (constructor 0) and `True` (constructor 1), no fields |
| `BigInteger` (also `int`, `long`, `short`, `byte`, `Long`, `Integer`) | `{ "dataType": "integer" }` |
| `byte[]`, `String` | `{ "dataType": "bytes" }` |
| `PubKeyHash`, `ScriptHash`, `ValidatorHash`, `PolicyId`, `TokenName`, `DatumHash`, `TxId` (`org.julclang.ledger`) | `{ "dataType": "bytes" }` |
| A `@NewType` record with one component | Its component's schema |
| `PlutusData` | `Data`: any Plutus data |
| `Value` | `Value`: a map from policy (bytes) to a map from token name (bytes) to quantity (integer) |
| `JulcList<T>` | `{ "dataType": "list", "items": T }` |
| `JulcMap<K, V>` | `{ "dataType": "map", "keys": K, "values": V }` |
| `Optional<T>` | `Optional`: `anyOf` `Some` (constructor 0, field `value`) and `None` (constructor 1) |
| A record | A `$ref` to its definition: one constructor, index 0 (or its position in a sealed parent's `permits`) |
| A sealed interface | A `$ref` to its definition: one constructor per permitted record, in `permits` order |
| Anything else | `Data` |

> **Caution:** 
A field's title replaces the schema's own title, so a `Bool` or `Optional` field is not titled `Bool` or `Optional`.
Clients recognise them **by shape**: two constructors named `False`/`True` (or `Some`/`None`) at indices 0 and 1, with
the right arity (`isBool` and `isOptional` in `js/state-client/src/data.js`).

##### x-joust

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | number | The description format: `2` (ADR-0015 D4). Version 2 adds the call `recipe`s and keeps every version 1 field |
| `contract` | string | The contract's simple name (`Counter`) |
| `package` | string | Its Java package |
| `validator` | string | The generated validator's simple name (`CounterValidator`) |
| `client` | string | The generated Java client's simple name (`CounterClient`) |
| `state` | `$ref` | The state record |
| `params` | `$ref` | The `@Params` record. Only when the contract has one |
| `stakeSelf` | boolean | `@StateContract(stakeSelf = true)`: state UTxOs are staked to the contract's own script |
| `minAda` | number | Lovelace kept in each state UTxO (`@StateContract(minAda)`) |
| `maxDatumBytes` | number | The largest state datum the contract accepts (`@StateContract(maxDatumBytes)`) |
| `assetAware` | boolean | Whether the contract handles native assets (`Funds`, sends, mints) |
| `owned` | array | The `@Owned` types (below) |
| `keyed` | array | The keyed types (below). Only in contracts with keyed types (ADR-0016) |
| `creations` | array | `@Init`, `@OwnedInit` and `@Migrate` methods (below) |
| `actions` | array | `@Action`, `@Destroy`, `@OwnedAction` and `@OwnedDestroy` methods, in `Calls` order (below) |
| `views` | array | `@View` methods (below) |
| `intents` | object | The `@Batched` actions as intents (below). Only when the contract has any |
| `purposes` | array | The `@Withdraw`, `@Certify`, `@Votes` and `@Propose` handlers (below). Only when the contract has any |
| `tokens` | object | How token names are derived (below) |
| `encoding` | object | The JSON conventions (below) |

###### owned

One entry per `@Owned` record:

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `type` | The record's definition key (`org.julclang.state.examples.bank.Bank.Account`) |
| `simple` | Its simple name (`Account`) |
| `lookup` | The name of the generated client's accessor for an object of this type (`account`) |
| `holding` | A `$ref` to its `Holding` datum |
| `tag` | The `Holding` constructor's index, which tells the types apart on chain |
| `multi` | Whether the contract has several owned types (`Holding_<Type>` datums) |

###### keyed

One entry per keyed type ([Keyed objects](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/keyed-objects/); ADR-0016 D11):

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `type`, `simple`, `lookup` | As for `owned`: the value record's definition key, its simple name (`Entry`), the client's accessor (`entry`) |
| `key`, `keyIndex` | The key component's name and index in the record |
| `maxKeyBytes`, `signedKey`, `linkCooldownMs`, `linkWindowMs` | The `@Owned` elements |
| `typeId` | The type id that, with the instance and the key, makes a node's token name |
| `head`, `node`, `retired` | The list datums (`Head_T`, `Keyed_T`, `Retired_T`) |
| `headTag`, `nodeTag`, `retiredTag` | Their constructor tags |
| `link`, `remove` | The `Link` spend redeemer and the `Remove_T` burn redeemer |
| `inserts`, `actions`, `removes`, `retires` | The type's keyed calls, by name |

A keyed call's `kind` is `keyedInit` (in `creations`), or `keyedAction`, `keyedRemove` or `keyedRetire` (in `actions`),
and it carries `keyed`, the type's simple name. `tokens.keyed` describes the token names:
`0x4b ++ blake2b_224(instance ++ typeId ++ key)`, 29 bytes, a list head's key being empty.

###### creations

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | The method's name |
| `kind` | `init`, `ownedInit` or `migrate` |
| `redeemer` | `{ purpose: "mint", constructor, index }`: `CreateInstance` for `init`, `Adopt` for `migrate`, the owned variant for `ownedInit` |
| `args` | The arguments the caller supplies: `[{ name, type, schema }]` (`type` is the Java type's name). The state, params, reads, `Ctx` and `Funds` are not arguments |
| `ctx` | Whether the method takes `Ctx` |
| `payable` | `@Payable`: the call pays lovelace in |
| `takesAssets` | Whether the call pays native assets in (`assetsIn`) |
| `owned` | For `ownedInit`: the owned type's definition key |
| `needsService` | See [needsService](#needsservice) |
| `recipe` | The call recipe (below) |

###### actions

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | The method's name |
| `kind` | `action`, `destroy`, `ownedAction` or `ownedDestroy` |
| `redeemer` | `{ purpose: "spend", constructor, index }`: its `Calls` constructor |
| `fields` | The redeemer's field names, in order |
| `args`, `ctx`, `payable`, `takesAssets`, `owned` | As for creations |
| `policies` | What the validator checks besides the method (below) |
| `returns` | What the method's result carries (below) |
| `needsService` | See [needsService](#needsservice) |
| `recipe` | The call recipe (below) |

`policies`:

| Key | Type | From |
|---|---|---|
| `signedBy` | field names | `@SignedBy` and `@OnlyOwner` (`["owner"]`) |
| `validAfter`, `validBefore` | field names | `@ValidAfter`, `@ValidBefore` |
| `quorum` | `{ keys, threshold }` or `null` | `@Quorum` (for example `{ "keys": "params.council", "threshold": "params.quorum" }`) |
| `authorizedBy` | array | `@AuthorizedBy` |
| `shared` | boolean | An owned method that reads `@Shared` state |
| `into` | boolean | An `@Into` move |
| `admits` | type or `null` | `@Admits`: the owned type it admits |
| `receives` | boolean | `@Receives`: the action takes deposits |
| `batched` | boolean | `@Batched` |
| `migrateTo` | string or `null` | `@MigrateTo`: the state or params field that names the successor |

`returns` (all booleans): `state` (the action continues the instance), `payouts`, `sends`, `mint`, `accepted`,
`events`, `deposits`.

###### The call recipe

`recipe` is version 2's addition (ADR-0015 D4): everything the generated Java client's `Call.Builder` encodes, as
data, so a runtime with no contract classes can build the call.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `transition` | The method the call runs (by name: its transition program, or the JVM method) |
| `redeemerFields` | The redeemer's fields in order: `seed`, `instance`, argument names, `ctx`, ... |
| `burn` | For a destroy: the mint redeemer that burns the token (`{ "constructor": "BurnInstance", "index": 1 }`) |
| `target` | The record the call acts on: the state, or the owned value |
| `shared` | Whether the transition also takes the `@Shared` state |
| `signers`, `validAfter`, `validBefore` | `[{ field, index }]`: the target's fields that hold the signer keys and time bounds, with their component index |
| `params` | Whether the transition takes the `@Params` record |
| `reads` | `@Reads`: `[{ name, params, index, type }]`, the params field naming the foreign instance and its index |
| `transitionArgs` | The transition's arguments in order. Besides argument names: `$params`, `$read:<name>`, `$funds`, `$into`, `$admitted` |
| `admits` | With `@Admits`: the admitted type |
| `stepEvents` | Whether the contract's steps carry events |

###### views

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | The method's name |
| `returns` | The result's schema |
| `args` | Every parameter after the state: `[{ name, schema }]` |

###### intents

Present when the contract has `@Batched` actions (ADR-0004): users lock intents, and a batcher applies them.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `datum` | A `$ref` to `Intent`, the intent UTxO's datum |
| `calls` | One per batched action: `{ name, call: { constructor, index }, only, args, payable, recipe }`. `only` marks a batch-only action |
| `refund` | A `$ref` to `IntentRefund`, the refund output's tag |
| `deposit` | Lovelace locked with each intent beyond what it pays, refunded with it: `2000000` |
| `batch`, `inBatch`, `cancel` | The `Calls` constructors `Batch`, `InBatch`, `CancelIntent`, with their indices |
| `create`, `burn` | The `Lifecycle` constructors `CreateIntent` and `BurnInstance`, with their indices |

###### purposes

Present when the contract has script-purpose handlers (ADR-0010). One entry per handler:

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | The method's name |
| `purpose` | `withdraw`, `certify`, `vote` or `propose` |
| `args`, `ctx` | As for actions |
| `policies` | `{ quorum, authorizedBy }` |
| `redeemer` | `@Withdraw`: `{ purpose: "withdraw", constructor: "Rewards", index: 0, marker: 74, fields }` (`marker`, `amount`, the arguments, `ctx`). The others: `{ purpose, constructor: "Unit", index: 0 }`, with `publish` for `@Certify` |
| `recipe` | `@Withdraw` only: `{ transition, transitionArgs: ["$params", "$amount", ...] }` |
| `returns` | `@Withdraw` only: `{ "sends": true }` |

`@Certify`, `@Votes` and `@Propose` decide on chain only; their redeemers carry nothing.

###### tokens

How the token names a client must derive are made (`seed` is the input the creation spends):

| Key | Rule |
|---|---|
| `instance` | `blake2b_256(seed txId ++ I2OSP(seed index, 2))`, 32 bytes |
| `object` | `0x4f ++ blake2b_224(seed txId ++ I2OSP(seed index, 2))`, 29 bytes |
| `intent` | `0x49 ++ blake2b_224(seed txId ++ I2OSP(seed index, 2))`, 29 bytes |

`@julclang/state-client` implements them as `instanceIdOf`, `objectIdOf` and `intentIdOf`.

###### encoding

`canonicalMaps: true`, and a note: inline datums are canonical CBOR, with map keys sorted (keep state maps ordered
with `SortedMaps`; see [Troubleshooting](https://joust.julc.dev/reference/troubleshooting/)). `encoding.json` states the JSON conventions
every client uses:

| Schema | JSON value |
|---|---|
| integer | A decimal string, or a safe JavaScript integer. `@julclang/state-client` also accepts a `bigint`, and decodes to `bigint` |
| bytes | Lowercase hex |
| constructor | An object by field title. A sum type adds `"$variant"`, its constructor title |
| Bool | `true` or `false` |
| Optional | `null` for None, else the value |
| list | An array |
| map | An array of `[key, value]` pairs, in canonical key order |
| Data | Hex CBOR of any Plutus data |

So an `increment` call's arguments are `{ "by": "5" }`, and a value of a sealed type is written
`{ "$variant": "Deposit", "amount": "10" }`.

###### needsService

`needsService` marks a call a JavaScript client cannot compute from the description and the chain alone. For an
action it is true when any of these hold: the target has MerkleMaps, the action is `@Batched`, it has `@Reads`, it is
a move, it makes or receives deposits, it sends or mints, or it takes `@Params`. For a creation: MerkleMaps, reads,
sends, mints or params.

> **Note:** 
ADR-0013 left calls with `needsService` out of generated clients, since a page could neither prepare nor verify them.
Since ADR-0015 M4 the runtime engine prepares them (in a page's worker or a service) and the page verifier covers
each of them, so `joust-gen` generates every call. The flag remains in the description as information.

##### Who reads it

| Reader | What it does with the description |
|---|---|
| `@julclang/state-client`: `codec(description)` | Turns JSON values into Plutus data and back, by schema |
| `@julclang/state-client`: `verifyPrepared`, `verifyComposed`, `verifyIntent`, `verifyPurpose` | The [page verifier](https://joust.julc.dev/reference/glossary/#page-verifier): checks a prepared transaction makes exactly the described call before the wallet signs |
| `@julclang/state-client`: `JoustContract` | Runs calls described by `x-joust` against a prepare service |
| `joust-gen` (`@julclang/state-client`) | Writes `<Contract>.js` and `<Contract>.d.ts`, with the description inlined so the page pins it: `joust-gen <description.json>... --out <dir> [--import <module>]` |
| `@julclang/joust-runtime` | Loads `contracts.json` into the runtime engine. Refuses any description whose `x-joust.version` is not 2, and a build by an incompatible toolchain. The engine refuses programs whose manifest does not match the description (its hash and each program's `transitionArgs`), and checks every program's inputs against the description's schemas |
| `julc-state-runtime` (`described` package) | `SchemaCodec` and `DescribedContract`: the description-driven dispatcher the engine and the service share. Refuses a description before version 2 |
| `julc-state-server` | Serves `GET /api/description?contract=...`; decodes `/api/prepare` arguments by the JSON conventions |
| `julc-state-testkit` | `Descriptions.assertMatches(Contract.class, ContractValidator.class)` checks a description against the generated validator: constructor order, indices and fields, the state, the owned values and the `Holding` tags |

> **Tip:** 
A page must never take a description from a service at run time. The typed client inlines it (and the Vite plugin
inlines `contracts.json` into a build), so a malicious service cannot change what the page verifies against.

- [@julclang/state-client](https://joust.julc.dev/reference/state-client/)

### Examples

URL: https://joust.julc.dev/reference/examples/

The repository's [`examples/`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples) directory holds one tested
example per feature. Each is real code, built by the same Gradle build as JOUST itself: when a guide shows a contract,
it usually comes from here. Use this page to find the example closest to what you are building.

##### What every example contains

- **The contract:** the only file a developer writes. The processor generates `<Name>Validator` and `<Name>Client`
  from it at build time.
- **Tests at three levels:**
  - **JVM** (`<Name>Test`): the contract's methods as plain Java.
  - **On-chain harness:** the validator as compiled by the build, evaluated against transactions shaped like the
    runtime's. Every accepted transaction also runs the attack suite (ADR-0001 D16), and every applicable mutation
    must be rejected.
  - **DevKit** (`<Name>DevnetTest`, tagged `devnet`): the generated client end to end on a live Yaci DevKit. It skips
    itself when DevKit is not running.
- **`DescriptionTest`:** checks the generated [contract description](https://joust.julc.dev/reference/description-format/).

##### Running an example

From a JOUST checkout (JDK 25; the build resolves JuLC and cardano-client-lib from Maven Central and the BloxBean repositories):

```sh
./gradlew :examples:token:test                   # JVM, harness and attack-suite tests; DevKit tests if it is up
yaci-devkit up --enable-yaci-store               # optional: the local network (Yaci Store on :8080, admin on :10000)
./gradlew :examples:vault:run                    # the example's app against DevKit
./gradlew :examples:token:test -PjoustFixtures   # re-record the ADR-0015 fixtures (DevKit must be up)
```

`./gradlew build` runs every example. The `run` task has an app for `counter`, `vault`, `escrow`, `crowdfund`,
`token` and `bank` (`<Name>App`), and for `dapp` (a web server); the other examples run their flows in their DevKit
tests.

> **Experimental, pre-release:** 
JOUST is a research and learning project, not for production. The examples build from a checkout, with JDK 25 (see
[Quick start: Java & Gradle](https://joust.julc.dev/start/quick-start-java/)). To try a contract without a JDK, start from the npm template
instead ([Quick start: npm & JavaScript](https://joust.julc.dev/start/quick-start-npm/)).

##### Option A: single-UTxO state machines

###### counter

[`examples/counter`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/counter) · `Counter.java`

The smallest contract: a count and an owner. `increment` is an `@Action` anyone can call, with no `Ctx` and no
value; `reset` and the `@Destroy` `close` are `@OnlyOwner`, and `close` returns the deposit. The starting point for
every tutorial; the browser dApp uses it, and the npm template (`create-joust`) starts from a counter too.

- **Annotations:** `@StateContract(maxDatumBytes = 128)`, `@Init`, `@Action`, `@OnlyOwner`, `@Destroy`, `@View`
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:counter:run`
- **Read:** [Your first contract](https://joust.julc.dev/start/first-contract/), [A counter dApp in the browser](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/counter-dapp/),
  [State and lifecycle](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/state-and-lifecycle/)

###### vault

[`examples/vault`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/vault) · `Vault.java`

A time-locked vault. `open` (`@Init @Payable`) records the owner and an unlock time; anyone may `deposit`
(`@Payable`); the owner may `withdraw` only after `unlockAt` and gets a payout, so the action returns a `Result`
record of the new state and its payouts. `close` pays everything out.

- **Annotations:** `@Payable`, `@OnlyOwner`, `@ValidAfter("unlockAt")`, `@Destroy`, `@View`
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:vault:run`
- **Read:** [Vault: deposits, time and payouts](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/vault/), [Time](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/time/),
  [Ctx, funds and payouts](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/ctx-and-funds/)

###### escrow

[`examples/escrow`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/escrow) · `Escrow.java`

The buyer funds the escrow at creation (`@Payable @Init`). It has two `@Destroy`s: `release` pays the seller, and
`refund` returns the funds, which anyone may trigger after the deadline (`Clock.after`).

- **Annotations:** `@Init @Payable`, two `@Destroy`, `@View`
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:escrow:run`
- **Read:** [Escrow and crowdfunding](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/escrow-crowdfund/), [Time](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/time/)

###### crowdfund

[`examples/crowdfund`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/crowdfund) · `Crowdfund.java`

A crowdfund with its backers in a `JulcMap` inside the state, kept in canonical order with `SortedMaps`. Refunds pay
the caller; the creator claims with `@SignedBy("creator")`. Its tests fill the datum to `maxDatumBytes = 1024`
(27 backers) to measure capacity.

- **Annotations:** `@StateContract(maxDatumBytes = 1024)`, `@Payable`, `@SignedBy("creator")`, two `@Destroy`, `@View`
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:crowdfund:run`
- **Read:** [Escrow and crowdfunding](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/escrow-crowdfund/), [State and lifecycle](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/state-and-lifecycle/)

##### Storage and execution strategies

###### token

[`examples/token`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/token) · `Token.java`

An account-model token whose balances live in a `MerkleMap`: an unbounded map behind a 32-byte root. `mint`,
`transfer` and `burn` prove only the keys they touch; the MPF proofs are checked by the shared map verifier
(withdraw-zero). The script is read by reference. Its DevKit test also rebuilds the map from the chain's history
with a fresh store.

- **Annotations:** `@StateContract(maxDatumBytes = 160)`, `@SignedBy("admin")`, `@Action`, `@View`
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:token:run`
- **Read:** [Token balances in a MerkleMap](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/token-merklemap/), [MerkleMaps](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/merklemaps/),
  [MerkleMap mirrors](https://joust.julc.dev/apps/map-mirrors/)

###### bank

[`examples/bank`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/bank) · `Bank.java`

Shared bank configuration (admin, paused, withdrawal limit) plus one owned `Account` per customer. Customers act in
parallel; `withdraw` reads the config by reference (`@Shared`); `close` works even when the bank is paused, the
escape hatch every owned type needs.

- **Annotations:** `@Owned`, `@OwnedInit`, `@OwnedAction`, `@OwnedDestroy`, `@Shared`, `@SignedBy("owner")`,
  `@SignedBy("admin")`
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:bank:run`
- **Read:** [Bank: owned objects](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/bank-owned-objects/), [Owned objects](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/owned-objects/)

###### registry

[`examples/registry`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/registry) · `Registry.java`

Keyed objects (ADR-0016): two keyed types in sorted on-chain lists. `Ballot` is keyed by the voter's key hash
(`signedKey`) and only retires, so each voter votes once, ever. `Entry` is a name registry: `claim` (payable) and the admin's `grant` insert a name, `upgrade`,
`withdraw` and the guardians' `recover` update it, `release` removes it (the name is free again) and `retire` keeps it
taken for good. The tests cover the attack suite, list integrity under mutated transactions, and DevKit runs of
concurrency, contested gaps, cooldowns, compositions and submission across relays; the JavaScript flow is in
`js/joust-runtime/test/examples.test.js`.

- **Annotations:** `@Owned(key = ..., maxKeyBytes = ..., signedKey = ...)`, `@OwnedInit`, `@OwnedAction`,
  `@OwnedDestroy`, `@OwnedDestroy(retire = true)`, `@Shared`, `@Quorum`, `@Invariant`
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:registry:test`
- **Read:** [Keyed objects](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/keyed-objects/), [Keyed objects in JavaScript](https://joust.julc.dev/apps/keyed-objects-js/)

###### pool

[`examples/pool`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/pool) · `Pool.java`

Donations and order-dependent ticket sales as intents. Users lock requests concurrently; a permissionless batcher
applies them to the instance in one transaction, with refunds, change payouts, a cancel and an expired intent in the
tests. `donate` is `@Batched` (direct call or intent); `buy` is `@Batched(only = true)`, because its price depends
on the order of the batch.

- **Annotations:** `@Batched`, `@Batched(only = true)`, `@Payable`, `@SignedBy("admin")`
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:pool:test`
- **Read:** [Pool: batched intents](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/pool-batched-intents/), [Batched intents](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/batched-intents/)

###### dsl

[`examples/dsl`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/dsl) · `src/main/jsc/.../{Jar,Points,Guards}.jsc`

Contracts written in `.jsc` and lowered to Java at build time by the `generateJsc` task (into
`build/generated/sources/jsc`):

- `Jar.jsc`: a tip jar. `tip` is `payable batched` (also an intent); `withdraw` has a rule inside an `if`.
- `Points.jsc`: loyalty points in a `Map<Key, Int>` (a MerkleMap), with `delete` and transfers to oneself.
- `Guards.jsc`: a semantics fixture. An untaken `if` arm and the right side of a false `||` must not run, on the JVM
  or on chain.

- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:dsl:test`
- **Read:** [.jsc](https://joust.julc.dev/languages/jsc/), [.jsc reference](https://joust.julc.dev/languages/jsc-reference/)

###### rollup

[`examples/rollup`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/rollup) · `Ledger.java`, `Rollup.java`, `Sequencer.java`

The Option F spike. `Ledger` is an off-chain payments ledger, a total JuLC-subset program (`@OnchainLibrary`) with
ed25519-signed orders. `Rollup` is an L1 contract that takes commitments (`commit`), opens a challenge window,
`finalize`s, and slashes the operator's bond when a `challenge` re-runs `Ledger.step` on chain and finds a wrong
step. `Sequencer` is the off-chain sequencer and watcher.

- **Annotations:** `@StateContract(maxDatumBytes = 320)`, `@SignedBy("operator")`, `@Payable`
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:rollup:test`
- **Read:** [ADR-0006](https://joust.julc.dev/project/architecture-decisions/#adr-0006-option-f-optimistic-l2-spike). It is a spike, not a product.

##### Assets, governance and composition

###### dex

[`examples/dex`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/dex) · `Dex.java`

A constant-product AMM for one ADA/token pair. The reserves are what the UTxO holds (lovelace above the deposit,
`ctx.balance()`, and the token, `funds.held()`), so the state cannot drift from the funds. LP tokens are minted and
burned by the contract's own policy, one name per pool; swaps send tokens with `Send`. Every call names exactly what
it `accepted`. Swaps pay a 0.3 % fee to the pool.

- **Annotations:** `@StateContract(maxDatumBytes = 256, assetSlots = 2)`, `@Payable`, `@SignedBy("admin")`;
  methods take `Funds` and return records with `payouts`, `sends`, `mint` and `accepted`
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:dex:test`
- **Read:** [DEX: native assets and LP tokens](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/dex-assets/), [Native assets, mints and sends](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/assets-mints-sends/)

###### market

[`examples/market`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/market) · `Market.java`

An NFT marketplace. Each listing is an owned object holding its NFT, so listings never contend. `buy` (a `@Payable`
owned destroy) pays the seller, sends the NFT to the buyer and a royalty to a script address with an inline datum.
`cancel` lets the seller take the NFT back whatever the market's state.

- **Annotations:** `@StateContract(maxDatumBytes = 384, assetSlots = 1)`, `@Owned`, `@OwnedInit`, `@OwnedAction`,
  `@OwnedDestroy`, `@Shared`, `@Into`, `@Admits`, `@SignedBy("seller")`
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:market:test`
- **Read:** [Native assets, mints and sends](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/assets-mints-sends/), [Owned objects](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/owned-objects/)

###### treasury

[`examples/treasury`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/treasury) · `Treasury.java`, `Guardian.java`

A multisig treasury. Deploy-time `@Params` hold a guardian credential and a payout cap. A council decides by
`@Quorum`. A guardian *script* (`Guardian`, a plain JuLC withdraw-zero validator) can freeze the treasury through a
zero withdrawal (`@AuthorizedBy("params.guardian")`, with a bound `Approvals` redeemer). An `@Invariant` holds on
every state, and `Paid`, `CouncilChanged` and `Frozen` events are authenticated in the redeemer.

- **Annotations:** `@Params`, `@Quorum(keys = "council", threshold = "quorum")`, `@AuthorizedBy`, `@Invariant`;
  `Guardian` uses JuLC's `@WithdrawValidator`
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:treasury:test`
- **Read:** [Multisig treasury](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/multisig-treasury/), [Params, invariants and events](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/params-invariants-events/),
  [Authorization](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/authorization/)

###### staking

[`examples/staking`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/staking) · `StakedVault.java`

A council-governed vault whose state UTxOs are staked to its own script (`stakeSelf = true`). `@Certify` allows only
registration and exact delegation to the params' pool; `@Withdraw` sends rewards only to the payee (claimed in the
output registry); `@Votes` votes as a script DRep by quorum; `@Propose` is a treasury-withdrawal guardrail. Built
with `-Ajulc.blueprint=false`.

- **Annotations:** `@StateContract(stakeSelf = true)`, `@Params`, `@Quorum(keys = "params.council", threshold = "params.quorum")`,
  `@Withdraw`, `@Certify`, `@Votes`, `@Propose`
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:staking:test`
- **Read:** [Staked vault and governance](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/staked-vault/), [Staking and governance](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/staking-and-governance/)

> **Note:** 
DevKit pays no rewards within a test (rewards take epochs), so the DevKit flow withdraws a zero balance. Votes and
proposals are covered by the harness, not on DevKit.

###### oracle

[`examples/oracle`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/oracle) · `Oracle.java`, `Shop.java`

A price `Oracle` and a `Shop` that reads it with `@Reads("params.oracle")`. The oracle instance is pinned in the
shop's params as a `ForeignInstance`; the generated code checks its token kind, address and datum shape, and the
shop checks freshness itself. The DevKit test composes a purchase and another oracle's update into one transaction
with `Compose`.

- **Annotations:** `@Params`, `@Reads`, `@Payable`, `@SignedBy("publisher")`
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:oracle:test`
- **Read:** [Oracle and composition](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/oracle-composition/), [Reads and composition](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/reads-and-composition/)

###### upgrade

[`examples/upgrade`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/upgrade) · `CounterV1.java`, `CounterV2.java`

`CounterV1` names a successor (`setSuccessor`) and migrates with `@Destroy @MigrateTo("successor")`. `CounterV2`
adopts it with `@Migrate(from = "params.previous")`, keeping its count and funds, in one composed transaction.

- **Annotations:** `@MigrateTo`, `@Migrate`, `@Params`, `@SignedBy("admin")`
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:upgrade:test`
- **Read:** [Upgrading a contract](https://joust.julc.dev/tutorials/upgrades/), [Upgrades and migration](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/upgrades/)

###### fees

[`examples/fees`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/fees) · `Stall.java`, `Pot.java`

A `Stall` deposits a 5 % fee from each sale into a `Pot` instance fixed in its params (a `ForeignInstance`).
`Pot.collect` takes the deposit in with `@Receives` in the same composed transaction. The output registry carries
the deposit claim, and both validators check their side.

- **Annotations:** `@Params`, `@Receives`, `@Payable`, `@SignedBy("owner")`; `Stall`'s sale returns a list of `Deposit`s
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:fees:test`
- **Read:** [Deposits](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/deposits/)

###### guild

[`examples/guild`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/guild) · `Guild.java`, `Armory.java`

`Guild` has two owned types, `Hero` and `Item`. Each owned method runs only on its own type's datum, and each type
has its own invariants. A hero moves to another guild with `@Into`, which that guild admits with `@Admits("Hero")`
in the same transaction (`transferAdmitted`). `Armory` holds `Vault` objects, each with a MerkleMap inventory.

- **Annotations:** two `@Owned` types, `@OwnedInit`, `@OwnedAction`, `@OwnedDestroy`, `@Shared`, `@Into`,
  `@Admits`, `@Invariant`
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:guild:test`
- **Read:** [Owned objects](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/owned-objects/)

###### locker

[`examples/locker`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/locker) · `Locker.java`, `Safes.java`

MerkleMaps with native assets (ADR-0014). `Locker` holds a native token for many users, with their balances in a
MerkleMap so the datum stays small: locking takes tokens in (`accepted`), unlocking sends them back. `Safes` has
owned safes, each holding tokens and a MerkleMap written at creation.

- **Annotations:** `@StateContract(assetSlots = 2)`, `@Owned`, `@OwnedInit`, `@OwnedAction`, `@OwnedDestroy`, `@Payable`
- **Run:** `./gradlew :examples:locker:test`
- **Read:** [MerkleMaps](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/merklemaps/), [Native assets, mints and sends](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/assets-mints-sends/)

##### Wallets and pages

###### wallet

[`examples/wallet`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/tree/main/examples/wallet) · tests and `js/page.mjs`

Wallet-signed transactions. A counter and a bank are used from an address-only `WalletAccount`:
`Compose.prepare()`, a CIP-30-style witness set, `PreparedTx.submit`. `js/page.mjs` (Node) plays the page: it

A browser dApp for `Counter` and `Bank` on DevKit. It uses typed JS clients generated from the contracts'

##### Script sizes and budgets

The validators are compiled by JuLC (target `plutus-v3-pv11`, `pv11-safe` optimisation), after the ADR-0008
optimisations. The budgets are per script execution, from the harness tests. For scale, a transaction may use
10,000M CPU and 14M memory units on mainnet (16.5M memory on DevKit). The ADR-0008 tables give the numbers from
before the optimisations.

| Contract | Script size | Call | Purpose | CPU | Mem |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Counter | 5,631 B | create | MINT | 86.2M | 271k |
| | | increment | SPEND | 73.4M | 213k |
| | | reset | SPEND | 74.2M | 216k |
| | | close | SPEND + MINT (burn) | 94.1M + 17.6M | 317k + 64k |
| Vault | 6,273 B | open | MINT | 92.7M | 290k |
| | | deposit | SPEND | 99.4M | 303k |
| | | withdraw | SPEND | 140.6M | 445k |
| | | close | SPEND + MINT | 97.9M + 17.6M | 330k + 64k |
| Escrow | 5,688 B | open | MINT | 102.5M | 314k |
| | | release / refund | SPEND + MINT | 92.1M + 17.6M | 309k + 64k |
| Crowdfund | 7,976 B | launch | MINT | 102.8M | 317k |
| | | contribute | SPEND | 132.8M | 385k |
| | | refund | SPEND | 156.9M | 460k |
| | | refund, 27 backers (`maxDatumBytes` = 1024, at capacity) | SPEND | 286.6M | 559k |
| | | claim | SPEND + MINT | 99.0M + 17.6M | 336k + 64k |
| Bank | 7,920 B | open account | MINT | 124.1M | 392k |
| | | deposit (owned) | SPEND | 105.9M | 323k |
| | | withdraw (owned, `@Shared` read) | SPEND | 171.4M | 547k |
| | | close (owned) | SPEND | 96.4M | 327k |
| Pool | 9,586 B | create intent | MINT | 110.3M | 321k |
| | | cancel intent | SPEND | 48.3M | 165k |
| | | batch of 3 (donate, buy, buy) | SPEND instance | 517.6M | 1,619k |
| | | batch of 10 donations (all scripts) | | 4,629.8M | 13,976k |
| Jar (.jsc) | 9,507 B | tip | SPEND | 102.3M | 312k |
| | | withdraw (with an `if` arm) | SPEND | 144.5M | 460k |
| Points (.jsc) | 12,276 B (+ MapVerifier) | give | SPEND + VERIFIER | 235.1M + 393.6M | 768k + 1,496k |
| Rollup | 10,447 B | commit (16 steps) | SPEND | 651.9M | 1,892k |
| | | challenge, worst case (32 accounts, 16 steps) | SPEND | 2,644.1M | 7,781k |
| Token | 11,718 B (+ MapVerifier 4,700 B, shared) | create | MINT + VERIFIER | 121.2M + 32.0M | 366k + 138k |
| | | mint (1 read, 1 write) | SPEND + VERIFIER | 156.2M + 336.5M | 483k + 1,277k |
| | | transfer (2 reads, 2 writes) | SPEND + VERIFIER | 218.4M + 502.3M | 707k + 1,901k |
| | | transfer, 203 holders in the map | SPEND + VERIFIER | 218.4M + 742.4M | 707k + 2,923k |
| Dex | 12,008 B (+ OutputVerifier 703 B, shared) | open | MINT | 100.4M | 302k |
| | | addLiquidity (LP minted, sent) | SPEND + MINT + VERIFIER | 256.5M + 57.8M + 21.2M | 793k + 214k + 86k |
| | | swapAdaForToken | SPEND + VERIFIER | 221.6M + 21.2M | 688k + 86k |
| | | swapTokenForAda | SPEND | 197.8M | 611k |
| | | removeLiquidity (LP burned) | SPEND + MINT + VERIFIER | 296.3M + 69.5M + 22.1M | 913k + 260k + 90k |
| Market | 11,325 B | offer (NFT in) | MINT | 159.1M | 497k |
| | | buy (payout, NFT send, royalty send) | SPEND + MINT + VERIFIER | 345.7M + 24.0M + 35.3M | 1,127k + 100k + 145k |
| | | cancel | SPEND + MINT + VERIFIER | 191.0M + 24.0M + 21.2M | 634k + 100k + 86k |

The registry's validator is 14,717 bytes; its whole-transaction budgets are on the
[Keyed objects](https://joust.julc.dev/contracts/keyed-objects/#costs) page (ADR-0016, M1 notes).

All contracts read their script by reference (ADR-0002 D9); the first deploy of a contract type publishes it.
ADR-0008 cut the generated checks' cost by 30-60 % in plain contracts and the scripts by about 2.4 KB, so the
size-based fee is now the largest part of a simple call's fee. The source of this table is
[`examples/README.md`](https://github.com/bloxbean/joust/blob/main/examples/README.md).

> **Tip:** 
A MerkleMap call runs two scripts: the contract's spend and the shared `MapVerifier`. The verifier's cost grows with
the number of keys touched and, slowly, with the map's size (compare the Token transfer with 203 holders). A batch
of 10 donations uses 13,976k memory, close to mainnet's 14M limit: the batcher's default is 8 intents
(`Batcher.DEFAULT_MAX`, ADR-0004 §6).
